requirements.text: rcp_discovery_encode_response() shall encode the response's leading RCP_DISCOVERY_GENERAL_SLICE_LEN octets, when present, as big-endian magic (32 bit at offset 0), svr_version (32 bit at offset 4), vendor_id (16 bit at offset 8), device_id (16 bit at offset 10), and svr_ep_count (16 bit at offset 12), taken from map.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 Table 17 ("Discovery response": subtype=NTSCF, acf_msg_type=ACF_ABB, Byte_bus_id=00000000000b, op=1b/read, byte_msg_payload=RC Server's register map content starting from address 0x00000), TC18.txt L2402-2427

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_encode_response() zero-fills beyond the general slice
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_encode_response() shall zero-fill any response payload octets beyond RCP_DISCOVERY_GENERAL_SLICE_LEN when read_size exceeds it.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 ("...length being determined by the read_size in the discovery request."), TC18.txt L2402-2403

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_decode_response() recovers a valid discovery result
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_decode_response() shall, on RCP_DISCOVERY_OK, populate out_result with valid = true, the response frame's own NTSCF stream_id as server_stream_id, and the general slice fields decoded from the payload at the offsets REQ-DISC-010 defines, with svr_version read as a 32-bit field.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 Table 17 ("Discovery response": subtype=NTSCF, acf_msg_type=ACF_ABB, Byte_bus_id=00000000000b, op=1b/read, byte_msg_payload=RC Server's register map content starting from address 0x00000), TC18.txt L2402-2427

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_decode_response() rejects a payload shorter than the general slice
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_decode_response() shall return RCP_DISCOVERY_ERR_SHORT_FRAME when the ACF payload is shorter than RCP_DISCOVERY_GENERAL_SLICE_LEN octets.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 Table 17 ("Discovery response": subtype=NTSCF, acf_msg_type=ACF_ABB, Byte_bus_id=00000000000b, op=1b/read, byte_msg_payload=RC Server's register map content starting from address 0x00000), TC18.txt L2402-2427

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_decode_response() applies the same AVTP/ACF-level checks as a request
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_decode_response() shall return RCP_DISCOVERY_ERR_NOT_NTSCF, RCP_DISCOVERY_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE, RCP_DISCOVERY_ERR_WRONG_BUS, or RCP_DISCOVERY_ERR_WRONG_OP under the same conditions rcp_discovery_decode_request() does.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.1 ("AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped without further response, as well as requests in ACF_GBB format."), TC18.txt L2367 -- the same AVTP/ACF-level checks apply to responses

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_claim_init() starts unheld with the given timeout
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_claim_init() shall initialize claim with held = false and timeout_ms set to the given value.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("...If the RC Server does not receive configuration requests on the stream for a certain time (Discovery_TimeOut) it will drop the discovery stream and is open for a new discovery."), TC18.txt L2356-2359

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_claim_is_open() reports lapsed or never-held claims as open
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_claim_is_open() shall return true when claim has never been held, or when now_ms is at or past claim's deadline_ms.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("...for a certain time (Discovery_TimeOut) it will drop the discovery stream and is open for a new discovery."), TC18.txt L2357-2359

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_claim_note_request() grants an open claim to the requester
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_claim_note_request() shall, when the claim is open, set held = true, claimant = requester, and deadline_ms = now_ms + timeout_ms.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("The first discovery request the RC server receives in HW_UNCONFIGURED or HW_CONFIGURED state is used to set the discovery stream from which now on configuration requests will be accepted."), TC18.txt L2355-2357

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_claim_note_request() does not preempt an active claimant
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_claim_note_request() shall leave an already-held, not-yet-lapsed claim by a different claimant unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("...but only the first one will be allowed as configuration stream. If others send configuration requests they will be rejected and get an error response."), TC18.txt L2359-2361

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant() checks held, deadline, and identity
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant() shall return true if and only if claim is held, now_ms is strictly before claim's deadline_ms, and claimant equals writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("...but only the first one will be allowed as configuration stream."), TC18.txt L2359-2360

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_claim_note_config_write() refreshes the deadline for the claimant
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_claim_note_config_write() shall, when writer is the current claimant, set deadline_ms = now_ms + timeout_ms and return true.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("...for a certain time (Discovery_TimeOut) it will drop the discovery stream..."), TC18.txt L2357-2359 -- receiving configuration requests on the stream is what resets the timeout

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_claim_note_config_write() rejects a non-claimant without mutating state
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_claim_note_config_write() shall return false and leave claim unchanged when writer is not the current claimant, including when the claim has already lapsed.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("...but only the first one will be allowed as configuration stream. If others send configuration requests they will be rejected..."), TC18.txt L2359-2361

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_claim_release() unconditionally clears the claim
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_claim_release() shall set held = false regardless of the claim's prior state.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("...it will drop the discovery stream and is open for a new discovery."), TC18.txt L2358-2359

requirements.title: The discovery result cache stores at most one entry per server_stream_id
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_cache_put() shall overwrite an existing entry whose server_stream_id matches result's in place, and otherwise append a new entry growing internal storage as needed; rcp_discovery_cache_find() shall return a pointer to the matching entry or NULL if none is on record.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 ("For each RC Server the RC Client can read the register map full or partially and maintain a table of relevant discovered RC Servers and their endpoints."), TC18.txt L2406-2408

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_strerror() never returns NULL and is unique per code
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty, distinct message for each rcp_discovery_errc_t value.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_strerror() never returns NULL and is unique per code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty, distinct message for each rcp_ep_gpio_errc_t value.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_pin_index_valid() bounds pin indices to 0..31
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_pin_index_valid() shall return true if and only if pin_index is strictly less than RCP_EP_GPIO_MAX_PINS (32).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("Each GPIO endpoint can handle up to 32 IOs."), TC18.txt L4381

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_pin_mask() derives a single-bit mask, or 0 for an invalid index
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_pin_mask() shall return (1u << pin_index) for a valid pin_index, and 0 for a pin_index that is not rcp_ep_gpio_pin_index_valid().
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("Each GPIO pin can be assigned to a bit position of the byte_msg_payload... In case the EP supports less than 32 pins, the least-significant bits are used."), TC18.txt L4389-4390

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_pin_get() reads one bit of a bitmask
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_pin_get() shall return true if and only if bitmask's bit at pin_index is set, and shall return false (not an error) for an invalid pin_index.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("A GPIO endpoint maps bits from a byte_msg_payload to physical pins."), TC18.txt L4380

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_write_semantics_valid() accepts exactly 0..7
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_write_semantics_valid() shall return true for every value v with v <= 7, and false for every v > 7.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 ("evt[2:0]" GPIO/PWM_OUT row, values 000b-111b), TC18.txt L3690-3717

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_REPLACE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() with evt = RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_REPLACE shall return request, discarding current.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=000b: "The byte_msg_payload is presented at the interface"), TC18.txt L3694

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_OR
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() with evt = RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_OR shall return current bitwise-ORed with request.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=001b: "The 'byte_msg_payload' bitwise OR 'current interface status' is written to the interface (example: with a byte_msg_payload of 0x0000 0002 the second IO pin will be set, while other IO pins remain unchanged)"), TC18.txt L3695-3698

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_AND
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() with evt = RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_AND shall return current bitwise-ANDed with request.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=010b: "The 'byte_msg_payload' bitwise AND 'current interface status' is written to the interface (example: with a byte_msg_payload of 0xFFFF FFFE the first IO pin will be reset, while other IO pins remain unchanged)"), TC18.txt L3699-3702

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_XOR
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() with evt = RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_XOR shall return current bitwise-XORed with request.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=011b: "The 'byte_msg_payload' bitwise XOR 'current interface status' is written to the interface (example: with a byte_msg_payload of 0x0000 0002 the second IO pin will be toggled, while other IO pins remain unchanged)"), TC18.txt L3703-3706

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() implements saturating RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_ADD
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() with evt = RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_ADD shall return current + request when that sum does not exceed 0xFFFFFFFF, and shall return 0xFFFFFFFF (saturating, not wrapping) when it would.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=101b: "The 'byte_msg_payload' plus 'current interface status' is written to the interface"), TC18.txt L3709-3711; saturation rule, TC18.txt L3719-3720

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() implements saturating RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_SUB as request minus current
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() with evt = RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_SUB shall return request - current when current <= request, and shall return 0 (saturating, not wrapping) when current > request.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=110b: "'byte_msg_payload' minus 'current interface status' is written as is to interface"), TC18.txt L3712-3714; saturation rule, TC18.txt L3719-3720

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() treats RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_RESERVED4 as a no-op
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write() with evt = RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_RESERVED4 shall return current unchanged, regardless of request.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=100b: "reserved -request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"), TC18.txt L3707-3708

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig() applies an addressed write into the GPIO EP_func register block
requirements.text: CORRECTED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group G): this entry previously described rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig() as toggling a per-pin bitmask's flagged pins between RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_OUTPUT and RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_INPUT -- a mechanism this codebase's own file header had already, honestly, labelled its own invented design, and which corresponds to no TC18 register or mechanism at all (Table 41, the real GPIO functional-configuration register block, has no per-pin direction field; direction lives in HW_config's own hw_pin_type, a different subsystem, configured only in HW_UNCONFIGURED state). That prior behavior is retained, under the honest name rcp_ep_gpio_toggle_pin_direction(), as a real but purely caller-side convenience no longer described as, or reachable from, evt[2:0]=111b. rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig() now names TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18's actual generic mechanism, common to every endpoint type: payload is a 16-bit big-endian relative start address into this endpoint's own EP_func block followed by configuration data octets, applied at octet granularity over the block rcp_ep_gpio_render_registers() renders, then adopted back into cfg. Returns RCP_EP_GPIO_RECONFIG_ERR_SHORT when payload_len is not at least RCP_EP_GPIO_RECONFIG_ADDR_LEN + 1, and RCP_EP_GPIO_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE when the addressed span would extend past RCP_EP_GPIO_EP_FUNC_LEN (0x0029); in both cases cfg is left entirely unchanged, per the specification's own "such a payload is to be ignored" rule. Octets landing on a read-only register (EP_LEN, IO_MAX, base_clk) are left unchanged while the rest of the span is still applied. This closes REQ-CFG-011/REQ-CFG-012's own gap for GPIO specifically (2 of 11 endpoint types now implement the mechanism; SPI/I2C/UART/LIN/CAN/ADC/ISELED/MDIO/wakeup remain open).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 18 ("the data of the byte_msg_payload from a write request is written into the section of the EP that is addressed... any byte_msg_payload for which the length plus the start_address results in a value larger than the EP_LEN, is to be ignored"), TC18.txt L2464-2486; §13.7.4.2 Table 41 (gpio functional configuration register block), TC18.txt L4441-4470

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_render_registers() serializes the GPIO EP_func block exactly as apply_reconfig() would read it back
requirements.text: ADDED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group G, REQ-GPIO-013): rcp_ep_gpio_render_registers() shall serialize cfg's EP_func registers into out[0..RCP_EP_GPIO_EP_FUNC_LEN) at the TC18 Table 41 offsets (gpio_ep_len=0x0000 reporting RCP_EP_GPIO_EP_FUNC_LEN itself; gpio_io_max=0x0001 reporting RCP_EP_GPIO_MAX_PINS; gpio_ep_enable&clr=0x0002/gpio_ep_options=0x0003 packed from regmap.h's shared common-entries flags; gpio_base_clk=0x0004 always 0; gpio_ep_status=0x0006; gpio_clk_divider=0x0008; gpio_debounce_IO0..IO31=0x0009..0x0028), matching the exact image rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig() patches in place and parses back. rcp_ep_gpio_encode_reconfig_request() shall encode an ACF_ABB write request (evt[2:0]=RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_RECONFIG) whose payload is start_address (16-bit big-endian) followed by data[0..data_len), returning a zeroed rcp_bytes_t when data_len is 0, data is NULL, the encoded payload would exceed RCP_ACF_MAX_PAYLOAD, or on allocation failure.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_reconfig_strerror() returns a distinct, non-NULL message per rcp_ep_gpio_reconfig_errc_t value
requirements.text: ADDED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group G, REQ-GPIO-013): rcp_ep_gpio_reconfig_strerror() shall return a distinct, non-NULL, human-readable message for each of RCP_EP_GPIO_RECONFIG_OK, RCP_EP_GPIO_RECONFIG_ERR_SHORT, and RCP_EP_GPIO_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE, and a non-NULL message for any other (invalid) value -- matching ep_pwm.h's own rcp_ep_pwm_out_reconfig_strerror() precedent exactly.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() never fires for RCP_EP_GPIO_TRIGGER_NONE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() with trigger = RCP_EP_GPIO_TRIGGER_NONE shall return false for every combination of prev_level and new_level.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("The GPIO endpoint generates triggers for all its mapped IO-pins on the change, falling and rising edge."), TC18.txt L4402

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_GPIO_TRIGGER_ANY_CHANGE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() with trigger = RCP_EP_GPIO_TRIGGER_ANY_CHANGE shall return true if and only if prev_level != new_level.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 Table 40 ("IO0 signal change"), TC18.txt L4414

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_GPIO_TRIGGER_RISING
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() with trigger = RCP_EP_GPIO_TRIGGER_RISING shall return true if and only if prev_level is false and new_level is true.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 Table 40 ("IO0 rising edge"), TC18.txt L4415

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_GPIO_TRIGGER_FALLING
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() with trigger = RCP_EP_GPIO_TRIGGER_FALLING shall return true if and only if prev_level is true and new_level is false.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 Table 40 ("IO0 falling edge"), TC18.txt L4416

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_init() shall set cfg's common functional-config flags all false and every pins[i].pin_property to 0 and pins[i].trigger to RCP_EP_GPIO_TRIGGER_NONE.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_writable() is unwritable while HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false while state is RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED, for every writer context.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2177-2178

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_writable() requires an authorized writer while HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_writable() shall return true while state is RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true, and false for an unauthorized writer. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group F): this entry previously claimed "for every writer context", superseded by REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036's authorization-gating fix (issue #198) -- the code and this module's own test (test_functional_cfg_writable_hw_configured_requires_authorization_or_discovery_stream, tests/test_ep_gpio.c) were already correct; only this entry's own text had gone stale.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured 'root client' of via the discovery stream."), TC18.txt L2184

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_writable() requires authorization once RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_writable() shall, while state is RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED, return true if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0 or writer.via_owning_stream is true.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3 ("...only write access to the EP's functional configurations is allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client access EP0... Write access to some parameters might be prohibited in this life-cycle state, this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables."), TC18.txt L2203-2206, L2225-2226

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_set_pin_property() rejects an invalid pin index or an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_set_pin_property() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when pin_index is not rcp_ep_gpio_pin_index_valid(), or when rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_writable() denies the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-GPIO-021

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_set_pin_property() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_set_pin_property() shall set cfg->pins[pin_index].pin_property to pin_property and return true when pin_index is valid and the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-GPIO-021

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_set_pin_trigger() rejects an invalid pin index or an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_set_pin_trigger() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when pin_index is not rcp_ep_gpio_pin_index_valid(), or when rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_writable() denies the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-GPIO-021

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_set_pin_trigger() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_set_pin_trigger() shall set cfg->pins[pin_index].trigger to trigger and return true when pin_index is valid and the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-GPIO-021

requirements.title: GPIO read request encode/decode round-trips
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_read_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_gpio_encode_read_request() with the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_GPIO_OK and recover the original transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("A request not having exactly four bytes is rejected and an error response with error code = INVALID_PARAMETER will be sent."), TC18.txt L4391-4392; general ACF frame basis, §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3710

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_read_request() rejects a malformed or misaddressed frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_read_request() shall return RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame shorter than the ACF_ABB fixed header or its declared payload length, RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE for a non-ACF_ABB frame, RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, and RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_WRONG_OP when op is not RCP_ACF_OP_READ.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3710 (general ACF frame-validation basis)

requirements.title: GPIO write request encode/decode round-trips, including evt[2:0]
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_write_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_gpio_encode_write_request() with the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_GPIO_OK and recover the original bitmask, evt[2:0] masked to its low three bits, and transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("A request not having exactly four bytes is rejected and an error response with error code = INVALID_PARAMETER will be sent."), TC18.txt L4391-4392; evt[2:0] semantics per §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3690-3717

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_write_request() rejects a malformed or misaddressed frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_write_request() shall return RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame shorter than the ACF_ABB fixed header or its declared payload length, RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE for a non-ACF_ABB frame, RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_WRONG_OP when op is not RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE, and RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_BAD_PAYLOAD_LEN when the payload is not exactly RCP_EP_GPIO_PAYLOAD_LEN octets.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("A request not having exactly four bytes is rejected and an error response with error code = INVALID_PARAMETER will be sent."), TC18.txt L4391-4392

requirements.title: GPIO response encode/decode round-trips when untimed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_gpio_encode_response() with timed = false and the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_GPIO_OK, recover the original bitmask and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = false with *out_timestamp = 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("A request not having exactly four bytes is rejected..."), TC18.txt L4391-4392; response payload format mirrors the request's byte_msg_payload bitmask, Figure 24, TC18.txt L4397-4399

requirements.title: GPIO response encode/decode round-trips when timed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_gpio_encode_response() with timed = true, the same byte_bus_id, and a timestamp, return RCP_EP_GPIO_OK, recover the original bitmask and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = true with *out_timestamp equal to the original timestamp.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("A request not having exactly four bytes is rejected..."), TC18.txt L4391-4392; response payload format mirrors the request's byte_msg_payload bitmask, Figure 24, TC18.txt L4397-4399

requirements.title: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_response() rejects a malformed or misaddressed frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_response() shall return RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for its applicable ACF fixed header, RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, and RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_BAD_PAYLOAD_LEN when the payload is not exactly RCP_EP_GPIO_PAYLOAD_LEN octets.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3710 (general ACF frame-validation basis)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_strerror() never returns NULL and is unique per code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty, distinct message for each rcp_ep_spi_errc_t value.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid() bounds channel indices to 0..5
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid() shall return true iff channel < RCP_EP_SPI_MAX_CHANNELS (6).
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (SPI row, "selects channel 0 … 5"), TC18.txt L3678; §13.7.3.1 ("the SPI endpoint may support up to 6 pre-configurable sets of SPI configurations"), TC18.txt L4192-4193

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_mode_valid() accepts exactly 0..3
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_mode_valid() shall return true iff v <= 3.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 39 ("spi_clk_polarity0"/"spi_clk_phase0", each 1-bit R/W), TC18.txt L4260-4265 -- the four (polarity, phase) combinations this implementation groups as "mode 0..3"

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_mode_cpol() derives CPOL correctly for all 4 modes
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_mode_cpol() shall return false for RCP_EP_SPI_MODE_0/_1 and true for RCP_EP_SPI_MODE_2/_3.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 39 ("spi_clk_polarity0 ... polarity of SCLK signal, 0b: normal, 1b: inverted"), TC18.txt L4260-4262

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_mode_cpha() derives CPHA correctly for all 4 modes
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_mode_cpha() shall return false for RCP_EP_SPI_MODE_0/_2 and true for RCP_EP_SPI_MODE_1/_3.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 39 ("spi_clk_phase0 ... sample phase of SCLK, 0b: sample on rising edge, 1b: sample on falling edge"), TC18.txt L4263-4265

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_trigger_fires() never fires for RCP_EP_SPI_TRIGGER_NONE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_trigger_fires() shall return false for trigger == RCP_EP_SPI_TRIGGER_NONE regardless of event. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): NONE, and this module's entire 4-value rcp_ep_spi_trigger_t, is an original simplification -- TC18 Table 38 documents 14 fixed, always-on, per-CS-channel trigger signals (execution-done plus an assert/de-assert pair for each of CS0-CS5) with no off/none state and no client-selectable register at all (Table 39 has no trigger-select field). See ep_spi.h's own file header for the full clarification.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.1 Table 38 ("An SPI endpoint creates the following trigger events"), TC18.txt L4204-4219 -- names 14 fixed, per-CS-channel hardware signals, not a client-configurable field this module's 4-value enum reproduces

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_SPI_TRIGGER_TRANSFER_DONE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_trigger_fires() shall return true for trigger == RCP_EP_SPI_TRIGGER_TRANSFER_DONE iff event == RCP_EP_SPI_EVENT_TRANSFER_DONE.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.1 Table 38 (trigger signal 0, "SPI execution done"), TC18.txt L4206

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_SPI_TRIGGER_CS_ASSERT
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_trigger_fires() shall return true for trigger == RCP_EP_SPI_TRIGGER_CS_ASSERT iff event == RCP_EP_SPI_EVENT_CS_ASSERT.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.1 Table 38 (trigger signals 2/4/6/8/10/12, "CSn asserted"), TC18.txt L4208-4218

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_SPI_TRIGGER_CS_DEASSERT
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_trigger_fires() shall return true for trigger == RCP_EP_SPI_TRIGGER_CS_DEASSERT iff event == RCP_EP_SPI_EVENT_CS_DEASSERT.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.1 Table 38 (trigger signals 3/5/7/9/11/13, "CS0 de-asserted"/"CS1 de-asserted"/.../"CS5 de-asserted"), TC18.txt L4209-4219

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_init() shall set every common flag false and, for every channel, mode = RCP_EP_SPI_MODE_0, bit_order = RCP_EP_SPI_BIT_ORDER_MSB_FIRST, cs_polarity = RCP_EP_SPI_CS_ACTIVE_LOW, trigger = RCP_EP_SPI_TRIGGER_NONE, and clock_divider/inter_byte_delay_ns/inter_transfer_delay_ns all 0.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable() is unwritable while HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED regardless of writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2177-2178

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable() requires an authorized writer while HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable() shall return true for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true, and false for an unauthorized writer. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group F): this entry previously claimed "regardless of writer", superseded by REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036's authorization-gating fix (v0.156.0, issue #198) -- the code and this module's own test (test_functional_cfg_writable_hw_configured_requires_authorization_or_discovery_stream, tests/test_ep_spi.c) were already correct; only this entry's own text had gone stale.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured 'root client' of via the discovery stream."), TC18.txt L2184

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable() requires authorization once RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED when writer indicates neither via_root_client_ep0 nor via_owning_stream, and true when either is set.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3 ("...only write access to the EP's functional configurations is allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client access EP0... Write access to some parameters might be prohibited in this life-cycle state, this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables."), TC18.txt L2203-2206, L2225-2226

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_mode() rejects an invalid channel or an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_mode() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when channel is not rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid() or the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.1 ("the SPI endpoint may support up to 6 pre-configurable sets of SPI configurations"), TC18.txt L4192-4193; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same authorization basis as REQ-SPI-013

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_mode() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_mode() shall return true and set cfg->channels[channel].mode to the requested mode when channel is valid and the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-SPI-013

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_bit_order() rejects an invalid channel or an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_bit_order() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when channel is not rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid() or the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable(). CORRECTED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): the prior citation named Table 39 fields (spi_clk_polarity0/spi_clk_phase0) as "bit-order-adjacent", implying bit_order has a TC18 counterpart nearby -- it does not. Table 39 defines no bit-order field at all (MSB-first/LSB-first is this module's own original addition); the channel-validity/authorization behavior this requirement actually describes is correctly implemented and is what §12.3.1.3's W* marker convention governs. See ep_spi.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- governs the write-authorization behavior; bit_order itself has no TC18 basis (see ep_spi.h's file header)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_bit_order() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_bit_order() shall return true and set cfg->channels[channel].bit_order to the requested bit_order when channel is valid and the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-SPI-013

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_cs_polarity() rejects an invalid channel or an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_cs_polarity() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when channel is not rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid() or the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 39 ("spi_cs_polarity0 ... polarity of CS signal, 0b: CS is low active, 1b: CS is high active"), TC18.txt L4266-4268; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_cs_polarity() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_cs_polarity() shall return true and set cfg->channels[channel].cs_polarity to the requested cs_polarity when channel is valid and the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-SPI-013

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_clock_divider() rejects an invalid channel or an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_clock_divider() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when channel is not rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid() or the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 39 ("spi_baud_rate0 ... SPI baud rate in kbit/s"), TC18.txt L4259; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_clock_divider() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_clock_divider() shall return true and set cfg->channels[channel].clock_divider to the requested value when channel is valid and the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-SPI-013

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_timing() rejects an invalid channel or an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_timing() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when channel is not rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid() or the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 39 ("spi_cs_clk_leadtime0"/"spi_clk_cs_trailtime0"/"spi_bits_max0"/"spi_pause_min0" timing fields), TC18.txt L4276-4285; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_timing() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_timing() shall return true and set cfg->channels[channel].inter_byte_delay_ns and inter_transfer_delay_ns to the requested values when channel is valid and the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-SPI-013

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_trigger() rejects an invalid channel or an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_trigger() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when channel is not rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid() or the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_writable(). CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): the channel-validity/authorization behavior this requirement describes is correctly implemented and governed by §12.3.1.3's W* marker convention; the `trigger` concept being written is this module's own original simplification of Table 38's 14 fixed hardware signals -- see REQ-SPI-006 and ep_spi.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- governs the write-authorization behavior; Table 38 (trigger outputs), TC18.txt L4204-4219, is the fixed-signal basis `trigger` simplifies (see REQ-SPI-006)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_trigger() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_set_channel_trigger() shall return true and set cfg->channels[channel].trigger to the requested trigger when channel is valid and the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-SPI-013

requirements.title: SPI transfer request encode/decode round-trips in the read direction, including channel selection via evt[2:0]
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_encode_transfer_request() shall encode op RCP_ACF_OP_READ (the reply-expected direction), and rcp_ep_spi_decode_transfer_request() shall, given a frame it produced with the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_SPI_OK and recover the original channel, PICO-out payload bytes, and transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.3 ("...even if the read_size is less than the number of bytes in the byte_msg_payload."), Figure 23 worked example ("write 20 bytes and get a response with 10 on SPI channel 3", op=0/read direction), TC18.txt L4355-4375; channel selection per §13.5 Table 30 SPI row, TC18.txt L3678-3680

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_decode_transfer_request() rejects a malformed, misaddressed, or bad-channel frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_decode_transfer_request() shall return RCP_EP_SPI_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame shorter than the ACF_ABB fixed header or its declared payload length, RCP_EP_SPI_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE for a non-ACF_ABB frame, RCP_EP_SPI_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, RCP_EP_SPI_ERR_WRONG_OP when op is not RCP_ACF_OP_READ, and RCP_EP_SPI_ERR_BAD_CHANNEL when evt[2:0] is not rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid().
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3693 (general ACF frame-validation basis, SPI row for channel selection)

requirements.title: SPI response encode/decode round-trips when untimed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_spi_encode_response() with timed = false and the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_SPI_OK, recover the original channel, POCI-in payload bytes, and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = false with *out_timestamp = 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.3 ("The SPI EP shall append zeros in case the read_size is larger than the number of bytes in the byte_msg_payload."), TC18.txt L4370-4371

requirements.title: SPI response encode/decode round-trips when timed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_spi_encode_response() with timed = true, the same byte_bus_id, and a timestamp, return RCP_EP_SPI_OK, recover the original channel, POCI-in payload bytes, and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = true with *out_timestamp equal to the original timestamp.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.3 ("The SPI EP shall append zeros in case the read_size is larger than the number of bytes in the byte_msg_payload."), TC18.txt L4370-4371

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_decode_response() rejects a malformed, misaddressed, or bad-channel frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_spi_decode_response() shall return RCP_EP_SPI_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for its applicable ACF fixed header, RCP_EP_SPI_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, and RCP_EP_SPI_ERR_BAD_CHANNEL when evt[2:0] is not rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid().
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3693 (general ACF frame-validation basis, SPI row for channel selection)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_mode_valid() accepts exactly the four defined presets
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_mode_valid() shall return true for v in 0..3 (RCP_EP_I2C_MODE_STANDARD..RCP_EP_I2C_MODE_HIGH_SPEED) and false for any other value.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.2 Table 46 (i2c functional configuration), TC18.txt L4795-4824 (i2c_mode, 0x0007, values 0-4 with a duplicated "3:" high-speed labeling -- see the pre-existing gap REQ-I2C-019); this module's conservative lower-numbered reading caps valid values at 0..3

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_init() shall set every rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t flag in cfg->common to false and cfg->i2c_mode to RCP_EP_I2C_MODE_STANDARD (0), regardless of cfg's prior contents.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_writable() is false while HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED, for any writer, by delegating to rcp_server_field_writable() with kind RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2177-2178

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_writable() requires an authorized writer while HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_writable() shall return true for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true, and false for an unauthorized writer. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group F): this entry previously claimed "regardless of writer's contents", superseded by REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036's authorization-gating fix (issue #198) -- the code and this module's own test (test_functional_cfg_writable_hw_configured_requires_authorization_or_discovery_stream, tests/test_ep_i2c.c) were already correct; only this entry's own text had gone stale.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured 'root client' of via the discovery stream."), TC18.txt L2184

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_writable() requires authorization once RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED when writer has neither via_root_client_ep0 nor via_owning_stream set, and true when either is set.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_set_mode() rejects an invalid mode value
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_set_mode() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when mode is not rcp_ep_i2c_mode_valid(), regardless of state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.2 Table 46 (i2c functional configuration), TC18.txt L4795-4824 (i2c_mode register), writability per §12.3.1.3 W* marker convention, TC18.txt L2225-2226

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_set_mode() rejects an unauthorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_set_mode() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_writable() does not authorize the write for state/writer, even when mode is valid.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.2 Table 46 (i2c functional configuration), TC18.txt L4795-4824 (i2c_mode register), writability per §12.3.1.3 W* marker convention, TC18.txt L2225-2226

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_set_mode() applies a valid, authorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_set_mode() shall set cfg->i2c_mode to mode and return true when mode is rcp_ep_i2c_mode_valid() and rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.2 Table 46 (i2c functional configuration), TC18.txt L4795-4824 (i2c_mode register), writability per §12.3.1.3 W* marker convention, TC18.txt L2225-2226

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_strerror() never returns NULL and returns distinct messages
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty message for every rcp_ep_i2c_errc_t value (including an out-of-range value), with a distinct message per defined error code.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_encode_transfer_request() encodes the requested RCP-level direction
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_encode_transfer_request() shall produce an ACF_ABB frame with evt == 0, byte_bus_id == byte_bus_id, transaction_num == transaction_num, payload exactly tx_data[0..tx_len), and op selected by direction: op == RCP_ACF_OP_READ (wire op=0, the payload-bearing-response direction) with read_size_or_segment_num == read_size for RCP_EP_I2C_DIR_READ, and op == RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE (wire op=1) with read_size_or_segment_num == 0 for RCP_EP_I2C_DIR_WRITE. The I2C-bus-level R/W bit inside the payload's address octet(s) is independent of op and shall be round-tripped unmodified.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.3 Figure 29 (i2c request format), TC18.txt L4829-4846; "no channel selector" per §13.5 Table 30 (I2C's row-2 group, only evt=111b defined), TC18.txt L3684-3693

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_transfer_request() round-trips payload, direction and read_size
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_transfer_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_i2c_encode_transfer_request() and the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_I2C_OK and recover the original tx bytes (address byte(s) included, unparsed), the encoded direction, the requested read_size (0 for RCP_EP_I2C_DIR_WRITE, whose header slot is a segment_num) and transaction_num unchanged, byte for byte.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.3 Figure 29 (i2c request format), TC18.txt L4829-4846; §13.7.7.1 ("Requests are accepted in ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB."), TC18.txt L4790-4791; evt[2:0] validation per §13.5 Table 30 (I2C's row-2 group, only evt=111b defined), TC18.txt L3684-3693

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_transfer_request() rejects a malformed or misaddressed frame and accepts both directions
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_transfer_request() shall return RCP_EP_I2C_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for the ACF_ABB fixed header or its declared payload length, RCP_EP_I2C_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE for a non-ACF_ABB frame, RCP_EP_I2C_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, and RCP_EP_I2C_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] is not 0b000 -- TC18 §13.5 Table 30's only legal value for a plain request in I2C's endpoint-type row; every other value shall be rejected with error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD at the dispatch layer. It shall accept BOTH op senses -- an I2C transfer is half duplex and either-directional, so neither is malformed -- and report which via *out_direction.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_encode_response() encodes the direction's op and the right framing
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_encode_response() shall produce an ACF_ABB frame when timed is false and an ACF_GBB frame with mtv == RCP_ACF_MTV_VALID and message_timestamp == timestamp when timed is true, in both cases with evt == 0 and op selected by direction: op == RCP_ACF_OP_READ with payload exactly rx_data[0..rx_len) for RCP_EP_I2C_DIR_READ (a read response has a byte_msg_payload), and op == RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE with no payload for RCP_EP_I2C_DIR_WRITE (a write response does not). It shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t when direction is not rcp_ep_i2c_dir_valid() or when rx_len != 0 with RCP_EP_I2C_DIR_WRITE.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.3 Figure 29 (i2c request format), TC18.txt L4829-4846; §13.7.7.3 ("The byte msg payload is the I2C payload including the address. The I2C endpoint does not know whether there is a 7- or 10-bit address, since the endpoint is just transparent."), TC18.txt L4830-4831

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_response() round-trips an untimed response
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_i2c_encode_response() with timed = false and the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_I2C_OK, recover the original rx payload bytes, the response's direction and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = false with *out_timestamp == 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.3 Figure 29 (i2c request format), TC18.txt L4829-4846; response timed/untimed ACF_GBB/ACF_ABB convention shared with every prior endpoint type

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_response() round-trips a timed response
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_i2c_encode_response() with timed = true, the same byte_bus_id, and a timestamp, return RCP_EP_I2C_OK, recover the original rx payload bytes, the response's direction and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = true with *out_timestamp equal to the original timestamp.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.3 Figure 29 (i2c request format), TC18.txt L4829-4846; response timed/untimed ACF_GBB/ACF_ABB convention shared with every prior endpoint type

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_response() rejects a malformed or misaddressed frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_decode_response() shall return RCP_EP_I2C_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for its applicable ACF fixed header and RCP_EP_I2C_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.3 Figure 29 (i2c request format), TC18.txt L4829-4846, TC18.txt L4846 -- general ACF frame-validation basis for the response wire format

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_dir_valid() accepts exactly the two defined directions
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_dir_valid() shall return true for RCP_EP_I2C_DIR_WRITE and RCP_EP_I2C_DIR_READ and false for any other value.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.1 ("The Client can request the I²C endpoint to send one or more bytes... Requests are accepted in ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB."), TC18.txt L4788-4791 -- I2C's genuinely bidirectional read/write op sense

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_encode_transfer_request() rejects unencodable direction/read_size inputs
requirements.text: rcp_ep_i2c_encode_transfer_request() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data == NULL) when direction is not rcp_ep_i2c_dir_valid(), when read_size exceeds RCP_EP_I2C_MAX_READ_SIZE (the ACF header read_size slot is 12 bits wide), or when read_size != 0 with direction RCP_EP_I2C_DIR_WRITE (in the write sense that slot carries a segment_num, not a read_size).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.3 Figure 29 (i2c request format), TC18.txt L4829-4846; "no channel selector" per §13.5 Table 30 (I2C's row-2 group, only evt=111b defined), TC18.txt L3684-3693

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_nr_bits_valid() accepts exactly 1..8
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_nr_bits_valid() shall return true for nr_bits in RCP_EP_UART_NR_BITS_MIN..RCP_EP_UART_NR_BITS_MAX (1..8) inclusive and false for 0 or any value above 8.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.2 Table 48 ("uart_nr_bits ... Nr of data bits", 8 bit R/W), TC18.txt L4930

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_bit_pad_mask() computes (1 << nr_bits) - 1, and 0 for an invalid nr_bits
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_bit_pad_mask() shall return (1u << nr_bits) - 1 for every rcp_ep_uart_nr_bits_valid() nr_bits (0xFF for nr_bits == 8, 0x7F for nr_bits == 7, ...) and 0 for any nr_bits outside 1..8.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.3 ("In case uart_nr_bits is not a multiple integer of 8, then the RC Client might need to append up to 'uart_nr_bits - 1' bits..."), TC18.txt L4989-4990

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_apply_bit_padding() masks every byte in place, and is a no-op for nr_bits == 8
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_apply_bit_padding() shall AND rcp_ep_uart_bit_pad_mask(nr_bits) into every byte of buf[0..len), leaving buf unchanged when nr_bits == 8 and clearing every byte to 0 when nr_bits is outside 1..8.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.3 ("When transmitting the EP ignores the last up to 'uart_nr_bits - 1' bits from the request payload, when the length of the payload is not an integer multiple of uart_nr_bits."), TC18.txt L4992-4993

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes cfg except uart_nr_bits
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_init() shall set every rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t flag in cfg->common to false, baud_rate/ep_rx_buffer_size/uart_timeout_ms to 0, parity to RCP_EP_UART_PARITY_NONE, stop_bits to RCP_EP_UART_STOP_BITS_ONE, and cfg->uart_nr_bits to RCP_EP_UART_NR_BITS_MAX (8), regardless of cfg's prior contents.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() is false while HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED, for any writer, by delegating to rcp_server_field_writable() with kind RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2177-2178

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() requires an authorized writer while HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() shall return true for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true, and false for an unauthorized writer. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group F): this entry previously claimed "regardless of writer's contents", superseded by REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036's authorization-gating fix (issue #198) -- the code was already correct; only this entry's own text had gone stale.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured 'root client' of via the discovery stream."), TC18.txt L2184

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() requires authorization once RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED when writer has neither via_root_client_ep0 nor via_owning_stream set, and true when either is set.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3 ("...only write access to the EP's functional configurations is allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client access EP0... Write access to some parameters might be prohibited in this life-cycle state, this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables."), TC18.txt L2203-2206, L2225-2226

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_set_baud_rate() rejects an unauthorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_set_baud_rate() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() does not authorize the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.2 Table 48 ("uart_baud_rate ... Baud rate in kbit/s", 16 bit R/W), TC18.txt L4929 -- NOTE: units diverge from TC18's own field (this implementation uses uint32_t with no documented unit); tracked separately at REQ-UART-037

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_set_baud_rate() applies an authorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_set_baud_rate() shall set cfg->baud_rate to baud_rate and return true when rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same authorization basis as REQ-UART-007

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_set_frame_format() rejects an invalid nr_bits
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_set_frame_format() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when nr_bits is not rcp_ep_uart_nr_bits_valid(), regardless of state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.2 Table 48 ("uart_nr_bits ... Nr of data bits", 8 bit R/W), TC18.txt L4930

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_set_frame_format() rejects an unauthorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_set_frame_format() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() does not authorize the write for state/writer, even when nr_bits is valid.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same authorization basis as REQ-UART-007

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_set_frame_format() applies a valid, authorized write to all three fields together
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_set_frame_format() shall set cfg->uart_nr_bits, cfg->parity, and cfg->stop_bits together and return true when nr_bits is rcp_ep_uart_nr_bits_valid() and rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.2 Table 48 ("uart_nr_bits"/"uart_parity_enable"/"uart_parity_pol"/"uart_stop_bits" fields), TC18.txt L4930, L4933, L4937, L4951

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_set_rx_buffer_size() rejects an unauthorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_set_rx_buffer_size() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() does not authorize the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("...the UART EP shifts the received data into a fifo-rx-buffer that has a length of uart_rx_fifo_size."), TC18.txt L4881 -- NOTE: TC18 describes uart_rx_fifo_size only in prose, not as a numbered Table 48 register; related gap tracked at REQ-UART-032/036

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_set_rx_buffer_size() applies an authorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_set_rx_buffer_size() shall set cfg->ep_rx_buffer_size to rx_buffer_size and return true when rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same authorization basis as REQ-UART-007

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_set_timeout() rejects an unauthorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_set_timeout() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() does not authorize the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.2 Table 48 ("uart_timeout ... receiver timeout in bit times, timeout is measure from last received stop bit", 8 bit R/W), TC18.txt L4952-4954 -- NOTE: units/representation diverge from TC18's own field; tracked separately at REQ-UART-037

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_set_timeout() applies an authorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_set_timeout() shall set cfg->uart_timeout_ms to timeout_ms and return true when rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same authorization basis as REQ-UART-007

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_strerror() never returns NULL and returns distinct messages
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty message for every rcp_ep_uart_errc_t value (including an out-of-range value), with a distinct message per defined error code.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_encode_write_request() encodes an ACF_ABB write with evt = 0
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_encode_write_request() shall produce an ACF_ABB frame with op == RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE, evt == 0, byte_bus_id == byte_bus_id, transaction_num == transaction_num, and payload exactly tx_data[0..tx_len).
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (ADC/PWM_IN/I²C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO row, evt[2:0]=000b-110b reserved so ordinary requests carry evt=0), TC18.txt L3684-3693; §13.7.8.1 ("A write request leads to a transmission of data to an external connected device."), TC18.txt L4883

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_decode_write_request() round-trips the raw TX payload
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_decode_write_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_uart_encode_write_request() and the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_UART_OK and recover the original tx bytes and transaction_num unchanged, byte for byte.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (ADC/PWM_IN/I²C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO row), TC18.txt L3684-3693

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_decode_write_request() rejects a malformed, misaddressed, misdirected, or wrong-evt frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_decode_write_request() shall return RCP_EP_UART_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for the ACF_ABB fixed header or its declared payload length, RCP_EP_UART_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE for a non-ACF_ABB frame, RCP_EP_UART_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, RCP_EP_UART_ERR_WRONG_OP when op is not RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE, and RCP_EP_UART_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] is not 0b000 -- TC18 §13.5 Table 30's only legal value for a plain request in UART's endpoint-type row; every other value shall be rejected with error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD at the dispatch layer.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_encode_write_response() encodes ACF_ABB when untimed and ACF_GBB when timed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_encode_write_response() shall produce an ACF_ABB frame when timed is false and an ACF_GBB frame with mtv == RCP_ACF_MTV_VALID and message_timestamp == timestamp when timed is true, in both cases with op == RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE, evt == 0, and payload exactly accepted_data[0..accepted_len).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("A write request leads to a transmission of data to an external connected device."), TC18.txt L4883; general ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB timed-response distinction, §11.2.1

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_decode_write_response() round-trips the accepted-bytes payload and timing
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_decode_write_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_uart_encode_write_response(), the same byte_bus_id, and either timed value, return RCP_EP_UART_OK, recover the accepted payload bytes and transaction_num, and report *out_timed/*out_timestamp consistently with the original timed/timestamp arguments; it shall return RCP_EP_UART_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for its applicable ACF fixed header and RCP_EP_UART_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("A write request leads to a transmission of data to an external connected device."), TC18.txt L4883

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_request() carries read_size in the ACF header's read_size_or_segment_num field, with no payload
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_request() shall produce an ACF_ABB frame with op == RCP_ACF_OP_READ, evt == 0, read_size_or_segment_num == read_size, byte_bus_id == byte_bus_id, transaction_num == transaction_num, and an empty payload.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("A read request will be started as soon as the fifo-rx-buffer is filled with as many bytes as requested in the read_size..."), TC18.txt L4884-4885

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_request() round-trips read_size and transaction_num
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_request() and the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_UART_OK and recover the original read_size and transaction_num unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (ADC/PWM_IN/I²C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO row), TC18.txt L3684-3693

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_request() rejects a payload-bearing read request with RCP_EP_UART_ERR_UNKNOWN_CMD
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_request() shall return RCP_EP_UART_ERR_UNKNOWN_CMD, rather than RCP_EP_UART_OK, when an otherwise well-formed read request carries a non-empty payload -- the deliberate asymmetry against GPIO/PWM_OUT request types documented in ep_uart.h. It shall also return RCP_EP_UART_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] is not 0b000 -- TC18 §13.5 Table 30's only legal value for a plain request in UART's endpoint-type row; every other value shall be rejected with error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD at the dispatch layer.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_response() encodes ACF_ABB when untimed and ACF_GBB when timed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_response() shall produce an ACF_ABB frame when timed is false and an ACF_GBB frame with mtv == RCP_ACF_MTV_VALID and message_timestamp == timestamp when timed is true, in both cases with op == RCP_ACF_OP_READ, evt == 0, and payload exactly rx_data[0..rx_len).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("...or in case the read_size is larger than the uart_rx_fifo_size, when the fifo is full. In the latter case the response is fragmented."), TC18.txt L4884-4886

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_response() round-trips a full-length and a short-read (single-AVTPDU) RX payload
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_response() with rx_len equal to or less than the originating request's read_size, return RCP_EP_UART_OK and recover the rx payload bytes, transaction_num, and timed/timestamp state unchanged, with no segment_num-based reassembly performed or required for a same-AVTPDU short read.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("...or in case the read_size is larger than the uart_rx_fifo_size, when the fifo is full. In the latter case the response is fragmented."), TC18.txt L4884-4886

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_response() rejects a malformed or misaddressed frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_response() shall return RCP_EP_UART_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for its applicable ACF fixed header and RCP_EP_UART_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (ADC/PWM_IN/I²C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO row), TC18.txt L3684-3693

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_write_semantics_valid() accepts exactly 0..7
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_write_semantics_valid() shall return true for every value v with v <= 7, and false for every v > 7.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 ("evt[2:0]" GPIO/PWM_OUT row, values 000b-111b), TC18.txt L3690-3717

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_REPLACE per field
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() shall, for evt == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_REPLACE, set result.period = request.period and result.active_duration = request.active_duration.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=000b: "The byte_msg_payload is presented at the interface"), TC18.txt L3694

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_OR per field
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() shall, for evt == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_OR, bitwise-OR request into current independently for the period and active_duration fields.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=001b: "The 'byte_msg_payload' bitwise OR 'current interface status' is written to the interface"), TC18.txt L3695-3698

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_AND per field
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() shall, for evt == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_AND, bitwise-AND request into current independently for the period and active_duration fields.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=010b: "The 'byte_msg_payload' bitwise AND 'current interface status' is written to the interface"), TC18.txt L3699-3702

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_XOR per field
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() shall, for evt == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_XOR, bitwise-XOR request into current independently for the period and active_duration fields.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=011b: "The 'byte_msg_payload' bitwise XOR 'current interface status' is written to the interface"), TC18.txt L3703-3706

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_ADD with per-field 16-bit saturation
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() shall, for evt == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_ADD, add request to current independently for the period and active_duration fields, each saturating at 0xFFFF rather than wrapping or carrying into the other field.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=101b: "The 'byte_msg_payload' plus 'current interface status' is written to the interface"), TC18.txt L3709-3711; saturation rule, TC18.txt L3719-3720

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() implements RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_SUB as request minus current with per-field 16-bit saturation
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() shall, for evt == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_SUB, subtract current from request independently for the period and active_duration fields, each saturating at 0x0000 rather than wrapping.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=110b: "'byte_msg_payload' minus 'current interface status' is written as is to interface"), TC18.txt L3712-3714; saturation rule, TC18.txt L3719-3720

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() treats RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_RESERVED4 as a no-op
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() shall return current unchanged for evt == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_RESERVED4.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=100b: "reserved -request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"), TC18.txt L3707-3708

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() fails safe for a misrouted RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_RECONFIG
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() shall return current unchanged for evt == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_WRITE_RECONFIG, since callers must route that value to rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_reconfig() instead.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=111b: "The byte_msg_payload is not presented to the interface but used to change the configuration of the endpoint (see 12.7.1)."), TC18.txt L3715-3717

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_reconfig() applies an addressed write into the PWM_OUT EP_func register block
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_reconfig() shall interpret its payload as a 16-bit big-endian relative start address followed by configuration data octets, and shall write those octets into cfg's EP_func registers from that address onward, leaving read-only registers (EP_LEN, the reserved octet, base_clk) unchanged while still applying the rest of the addressed span, and shall return RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_RECONFIG_OK.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.2 Table 43 (pwmo functional configuration register block), TC18.txt L4557-4607

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_reconfig() ignores a configuration write that is short or extends past EP_LEN
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_reconfig() shall return RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_RECONFIG_ERR_SHORT when the payload does not carry a 2-octet address plus at least one data octet, and RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE when start_address plus the data length exceeds RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_EP_FUNC_LEN; in both cases cfg shall be left entirely unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.2 Table 43 (pwmo functional configuration register block, pwmo_ep_len fixed at 0x06), TC18.txt L4557-4607

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires() never fires for RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_TRIGGER_NONE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires() shall return false for trigger == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_TRIGGER_NONE regardless of event. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): NONE is this module's own original addition -- TC18 Table 42 documents three fixed, always-on trigger signals with no off/none state, and Table 43 defines no client-selectable register for choosing among them at all. See ep_pwm.h's own file header for the full clarification.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.1 Table 42 ("A PWM endpoint creates three trigger events"), TC18.txt L4525-4537 -- names three fixed hardware signals, not a client-configurable field; Table 43 (pwmo functional configuration), TC18.txt L4562-4602, defines no trigger-select register

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_TRIGGER_CYCLE_START
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires() shall return true for trigger == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_TRIGGER_CYCLE_START iff event == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_EVENT_CYCLE_START. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): this evaluates one of Table 42's three fixed hardware signals against a caller-selected mode -- an original single-select simplification of TC18's own always-on, non-selectable signal model; see ep_pwm.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.1 Table 42 (trigger signal 1, "at the start of the cycle"), TC18.txt L4534 -- a fixed hardware signal, not a client-configurable field

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_TRIGGER_MID_PULSE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires() shall return true for trigger == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_TRIGGER_MID_PULSE iff event == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_EVENT_MID_PULSE. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): this evaluates one of Table 42's three fixed hardware signals against a caller-selected mode -- an original single-select simplification of TC18's own always-on, non-selectable signal model; see ep_pwm.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.1 Table 42 (trigger signal 2, "in the middle of the active pulse"), TC18.txt L4535 -- a fixed hardware signal, not a client-configurable field

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_TRIGGER_DONE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires() shall return true for trigger == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_TRIGGER_DONE iff event == RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_EVENT_DONE. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): this evaluates one of Table 42's three fixed hardware signals against a caller-selected mode -- an original single-select simplification of TC18's own always-on, non-selectable signal model; see ep_pwm.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.1 Table 42 (trigger signal 0, "PWM request exec done (requested values applied)"), TC18.txt L4533 -- a fixed hardware signal, not a client-configurable field

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_init() shall set every common flag false, trigger = RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_TRIGGER_NONE, and every EP_func register (base_clk, ep_status, clk_divider, signal_flags, duty_cycle_min, duty_cycle_max, skew) to 0, regardless of cfg's prior contents.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_writable() is unwritable while HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED regardless of writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2177-2178

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_writable() requires an authorized writer while HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_writable() shall return true for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true, and false for an unauthorized writer. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group F): this entry previously claimed "regardless of writer", superseded by REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036's authorization-gating fix (issue #198) -- the code and this module's own test (test_out_functional_cfg_writable_hw_configured_requires_authorization_or_discovery_stream, tests/test_ep_pwm.c) were already correct; only this entry's own text had gone stale.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured 'root client' of via the discovery stream."), TC18.txt L2184

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_writable() requires authorization once RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED when writer indicates neither via_root_client_ep0 nor via_owning_stream, and true when either is set.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3 ("...only write access to the EP's functional configurations is allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client access EP0... Write access to some parameters might be prohibited in this life-cycle state, this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables."), TC18.txt L2203-2206, L2225-2226

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_set_trigger() rejects an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_set_trigger() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-PWM-019

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_set_trigger() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_set_trigger() shall return true and set cfg->trigger to the requested trigger when the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-PWM-019

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_set_enabled() rejects an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_set_enabled() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-PWM-019

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_set_enabled() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_set_enabled() shall return true and set cfg->common.ep_enable to the requested value when the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-PWM-019

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_strerror() never returns NULL and is unique per code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty, distinct message for each rcp_ep_pwm_out_errc_t value, including an out-of-range value.

requirements.title: PWM_OUT read request encode/decode round-trips
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_read_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_pwm_out_encode_read_request() with the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_OK and recover the original transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3710 (general ACF frame-validation basis for the request/response wire format)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_read_request() rejects a malformed, misaddressed, or wrong-op frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_read_request() shall return RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame shorter than the ACF_ABB fixed header, RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE for a non-ACF_ABB frame, RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, and RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_ERR_WRONG_OP when op is not RCP_ACF_OP_READ.

requirements.title: PWM_OUT write request encode/decode round-trips, including evt[2:0] write semantics
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_write_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_pwm_out_encode_write_request() with the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_OK and recover the original value, evt[2:0], and transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.3 ("The PWM_out request and response contain two values in the payload. The active time of the PWM signal as well as the period of the signal in clock ticks of the clock selected for this PWM_out endpoint."), TC18.txt L4621-4623; evt[2:0] semantics per §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3690-3717
