requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_write_request() rejects a malformed, wrong-op, or bad-payload-length frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_write_request() shall return RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_ERR_WRONG_OP when op is not RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE, and RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_ERR_BAD_PAYLOAD_LEN when the payload is not exactly RCP_EP_PWM_PAYLOAD_LEN octets.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.3 ("A request not having exactly four bytes is rejected and an error response with error code = INVALID_PARAMETER will be sent."), TC18.txt L4630-4631

requirements.title: PWM_OUT response encode/decode round-trips when untimed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_pwm_out_encode_response() with timed = false and the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_OK, recover the original value and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = false with *out_timestamp = 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.3 ("The PWM_out request and response contain two values in the payload."), TC18.txt L4621-4623

requirements.title: PWM_OUT response encode/decode round-trips when timed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_pwm_out_encode_response() with timed = true, the same byte_bus_id, and a timestamp, return RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_OK, recover the original value and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = true with *out_timestamp equal to the original timestamp.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.3 ("The PWM_out request and response contain two values in the payload."), TC18.txt L4621-4623

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_response() rejects a malformed or misaddressed frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_out_decode_response() shall return RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for its applicable ACF fixed header and RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3710 (general ACF frame-validation basis)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_trigger_fires() never fires for RCP_EP_PWM_IN_TRIGGER_NONE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_trigger_fires() shall return false for trigger == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_TRIGGER_NONE regardless of the level transition. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): NONE is this module's own original addition -- TC18 Table 44 documents two fixed, always-on trigger signals with no off/none state and no client-selectable register at all (PWM_IN's functional config has no trigger-select field). See ep_pwm.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.1 Table 44 ("The PWM_IN endpoint generates two trigger events"), TC18.txt L4673-4676 -- names two fixed hardware signals, not a client-configurable field

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_PWM_IN_TRIGGER_RISING
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_trigger_fires() shall return true for trigger == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_TRIGGER_RISING iff prev_level is false and new_level is true. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): this evaluates one of Table 44's two fixed hardware signals against a caller-selected mode -- an original single-select simplification; see ep_pwm.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.1 Table 44 (trigger signal 0, "rising edge of PWM_IN signal"), TC18.txt L4674 -- a fixed hardware signal, not a client-configurable field

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_trigger_fires() implements RCP_EP_PWM_IN_TRIGGER_FALLING
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_trigger_fires() shall return true for trigger == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_TRIGGER_FALLING iff prev_level is true and new_level is false. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): this evaluates one of Table 44's two fixed hardware signals against a caller-selected mode -- an original single-select simplification; see ep_pwm.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.1 Table 44 (trigger signal 1, "falling edge of PWM_IN signal"), TC18.txt L4675 -- a fixed hardware signal, not a client-configurable field

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_init() shall set every common flag false and trigger = RCP_EP_PWM_IN_TRIGGER_NONE, regardless of cfg's prior contents.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_writable() is unwritable while HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED regardless of writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2177-2178

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_writable() requires an authorized writer while HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_writable() shall return true for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true, and false for an unauthorized writer. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group F): this entry previously claimed "regardless of writer", the same staleness as REQ-PWM-018's PWM_OUT counterpart -- the code and this module's own test (test_in_functional_cfg_writable_hw_configured_requires_authorization_or_discovery_stream, tests/test_ep_pwm.c) were already correct; only this entry's own text had gone stale.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured 'root client' of via the discovery stream."), TC18.txt L2184

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_writable() requires authorization once RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED when writer indicates neither via_root_client_ep0 nor via_owning_stream, and true when either is set.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2203-2206, L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-PWM-019

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_set_trigger() rejects an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_set_trigger() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-PWM-019

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_set_trigger() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_set_trigger() shall return true and set cfg->trigger to the requested trigger when the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same basis as REQ-PWM-019

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_strerror() never returns NULL and is unique per code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty, distinct message for each rcp_ep_pwm_in_errc_t value.

requirements.title: PWM_IN read request encode/decode round-trips
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_read_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_pwm_in_encode_read_request() with the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_PWM_IN_OK and recover the original transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.3 ("The PWM_IN request and response contain two 16 bit values in the payload... The interpretation of the evt-bits is described in the section 'The usage of evt bits in requests'."), TC18.txt L4757-4758

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_read_request() rejects a malformed or misaddressed frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_read_request() shall return RCP_EP_PWM_IN_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame shorter than the ACF_ABB fixed header and RCP_EP_PWM_IN_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3710 (general ACF frame-validation basis)

requirements.title: PWM_IN response encode/decode round-trips when untimed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_pwm_in_encode_response() with timed = false and the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_PWM_IN_OK, recover the original value and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = false with *out_timestamp = 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.3 ("Responses include the measured active time of the PWM signal as well as the period of the signal in clock ticks of the clock selected for this PWM_IN endpoint."), TC18.txt L4759-4761

requirements.title: PWM_IN response encode/decode round-trips when timed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_pwm_in_encode_response() with timed = true, the same byte_bus_id, and a timestamp, return RCP_EP_PWM_IN_OK, recover the original value and transaction_num, and report *out_timed = true with *out_timestamp equal to the original timestamp.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.3 ("Responses include the measured active time of the PWM signal as well as the period of the signal in clock ticks of the clock selected for this PWM_IN endpoint."), TC18.txt L4759-4761

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_response() rejects a misaddressed frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_response() shall return RCP_EP_PWM_IN_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3710 (general ACF frame-validation basis)

requirements.title: PWM_IN response encode/decode round-trips RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL verbatim
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_pwm_in_encode_response() with either or both of value's fields equal to RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL, recover that sentinel unchanged, treating it as an ordinary uint16_t value with no special decode-time handling.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_mode_valid() accepts exactly 4..7
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_mode_valid() shall return true for every value v with 4 <= v <= 7, and false for every other value.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1 ("evt[2:0] = 100b ... wait condition is met when the first two bytes... larger or equal..." through "evt[2:0] = 111b"), TC18.txt L3771-3782

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() implements RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_PERIOD_GE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() shall, for mode == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_PERIOD_GE, return true iff captured.period is not RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL and captured.period <= threshold (threshold is TC18's byte_msg_payload, captured.period is the current interface status -- "GE" describes payload >= status, not status >= threshold). Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group B): this entry, and the code it described, previously had the comparison reversed (captured.period >= threshold), contradicted by both the primary source and this codebase's own reference implementation of the identical §13.5.1 rule, rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() (src/acf.c).
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1 ("evt[2:0] = 100b 0xB - wait condition is met when the first two bytes of the first quadlet of 'byte_msg_payload' is larger or equal to the first two bytes of the first quadlet of the 'current interface status' (example: this can be used to check the period of PWM_in)"), TC18.txt L3771-3773

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() implements RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_PERIOD_LE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() shall, for mode == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_PERIOD_LE, return true iff captured.period is not RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL and captured.period >= threshold (threshold is TC18's byte_msg_payload, captured.period is the current interface status -- "LE" describes payload <= status, not status <= threshold). Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group B): this entry, and the code it described, previously had the comparison reversed (captured.period <= threshold), the mirror of REQ-PWM-049's own correction.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1 ("evt[2:0] = 101b - wait condition is met when the first two bytes of the first quadlet of 'byte_msg_payload' is smaller or to equal the first two bytes of the first quadlet of the 'current interface status' (example: this can be used to check the period of PWM_in)"), TC18.txt L3774-3776

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() implements RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_DUTY_GE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() shall, for mode == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_DUTY_GE, return true iff captured.active_duration is not RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL and captured.active_duration <= threshold (threshold is TC18's byte_msg_payload, captured.active_duration is the current interface status -- "GE" describes payload >= status, not status >= threshold). Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group B): this entry, and the code it described, previously had the comparison reversed (captured.active_duration >= threshold), the same class of error as REQ-PWM-049.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1 ("evt[2:0] = 110b - wait condition is met when the last two bytes of the first quadlet of 'byte_msg_payload' is larger or equal to the last two bytes of the first quadlet of the 'current interface status' (example: this can be used to check the duty_cycle of PWM_in)"), TC18.txt L3777-3779

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() implements RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_DUTY_LE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() shall, for mode == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_DUTY_LE, return true iff captured.active_duration is not RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL and captured.active_duration >= threshold (threshold is TC18's byte_msg_payload, captured.active_duration is the current interface status -- "LE" describes payload <= status, not status <= threshold). Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group B): this entry, and the code it described, previously had the comparison reversed (captured.active_duration <= threshold), the mirror of REQ-PWM-051's own correction.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1 ("evt[2:0] = 111b - wait condition is met when the last two bytes of the first quadlet of 'byte_msg_payload' is smaller or to equal... (example: this can be used to check the duty_cycle of PWM_in)"), TC18.txt L3780-3782

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() returns false for an invalid mode
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() shall return false, never treating it as a match, for any mode value outside RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_PERIOD_GE..RCP_EP_PWM_IN_CMP_DUTY_LE (4..7).
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1, TC18.txt L3771-3782 -- only evt[2:0]=100b..111b (4..7) are defined compound-wait comparison modes for PWM_in in this table

requirements.title: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() never matches a RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL sub-field
requirements.text: rcp_ep_pwm_in_compound_wait_compare() shall return false for every defined mode whenever the sub-field that mode compares (captured.period for PERIOD_GE/PERIOD_LE, captured.active_duration for DUTY_GE/DUTY_LE) equals RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL, regardless of threshold.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_response_value_count() returns half a request's read_size
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_response_value_count() shall return read_size / RCP_EP_ADC_VALUE_LEN when read_size is even, and 0 when read_size is odd.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("Responses contain as much measurement values as requested by half the read size of a request."), TC18.txt L5162-5163

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() computes the arithmetic mean of its raw samples
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() shall, given sample_count samples none of which equal RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL, return a value equal to their arithmetic mean, rounded down.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.1 ("...further samples are taken with a timely distance of one 'adc_sample_interval'... For the readings acquired during the averaging interval given in number of samples... the average is calculated."), TC18.txt L5036-5040

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() returns RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL with a zero timestamp when sample_count is 0
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() shall return value == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL and timestamp == 0 when sample_count == 0.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() excludes RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL samples from its mean, and reports NO_SIGNAL only if every sample timed out
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() shall exclude every sample whose value equals RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL from its arithmetic mean, and shall return value == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL only when every sample in the interval equals RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() reports the timestamp of the last sample that fed the mean
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() shall set the returned timestamp to the timestamp of the last samples[i] not equal to RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL, or, when every sample timed out, to samples[sample_count - 1].timestamp, for any sample_count > 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("If the response includes a timestamp, it shall represent the point in time when the last sample that was used for the first average value that is included in the response has been captured."), TC18.txt L5143-5145

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() packs averaged values in capture order
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() shall copy avg_values[i].value into out_values[i] for i in 0..min(avg_count, value_count), preserving capture order.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.1 ("...the COMBINE_NR_VAL defines how many measurement values (i.e. averaging results) will be put in one response frame."), TC18.txt L5040-5042

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() packs exactly value_count values when enough are available
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() shall, when avg_count >= value_count, write exactly value_count values -- the leading ones -- and return value_count.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.2 Table 51 ("adc_combine_avg_values ... Nr of output values to be combined in one response"), TC18.txt L5110-5111

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() reports a short count without touching the unwritten entries
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() shall, when avg_count < value_count, write avg_count values, return avg_count, and leave out_values[avg_count..value_count) untouched.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.2 ("When adc_combine_avg_values < adc_avg_intervals_per_request, then there are multiple responses per request execution."), TC18.txt L5132-5133

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() carries RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL through verbatim
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() shall copy an avg_values[i].value equal to RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL into its own out_values slot unchanged, never substituting or averaging it away.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() returns 0 when either count is 0
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() shall return 0 and write nothing when avg_count == 0 or value_count == 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("Responses contain as much measurement values as requested by half the read size of a request."), TC18.txt L5162-5163

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_encode_response() carries value_count measurement values and reports 2 * value_count as read_size
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_encode_response() shall encode values[0..value_count) as a value_count * RCP_EP_ADC_VALUE_LEN octet big-endian payload with the header's read_size set to that payload length, and shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t when value_count is 0 or exceeds RCP_EP_ADC_MAX_VALUES.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("Responses contain as much measurement values as requested by half the read size of a request."), TC18.txt L5162-5163

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_capture_moment_timestamp() returns the first response value's timestamp
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_capture_moment_timestamp() shall return avg_values[0].timestamp for any avg_count > 0 -- the moment the last sample feeding the response's first measurement value was captured.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("If the response includes a timestamp, it shall represent the point in time when the last sample that was used for the first average value that is included in the response has been captured."), TC18.txt L5143-5145

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_capture_moment_timestamp() returns 0 when avg_count is 0
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_capture_moment_timestamp() shall return 0 when avg_count == 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("If the response includes a timestamp, it shall represent the point in time when the last sample..."), TC18.txt L5143-5145

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_init() shall set every common flag false and adc_samples_per_avg_interval, adc_avg_intervals_per_request and adc_combine_avg_values all to 0, regardless of cfg's prior contents.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable() is unwritable while HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED regardless of writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2177-2178

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable() is writable by any writer while HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable() shall return true for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED regardless of writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2177-2178 -- writable once concluded (i.e. HW_CONFIGURED)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable() requires authorization once RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for state == RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED when writer indicates neither via_root_client_ep0 nor via_owning_stream, and true when either is set.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3 ("...only write access to the EP's functional configurations is allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client access EP0... Write access to some parameters might be prohibited in this life-cycle state, this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables."), TC18.txt L2203-2206, L2225-2226

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_set_samples_per_avg_interval() rejects an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_set_samples_per_avg_interval() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same authorization basis as REQ-ADC-019 (corrected 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group J: this entry previously cited §13.7.9.1's own averaging-interval prose, TC18.txt L5040/L5107 -- background on why this field is writable at all, not the authorization-rejection behavior this requirement actually describes; REQ-ADC-019's own citation already correctly names this entry as sharing its W*-marker basis, so this entry's citation was the one out of step)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_set_samples_per_avg_interval() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_set_samples_per_avg_interval() shall return true and set cfg->adc_samples_per_avg_interval to the requested value when the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same authorization basis as REQ-ADC-018

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_set_avg_intervals_per_request() rejects an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_set_avg_intervals_per_request() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.2 Table 51 ("adc_avg_intervals_per_request ... Intervals to be captures per measurement cycle"), TC18.txt L5102-5103; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_set_avg_intervals_per_request() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_set_avg_intervals_per_request() shall return true and set cfg->adc_avg_intervals_per_request to the requested value when the write is authorized.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same authorization basis as REQ-ADC-018

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_set_combine_avg_values() rejects an unauthorized write without mutating cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_set_combine_avg_values() shall return false and leave cfg unchanged when the write is not authorized by rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_writable().
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.2 Table 51 ("adc_combine_avg_values ... Nr of output values to be combined in one response"), TC18.txt L5110-5111; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_set_combine_avg_values() applies the write when authorized
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_set_combine_avg_values() shall return true and set cfg->adc_combine_avg_values to the requested output-value count when the write is authorized; every value the one-octet field can hold is a legal count.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2225-2226 (W* marker convention) -- same authorization basis as REQ-ADC-018

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_strerror() never returns NULL and is unique per code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty, distinct message for each rcp_ep_adc_errc_t value, including an out-of-range value.

requirements.title: ADC read request encode/decode round-trips, carrying read_size
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_decode_read_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_adc_encode_read_request() with the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_ADC_OK and recover the original read_size and transaction_num; the request itself shall carry no payload.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("The ADC request has no byte_msg_payload..."), TC18.txt L5162

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_decode_read_request() rejects a malformed, misaddressed, wrong-op, or wrong-evt frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_decode_read_request() shall return RCP_EP_ADC_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame shorter than the ACF_ABB fixed header, RCP_EP_ADC_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, RCP_EP_ADC_ERR_WRONG_OP when op is not RCP_ACF_OP_READ, and RCP_EP_ADC_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] is not 0b000 -- TC18 §13.5 Table 30's only legal value for a plain request in ADC's endpoint-type row (ADC, PWM_IN, I2C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO); every other value shall be rejected with error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD at the dispatch layer.

requirements.title: ADC response encode/decode round-trips every measurement value when untimed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_adc_encode_response() with timed = false and the same byte_bus_id, return RCP_EP_ADC_OK, recover all value_count values in order plus the original transaction_num, and report *out_timed = false with *out_timestamp = 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("Responses contain as much measurement values as requested by half the read size of a request." / Figure 32, "Response with a single measurement value"), TC18.txt L5162-5167

requirements.title: ADC response encode/decode round-trips every measurement value when timed
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_adc_encode_response() with timed = true, the same byte_bus_id, and a timestamp, return RCP_EP_ADC_OK, recover all value_count values in order plus the original transaction_num, and report *out_timed = true with *out_timestamp equal to the original timestamp.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("Responses contain as much measurement values as requested by half the read size of a request." / Figure 32), TC18.txt L5162-5167

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_decode_response() rejects a bad-payload-length or over-long frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_decode_response() shall return RCP_EP_ADC_ERR_BAD_PAYLOAD_LEN when the decoded payload is empty or is not a whole number of RCP_EP_ADC_VALUE_LEN-octet values, and RCP_EP_ADC_ERR_TOO_MANY_VALUES when the payload holds more values than max_values.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (ADC/PWM_IN/I²C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO row), TC18.txt L3684-3693

requirements.title: ADC response encode/decode round-trips RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL verbatim in its own value slot
requirements.text: rcp_ep_adc_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_adc_encode_response() where some values[i] == RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL, recover that sentinel unchanged in out_values[i].

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_table_new() treats count == 0 as unsupported, not a failure
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_table_new() shall, given count == 0, return a table with state == NULL and count == 0, and rcp_sequencer_table_unsupported() shall report true for that table.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 ("[an implementation] may support only a lower number of sequencers"), TC18.txt L3473

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_table_new() reports allocation failure via a zeroed table
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_table_new() shall, given a nonzero count for which the underlying allocation fails, return a table with state == NULL and count == 0.
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("After power-on/reset all sequencers are in state 1."), TC18.txt L3468; §12.7.10 ("Upon power-on reset all sequencer state values are set to '1'."), TC18.txt L3068-3069

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_table_new() initializes every register to the power-on default
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_table_new() shall, given a nonzero count for which allocation succeeds, return a table with count registers, each initialized to RCP_SEQUENCER_POWER_ON_STATE (1).
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("After power-on/reset all sequencers are in state 1."), TC18.txt L3468; §12.7.10 ("Upon power-on reset all sequencer state values are set to '1'."), TC18.txt L3068-3069

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_table_unsupported() is true iff count == 0
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_table_unsupported() shall return true iff table->count == 0.
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("An RC Server implementation may support only a lower number of sequencers."), TC18.txt L3473-3474; the implementation of one or more sequencers into an RC Server is optional, TC18.txt L3072-3073

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_table_reset() restores every register to the power-on default
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_table_reset() shall set every sequencer in a nonzero-count table back to RCP_SEQUENCER_POWER_ON_STATE, and shall be a no-op on a count == 0 table.
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("After power-on/reset all sequencers are in state 1."), TC18.txt L3468; §12.7.10 ("Upon power-on reset all sequencer state values are set to '1'."), TC18.txt L3068-3069

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_table_free() zeroes the table and is idempotent
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_table_free() shall free table->state (if any) and set table->state = NULL and table->count = 0, and shall be safe to call again on an already-zeroed table.
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("Sequencers are simply a state register which stores the current state of the sequencer."), TC18.txt L3466; readable/writable via §12.7.10's SEQUENCER_config register map, TC18.txt L3075-3092

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_index_valid() bounds idx to 0..count-1
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_index_valid() shall return true iff idx < table->count.
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("The number of sequencers and states per sequencer are limited to 256 by this definition."), TC18.txt L3472-3473

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_get_state() reads the current state of a valid index
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_get_state() shall, given a valid idx, return true and set *out_state to table->state[idx].
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("Sequencers are simply a state register which stores the current state of the sequencer."), TC18.txt L3466; readable/writable via §12.7.10's SEQUENCER_config register map, TC18.txt L3075-3092

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_get_state() rejects an invalid index without touching *out_state
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_get_state() shall, given an idx for which rcp_sequencer_index_valid() is false, return false and leave *out_state unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("The number of sequencers and states per sequencer are limited to 256 by this definition."), TC18.txt L3472-3473

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_set_state() overwrites the state of a valid index
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_set_state() shall, given a valid idx, set table->state[idx] to state and return true.
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("Sequencers are simply a state register which stores the current state of the sequencer."), TC18.txt L3466; readable/writable via §12.7.10's SEQUENCER_config register map, TC18.txt L3075-3092; §12.7.10 Table 25 ("Seq_state ... if manually set to 0 then disabled"), TC18.txt L3082, L3090

requirements.title: rcp_sequencer_set_state() rejects an invalid index without changing table
requirements.text: rcp_sequencer_set_state() shall, given an idx for which rcp_sequencer_index_valid() is false, return false and leave table entirely unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("The number of sequencers and states per sequencer are limited to 256 by this definition."), TC18.txt L3472-3473

requirements.title: rcp_request_type_is_safety() reports the MSB (0x80) of request_type
requirements.text: rcp_request_type_is_safety() shall return true iff (request_type & 0x80) != 0.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 (request_type MSB selects the safety variant), TC18.txt L1189-1191

requirements.title: rcp_request_type_is_compound() recognizes RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_COMPOUND and its safety variant
requirements.text: rcp_request_type_is_compound() shall return true iff request_type == RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_COMPOUND or request_type == RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_COMPOUND_SAFETY.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 (request_type 0x0F/0x8F = Compound), TC18.txt L1194

requirements.title: rcp_request_type_is_compound_wait() recognizes RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_COMPOUND_WAIT and its safety variant
requirements.text: rcp_request_type_is_compound_wait() shall return true iff request_type == RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_COMPOUND_WAIT or request_type == RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_COMPOUND_WAIT_SAFETY.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 (request_type 0x0B/0x8B = Compound wait), TC18.txt L1195

requirements.title: rcp_compound_strerror() never returns NULL and is unique per code
requirements.text: rcp_compound_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty, distinct message for each rcp_compound_errc_t value, and a non-NULL message for any other value.

requirements.title: rcp_compound_peek_request_type() rejects a frame shorter than the ACF_GBB header
requirements.text: rcp_compound_peek_request_type() shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_SHORT_FRAME when len < RCP_ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: rcp_compound_peek_request_type() rejects a non-ACF_GBB message
requirements.text: rcp_compound_peek_request_type() shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE when b[0] != RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: rcp_compound_peek_request_type() reads the repurposed opcode byte when mtv is untimed
requirements.text: rcp_compound_peek_request_type() shall, given a well-formed ACF_GBB frame whose decoded mtv nibble equals RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED, return RCP_COMPOUND_OK and set *out_request_type to b[RCP_ACF_ABB_HEADER_LEN]; and shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_NOT_REPURPOSED when that mtv nibble is not RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("first byte in message_timestamp field" -> "type of condition": 0x0F/0x8F Compound, 0x0B/0x8B Compound wait), TC18.txt L1186-1199

requirements.title: rcp_compound_encode_request() rejects an unrecognized request_type
requirements.text: rcp_compound_encode_request() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data == NULL) when request_type is neither rcp_request_type_is_compound() nor rcp_request_type_is_compound_wait().
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.1 Table 6 / Figure 8 (GBB message for compound requests: request_type, cmp_start_state, cmp_next_state, cmp_sequencer, cmp_exec_delay, cmp_repetitions), TC18.txt L1221-1281; §11.2.2.2 Table 7 / Figure 9 (GBB message for compound wait requests: request_type, cmpw_start_state, cmpw_next_state, cmpw_sequencer, cmpw_exec_delay, cmpw_repetitions), TC18.txt L1320-1389

requirements.title: rcp_compound_encode_request() rejects an oversized payload
requirements.text: rcp_compound_encode_request() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data == NULL) when payload_len exceeds RCP_ACF_MAX_PAYLOAD.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.1 Table 6 / Figure 8 (GBB message for compound requests: request_type, cmp_start_state, cmp_next_state, cmp_sequencer, cmp_exec_delay, cmp_repetitions), TC18.txt L1221-1281; §11.2.2.2 Table 7 / Figure 9 (GBB message for compound wait requests: request_type, cmpw_start_state, cmpw_next_state, cmpw_sequencer, cmpw_exec_delay, cmpw_repetitions), TC18.txt L1320-1389

requirements.title: rcp_compound_encode_request() packs the step at the specification's own sub-field offsets
requirements.text: rcp_compound_encode_request() shall, given a recognized request_type and payload_len <= RCP_ACF_MAX_PAYLOAD, produce an RCP_ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN + payload_len byte frame of type RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB addressed to byte_bus_id with mtv forced to RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED, and shall write the repurposed message_timestamp region as: request_type at octet offset 0, step->start_state at offset 1, step->next_state at offset 2, step->sequencer_index at offset 3, step->exec_delay as two big-endian octets at offsets 4-5, and step->repeat_count as two big-endian octets at offsets 6-7 (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.1 Figure 8 / Table 6, §11.2.2.2 Figure 9 / Table 7).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Figure 9 (compound-wait GBB sub-field offsets), TC18.txt L1316-1328

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_request() rejects a frame shorter than declared
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_request() shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_SHORT_FRAME when b is shorter than the ACF_GBB fixed header or its declared payload length.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_request() rejects a non-ACF_GBB message
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_request() shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE when b[0] != RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_request() rejects a message whose mtv is not untimed
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_request() shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_NOT_REPURPOSED when the decoded byte_message_info.mtv is not RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_request() rejects a request_type it does not recognize
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_request() shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_UNKNOWN_TYPE when the decoded opcode byte is neither rcp_request_type_is_compound() nor rcp_request_type_is_compound_wait().
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("first byte in message_timestamp field" -> "type of condition": 0x0F/0x8F Compound, 0x0B/0x8B Compound wait), TC18.txt L1186-1199

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_request() recovers every sub-field from the specification's own offsets
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_request() shall, given a frame whose repurposed message_timestamp region carries the layout REQ-CMP-010 defines, return RCP_COMPOUND_OK and recover request_type, byte_bus_id, transaction_num, and every rcp_compound_step_t sub-field (start_state, next_state, sequencer_index, exec_delay, repeat_count) from those same offsets and widths, with sequencer_index one octet wide and repeat_count two octets wide.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Figure 9 (compound-wait GBB sub-field offsets), TC18.txt L1316-1328

requirements.title: rcp_compound_encode_clear_non_safestate() encodes an RCP_ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN-byte, opcode-0x06, mtv-untimed frame
requirements.text: rcp_compound_encode_clear_non_safestate() shall produce an RCP_ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN-byte frame of type RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB addressed to byte_bus_id, echoing transaction_num, with mtv RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED and the message_timestamp region's leading byte equal to RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_CLEAR_NON_SAFESTATE and its remaining 7 bytes zero.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 12 (clear-non-safestate, request_type 0x06), TC18.txt L1759-1775

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_clear_non_safestate() round-trips a frame produced by its own encoder
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_clear_non_safestate() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_compound_encode_clear_non_safestate(), return RCP_COMPOUND_OK and recover the original byte_bus_id and transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Figure 14 (clear-non-safestate GBB layout), TC18.txt L1737-1750

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_clear_non_safestate() rejects a request_type other than 0x06
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_clear_non_safestate() shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_UNKNOWN_TYPE when the decoded opcode byte is not RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_CLEAR_NON_SAFESTATE, given the same short-frame/bad-msg-type/not-repurposed failure modes as rcp_compound_decode_request().
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 12 (clear-non-safestate, request_type 0x06), TC18.txt L1759-1775

requirements.title: rcp_compound_advance_guard() is true iff the target sequencer is still in start_state
requirements.text: rcp_compound_advance_guard() shall return true iff step->sequencer_index is rcp_sequencer_index_valid() for table and table's current state at that index equals step->start_state, and shall return false for an invalid index. It shall not treat a start_state of zero specially -- that sentinel governs whether a request may start (REQ-CMP-025), not whether its sequencer is advanced afterwards.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.1 ("the state (cmp_next_state) the sequencer shall enter after the compound request has been executed (if the sequencer is still in cmp_start_state)"), TC18.txt L1207-1211

requirements.title: rcp_compound_exec_delay_elapsed() compares elapsed against exec_delay
requirements.text: rcp_compound_exec_delay_elapsed() shall return true iff elapsed >= step->exec_delay, both expressed in multiples of the addressed endpoint's configured ep_delay_time (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.1 Table 6), not in milliseconds.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.1 Table 6 ("cmp_exec_delay: delay time between the sequencer reaching the state defined in start_state and the start of the execution of the request... execution shall happen even in case the state changes before the delay expired"), TC18.txt L1262-1265

requirements.title: rcp_compound_tick() advances the sequencer only once both the delay has elapsed and the guard holds
requirements.text: rcp_compound_tick() shall set table's sequencer step->sequencer_index to step->next_state and return true iff both rcp_compound_exec_delay_elapsed(step, elapsed) and rcp_compound_advance_guard(table, step) hold; otherwise it shall leave table unchanged and return false. When step->next_state is zero it shall leave the sequencer in its current state and still return true, per the "sequencer remains in the current state" sentinel of TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.1.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.1 Table 6 / Figure 8 (GBB message for compound requests: request_type, cmp_start_state, cmp_next_state, cmp_sequencer, cmp_exec_delay, cmp_repetitions), TC18.txt L1221-1281; "If cmp_next_state is = 0 then the sequencer remains in the current state, when the execution is finalized.", TC18.txt L1209-1211

requirements.title: rcp_compound_tick() never advances a sequencer that has already left start_state, even after its delay elapses
requirements.text: rcp_compound_tick() shall return false and leave table unchanged when elapsed_ms >= step->exec_delay_ms but the target sequencer's current state does not equal step->start_state.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.1 Table 6 ("cmp_exec_delay: delay time between the sequencer reaching the state defined in start_state and the start of the execution of the request... execution shall happen even in case the state changes before the delay expired"), TC18.txt L1262-1265; §11.2.2.1 ("the state (cmp_next_state) the sequencer shall enter after the compound request has been executed (if the sequencer is still in cmp_start_state)"), TC18.txt L1207-1211

requirements.title: rcp_compound_wait_tick() advances the sequencer only once both condition_met and the guard hold
requirements.text: rcp_compound_wait_tick() shall set table's sequencer step->sequencer_index to step->next_state and return true iff both condition_met and rcp_compound_advance_guard(table, step) are true; otherwise it shall leave table unchanged and return false. When step->next_state is zero it shall leave the sequencer in its current state and still return true, per the same sentinel REQ-CMP-021 names (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.2).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 ("When the check finds that the condition is met the cmpw_exec_delay needs to expire before a response is generated, else the request execution is finalized without further action."), TC18.txt L1307-1309; §11.2.2.1 ("the state (cmp_next_state) the sequencer shall enter after the compound request has been executed (if the sequencer is still in cmp_start_state)"), TC18.txt L1207-1211

requirements.title: rcp_compound_wait_tick() never advances a sequencer that has already left start_state, even on a condition match
requirements.text: rcp_compound_wait_tick() shall return false and leave table unchanged when condition_met is true but the target sequencer's current state does not equal step->start_state.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 ("When the check finds that the condition is met the cmpw_exec_delay needs to expire before a response is generated, else the request execution is finalized without further action."), TC18.txt L1307-1309

requirements.title: rcp_request_type_is_triggered() recognizes RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_TRIGGERED and its safety variant
requirements.text: rcp_request_type_is_triggered() shall return true iff request_type == RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_TRIGGERED or request_type == RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_TRIGGERED_SAFETY.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 (request_type 0x0E/0x8E = Triggered), TC18.txt L1196; §11.2.2.3 ("Each endpoint may be configured to start a request upon receiving a selected trigger signal"), TC18.txt L1413

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_strerror() never returns NULL and gives every error code a distinct message
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_strerror() shall return a non-NULL string for every rcp_triggered_errc_t value, including unrecognized ones, with each defined error code mapped to a distinct message.

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_encode_request() rejects a request_type it does not recognize
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_encode_request() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data == NULL) when request_type is neither RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_TRIGGERED nor RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_TRIGGERED_SAFETY.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 Figure 10 / Table 8 (GBB message for triggered requests: request_type=0x0E/0x8E, trigger_source_ep, trigger_signal_nr, trigger_threshold, trigger_exec_delay, trigger_repetitions), TC18.txt L1414-1462

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_encode_request() packs the trigger-selection sub-fields at the specification's own offsets
requirements.text: For a recognized request_type, rcp_triggered_encode_request() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED and shall write the repurposed message_timestamp region as: request_type at octet offset 0, step->trigger_source_ep at offset 1, step->trigger_signal_nr at offset 2, step->trigger_threshold at offset 3, step->exec_delay as two big-endian octets at offsets 4-5, and step->repeat_count as two big-endian octets at offsets 6-7 (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Figure 10 / Table 8).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 Table 8 (trigger_source_ep/trigger_signal sub-field offsets), TC18.txt L1447-1461

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_decode_request() maps ACF decode failures to their rcp_triggered_errc_t equivalents
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_decode_request() shall return RCP_TRIGGERED_ERR_SHORT_FRAME or RCP_TRIGGERED_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE when rcp_acf_decode_gbb() reports the corresponding failure.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_decode_request() rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_decode_request() shall return RCP_TRIGGERED_ERR_NOT_REPURPOSED when the decoded mtv is not RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_decode_request() rejects a non-triggered opcode and otherwise recovers every sub-field
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_decode_request() shall return RCP_TRIGGERED_ERR_UNKNOWN_TYPE when the decoded opcode byte does not satisfy rcp_request_type_is_triggered(), and shall otherwise populate *out_request_type, *out_byte_bus_id, *out_transaction_num, a borrowed *out_payload/*out_payload_len view, and every rcp_triggered_step_t sub-field from the offsets and widths REQ-TRIG-004 defines.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("0x0E, 0x8E" -> "Triggered"), TC18.txt L1186-1199

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_runtime_enter_started() resets the trigger-occurrence counter
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_runtime_enter_started() shall set occurrence_count to 0 and started to true.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 26 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3292-3296

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_runtime_record_occurrence() counts only the trigger this request selected
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_runtime_record_occurrence() shall increment rt->occurrence_count and return true iff rt->started is true and the observed occurrence matches this request's own selection, i.e. source_ep == step->trigger_source_ep and signal_nr == step->trigger_signal_nr. It shall leave rt entirely unchanged and return false for an occurrence from any other endpoint or any other trigger signal number, and for any occurrence while rt->started is false (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Table 8).
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 26 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3292-3296; §11.2.2.3 Table 8 ("trigger_source_ep defines the endpoint which issues the trigger... trigger_signal_nr defines the trigger number of the endpoint addressed by trigger_source_ep"), TC18.txt L1454-1455

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_threshold_reached() counts occurrences that must precede execution
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_threshold_reached() shall return true iff rt->occurrence_count > step->trigger_threshold, so that a trigger_threshold of zero is satisfied by one occurrence and a trigger_threshold of N by N+1 occurrences, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Table 8 ("'0' results in execution after one trigger signal while a '3' will cause an execution after four occurrences").
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 Table 8 (trigger_threshold), TC18.txt L1456-1458

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_exec_delay_elapsed() compares elapsed against exec_delay
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_exec_delay_elapsed() shall return true iff elapsed >= step->exec_delay, both expressed in multiples of the addressed endpoint's configured ep_delay_time (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Table 8), not in milliseconds.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 Table 8 (trigger_exec_delay), TC18.txt L1459-1461

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_tick() only fires when started, the threshold is reached, the delay has elapsed, and the endpoint is idle
requirements.text: rcp_triggered_tick() shall return false and leave rt unchanged unless rt->started is true, rcp_triggered_threshold_reached(step, rt) holds, rcp_triggered_exec_delay_elapsed(step, elapsed) holds, and endpoint_idle is true.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 26 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3292-3296; "When the trigger_exec_delay timer has expired the state advances to RE as soon as the EP is idle and no request with higher priority is pending.", TC18.txt L3296-3298

requirements.title: rcp_triggered_tick() resets the runtime on a successful fire and advances no sequencer
requirements.text: When every condition REQ-TRIG-012 names holds, rcp_triggered_tick() shall reset rt->occurrence_count to 0 and rt->started to false and return true. It shall not read or write any sequencer state: a triggered request carries no sequencer, start_state, or next_state sub-field (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Table 8).
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 26 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3292-3296; TC18.txt L3296-3298 (trigger_exec_delay expiry + EP-idle gating)

requirements.title: rcp_chained_strerror() never returns NULL and gives every error code a distinct message
requirements.text: rcp_chained_strerror() shall return a non-NULL string for every rcp_chained_errc_t value, including unrecognized ones, with each defined error code mapped to a distinct message.

requirements.title: rcp_chained_encode_member() leaves every reserved sub-field octet zero
requirements.text: rcp_chained_encode_member() shall write octets 1-3 and 6-7 of the repurposed message_timestamp region as all-zero, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 Table 9 ("All bits shall be written as 0, else the request will be rejected"). It shall not encode any chain_length or chain_position sub-field: the specification defines neither, and a member's position in a chain is its position among the enclosing AVTPDU's requests.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 Table 9 (chained request reserved fields), TC18.txt L1548-1552

requirements.title: rcp_chained_encode_member() rejects an oversized payload
requirements.text: rcp_chained_encode_member() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data == NULL) when payload_len exceeds RCP_ACF_MAX_PAYLOAD or on allocation failure.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 Figure 11 / field table (GBB for chained requests: request_type=0x01, reserved octets, chain_exec_delay, cs), TC18.txt L1503-1560; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: rcp_chained_encode_member() packs chain_exec_delay and cs at the specification's own positions
requirements.text: For valid inputs, rcp_chained_encode_member() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED, the opcode byte RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_CHAINED at octet offset 0 of the repurposed message_timestamp region, chain_exec_delay as two big-endian octets at offsets 4-5, and cs encoded into byte_message_info's own cs bit (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 Figure 11 / Table 9).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 Table 9 (chain_exec_delay, cs semantics), TC18.txt L1548-1560

requirements.title: rcp_chained_decode_member() maps ACF decode failures to their rcp_chained_errc_t equivalents
requirements.text: rcp_chained_decode_member() shall return RCP_CHAINED_ERR_SHORT_FRAME or RCP_CHAINED_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE when rcp_acf_decode_gbb() reports the corresponding failure.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: rcp_chained_decode_member() rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp_chained_decode_member() shall return RCP_CHAINED_ERR_NOT_REPURPOSED when the decoded mtv is not RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189

requirements.title: rcp_chained_decode_member() rejects a non-chained opcode and otherwise recovers chain_exec_delay and cs
requirements.text: rcp_chained_decode_member() shall return RCP_CHAINED_ERR_UNKNOWN_TYPE when the decoded opcode byte is not RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_CHAINED, and shall otherwise populate *out_byte_bus_id, *out_chain_exec_delay (from offsets 4-5), *out_cs, *out_transaction_num, and a borrowed *out_payload/*out_payload_len view.

requirements.title: rcp_chained_advance() reports CHAIN_ERROR for a chained member with no predecessor
requirements.text: rcp_chained_advance() shall return RCP_CHAINED_MEMBER_CHAIN_ERROR and set *chain_aborted to true whenever has_predecessor is false, so that a chained request appearing as the enclosing AVTPDU's first request, and every member after it, is ignored -- per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 ("If the first request in an AVTPDU is a chain request, then there is no predecessor to chain to, thus the entire chain will be ignored").
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 ("If the first request in an AVTPDU is a chain request, then there is no predecessor to chain to, thus the entire chain will be ignored. An error response with the error code 'CHAIN_ERROR' to each request will be generated"), TC18.txt L1518-1521

requirements.title: rcp_chained_advance() reports CHAIN_ABORTED once the chain has been aborted
requirements.text: rcp_chained_advance() shall return RCP_CHAINED_MEMBER_CHAIN_ABORTED, without consulting predecessor_errored or cs and leaving *chain_aborted true, whenever has_predecessor is true and *chain_aborted is already true on entry.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 ("cs ... 1b: request will not be executed in case the previous request returned an error, as a consequence the remainder of the chain is not executed, and the request send an error response with error code = CHAIN_ABORTED"), TC18.txt L1555-1560

requirements.title: rcp_chained_advance() reads cs off the member about to run, about its predecessor's outcome
requirements.text: When has_predecessor is true and *chain_aborted is false on entry, rcp_chained_advance() shall return RCP_CHAINED_MEMBER_CHAIN_ABORTED and set *chain_aborted to true iff predecessor_errored is true AND cs == RCP_CHAINED_CS_ABORT_ON_ERROR, and shall otherwise return RCP_CHAINED_MEMBER_OK leaving *chain_aborted false -- including when predecessor_errored is true but cs == RCP_CHAINED_CS_CONTINUE_ON_ERROR. cs is the conditional-start selector of the member about to execute, not of the member that errored (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 Table 9).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 Table 9 (cs conditional-start semantics), TC18.txt L1555-1560

requirements.title: rcp_timed_strerror() never returns NULL and gives every error code a distinct message
requirements.text: rcp_timed_strerror() shall return a non-NULL string for every rcp_timed_errc_t value, including unrecognized ones, with each defined error code mapped to a distinct message.

requirements.title: rcp_timed_feature_enabled() requires both time-sync option bits set
requirements.text: rcp_timed_feature_enabled() shall return true iff both RCP_REGMAP_OPT_TIME_SYNC_TSCF and RCP_REGMAP_OPT_TIME_SYNC_PRESENTATION are set in options.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 ("requests can be sent under TSCF header, where an avtp_timestamp is included... A second option is to convey the presentation time in the message_timestamp field of an ACF_GBB."), TC18.txt L1589-1592; conformance bullets "Implementation of gPTP (IEEE802.1as)" / "Support of timed request", TC18.txt L2024-2025

requirements.title: rcp_timed_encode_request() packs a 48-bit presentation_time and holds the reserved octet at zero
requirements.text: rcp_timed_encode_request() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED, hs and cs clear, the opcode byte RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_TIMED at octet offset 0 of the repurposed message_timestamp region, an all-zero reserved octet at offset 1, and presentation_time as six big-endian octets spanning offsets 2-7 (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.5 Figure 12 / Table 10). It shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data == NULL), never a truncated frame, when presentation_time exceeds RCP_TIMED_PRESENTATION_TIME_MAX.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Figure 12 (48-bit presentation_time offset), TC18.txt L1593-1604

requirements.title: rcp_timed_decode_request() maps ACF decode failures and rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp_timed_decode_request() shall return RCP_TIMED_ERR_SHORT_FRAME or RCP_TIMED_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE when rcp_acf_decode_gbb() reports the corresponding failure, and RCP_TIMED_ERR_NOT_REPURPOSED when the decoded mtv is not RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: rcp_timed_decode_request() rejects a non-timed opcode and otherwise recovers the 48-bit presentation_time
requirements.text: rcp_timed_decode_request() shall return RCP_TIMED_ERR_UNKNOWN_TYPE when the decoded opcode byte is not RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_TIMED, and shall otherwise populate *out_byte_bus_id, *out_transaction_num, a borrowed *out_payload/*out_payload_len view, and *out_presentation_time from the six octets at offsets 2-7 of the repurposed region, in [0, RCP_TIMED_PRESENTATION_TIME_MAX].

requirements.title: rcp_timed_too_far() is wraparound-safe in the 48-bit presentation-time domain
requirements.text: rcp_timed_too_far() shall compute presentation_time - now modulo RCP_TIMED_PRESENTATION_TIME_MODULUS, shall return false whenever that difference exceeds half the modulus (i.e. presentation_time is at or before now), and shall otherwise return true iff the difference exceeds max_horizon.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 ("The RC Server may reject the request, when the presentation_time is too far in the future, which is implementation dependent (error code = PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR)."), TC18.txt L1649-1650

requirements.title: rcp_timed_admit() reports RCP_TIMED_REJECT_GPTP_FAIL whenever gptp_locked is false
requirements.text: rcp_timed_admit() shall return RCP_TIMED_REJECT_GPTP_FAIL whenever gptp_locked is false, regardless of presentation_time, now, or max_horizon (all 64-bit, in the 48-bit gPTP domain).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 ("In case the time synchronization hasn't been established, timed requests (either in the format shown here or under TSCF header) shall be rejected and an error response shall be sent (error code = GPTP_FAIL)."), TC18.txt L1651-1653

requirements.title: rcp_timed_admit() reports RCP_TIMED_REJECT_PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR or RCP_TIMED_ACCEPT when gPTP is locked
requirements.text: rcp_timed_admit() shall return RCP_TIMED_REJECT_PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR when gptp_locked is true and rcp_timed_too_far(presentation_time, now, max_horizon) holds, and RCP_TIMED_ACCEPT otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 ("The RC Server may reject the request, when the presentation_time is too far in the future"), TC18.txt L1649

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_strerror() never returns NULL and gives every error code a distinct message
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_strerror() shall return a non-NULL string for every rcp_cancel_errc_t value, including unrecognized ones, with each defined error code mapped to a distinct message.

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_encode_clear_all() encodes a zero-payload clear-all request
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_encode_clear_all() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED, the opcode byte set to RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_CLEAR_ALL, and the remaining repurposed sub-field bytes zeroed.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Figure 13 + Table 11 (clear-all, request_type 0x05), TC18.txt L1682-1710

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_all() maps ACF decode failures and rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_all() shall return RCP_CANCEL_ERR_SHORT_FRAME or RCP_CANCEL_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE when rcp_acf_decode_gbb() reports the corresponding failure, and RCP_CANCEL_ERR_NOT_REPURPOSED when the decoded mtv is not RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Figure 13 / Table 11 (Usage of GBB message to cancel all requests, request_type=0x05), TC18.txt L1681-1719; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis and §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_all() rejects an opcode byte that is not RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_CLEAR_ALL
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_all() shall return RCP_CANCEL_ERR_UNKNOWN_TYPE when the decoded opcode byte is not RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_CLEAR_ALL, and shall otherwise populate *out_byte_bus_id and *out_transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Table 11 (clear-all, request_type 0x05), TC18.txt L1704-1710

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_encode_clear_single() packs clear_transaction_num at the specification's own offset
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_encode_clear_single() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED, the opcode byte RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_CLEAR_SINGLE at octet offset 0 of the repurposed message_timestamp region, clear_transaction_num at octet offset 3, and octets 1-2 and 4-7 all-zero (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.3.3 Figure 15 / Table 13).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 Figure 15 (clear-single, clear_transaction_num offset), TC18.txt L1797-1810

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_single() maps ACF decode failures and rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_single() shall return RCP_CANCEL_ERR_SHORT_FRAME or RCP_CANCEL_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE when rcp_acf_decode_gbb() reports the corresponding failure, and RCP_CANCEL_ERR_NOT_REPURPOSED when the decoded mtv is not RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 Figure 15 / Table 13 (Usage of GBB message to cancel a single, specific request, request_type=0x07, clear_transaction_num), TC18.txt L1794-1835; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis and §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1186-1189

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_single() recovers clear_transaction_num from the specification's own offset
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_single() shall return RCP_CANCEL_ERR_UNKNOWN_TYPE when the decoded opcode byte is not RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_CLEAR_SINGLE, RCP_CANCEL_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO when any of octets 1-2 or 4-7 of the repurposed region carries a set bit, and shall otherwise populate *out_byte_bus_id, *out_transaction_num, and *out_clear_transaction_num from octet offset 3.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 Table 13 (clear-single, clear_transaction_num), TC18.txt L1819-1821

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_is_cancellable() is true only for RCP_CANCEL_LIFECYCLE_QUEUED
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_is_cancellable() shall return true iff state == RCP_CANCEL_LIFECYCLE_QUEUED, and false for RCP_CANCEL_LIFECYCLE_EXECUTING or RCP_CANCEL_LIFECYCLE_DONE.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("A request can be cancelled while it is pending and after it has been started until it is under execution. Requests under execution will not be aborted."), TC18.txt L1673-1675

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_attempt() reports RCP_CANCEL_RESULT_NOT_FOUND when the target was not found
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_attempt() shall return RCP_CANCEL_RESULT_NOT_FOUND whenever found is false, regardless of state.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 ("The request initiating the cancellation will create an error response with the error code = REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, when the clear_transaction_num was not found."), TC18.txt L1836-1837

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_attempt() reports RCP_CANCEL_RESULT_NOT_CANCELLABLE for a found request outside the cancellable window
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_attempt() shall return RCP_CANCEL_RESULT_NOT_CANCELLABLE whenever found is true and !rcp_cancel_is_cancellable(state).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("A request can be cancelled while it is pending and after it has been started until it is under execution. Requests under execution will not be aborted."), TC18.txt L1673-1675

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_attempt() reports RCP_CANCEL_RESULT_CANCELED for a found, cancellable request
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_attempt() shall return RCP_CANCEL_RESULT_CANCELED whenever found is true and rcp_cancel_is_cancellable(state).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("A request can be cancelled while it is pending and after it has been started until it is under execution. Requests under execution will not be aborted."), TC18.txt L1673-1675; §11.2.3.3 ("The request initiating the cancellation will create an error response with the error code = REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, when the clear_transaction_num was not found."), TC18.txt L1836-1837

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_chain_should_cascade() cascades to a chain member's own position and every position after it
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_chain_should_cascade() shall return true iff member_position >= canceled_position. PARTIAL as of 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): the function itself is correct and directly unit-tested, but no real dispatch path calls it -- src/mock.c's apply_cancellation() cancels only the single targeted transaction on a clear-single (0x07) request; it never checks whether other queued requests are chained to the one being cancelled, so TC18's own cascade rule (quoted below) is not actually enforced by this server's reference implementation. Wiring this correctly needs real chain-position tracking across the request queue (which member is chained to which, and each member's own position), a larger feature than this requirement's own narrow scope -- tracked here as a known gap rather than silently claimed complete.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("If a request is cancelled to which a request is chained, then the chained successors shall be cancelled by the RC Server as well."), TC18.txt L1674-1675

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_all() rejects a nonzero reserved message_timestamp octet
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_all() shall return RCP_CANCEL_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO when any of message_timestamp's 7 trailing octets (every octet after the leading request_type byte) carries a set bit, since clear-all carries no sub-field of its own. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): the decode function previously read only the leading request_type byte and never validated the remaining 7 octets TC18 Table 11 marks reserved.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Table 11 ("reserved: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected"), TC18.txt L1704-1710

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_all() rejects nonzero evt[2:0], hs, or cs
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_all() shall return RCP_CANCEL_ERR_EVT_HS_CS_NONZERO when the decoded ACF byte_message_info header's evt[2:0], hs, or cs is nonzero -- TC18 Table 11 defines only evt = 0000b (no ack) or 1000b (ack requested) as valid, meaning evt[2:0] must be zero, and both hs and cs are documented as always 0b. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): this ACF-header-level field was entirely unvalidated by any of the three cancel-family decode functions before this milestone.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Table 11 (evt/hs/cs field descriptions), TC18.txt L1704-1710

requirements.title: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_single() rejects nonzero evt[2:0], hs, or cs
requirements.text: rcp_cancel_decode_clear_single() shall return RCP_CANCEL_ERR_EVT_HS_CS_NONZERO when the decoded ACF byte_message_info header's evt[2:0], hs, or cs is nonzero, per TC18 Table 13's explicit prose ("Evt, hs and cs shall be zero") -- the same rule as REQ-CANCEL-014's clear-all case, applied to clear-single. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H). Distinct from REQ-CANCEL-007's own RCP_CANCEL_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO check, which validates message_timestamp's own reserved octets, a different wire region from the ACF header's evt/hs/cs bits.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 ("Evt, hs and cs shall be zero"), Table 13, TC18.txt L1795-1821

requirements.title: rcp_sched_classify() classifies every repurposed opcode this project's request-kind modules define
requirements.text: rcp_sched_classify() shall return RCP_SCHED_KIND_STANDARD whenever is_repurposed is false, and shall otherwise classify request_type into RCP_SCHED_KIND_CANCELLATION (clear-all/clear-non-safestate/clear-single), RCP_SCHED_KIND_TRIGGERED, RCP_SCHED_KIND_TIMED, RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND, RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND_WAIT, RCP_SCHED_KIND_CHAINED, or RCP_SCHED_KIND_STANDARD for any opcode not recognized by those modules.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("In case two or more requests are due for execution then the priorities are as follows: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard"), TC18.txt L3248-3266; request_type identifiers per §11.2.2 Table 5, TC18.txt L1186-1199

requirements.title: rcp_sched_kind_rank() encodes the cancellation > triggered > timed > compound > compound-wait > chained > standard ordering
requirements.text: rcp_sched_kind_rank() shall return a strictly higher value for RCP_SCHED_KIND_CANCELLATION than RCP_SCHED_KIND_TRIGGERED, for RCP_SCHED_KIND_TRIGGERED than RCP_SCHED_KIND_TIMED, for RCP_SCHED_KIND_TIMED than RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND, for RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND than RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND_WAIT, for RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND_WAIT than RCP_SCHED_KIND_CHAINED, and for RCP_SCHED_KIND_CHAINED than RCP_SCHED_KIND_STANDARD.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("In case two or more requests are due for execution then the priorities are as follows: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard"), TC18.txt L3248-3266

requirements.title: rcp_sched_compare() orders by rank first and FIFO sequence second
requirements.text: rcp_sched_compare() shall return a negative value when a's rank exceeds b's rank (regardless of sequence), a positive value when b's rank exceeds a's, and among equal ranks shall return negative iff a->sequence < b->sequence, positive iff a->sequence > b->sequence, and zero only when both kind and sequence are equal.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("In case two or more requests are due for execution then the priorities are as follows: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard"), TC18.txt L3248-3266; §12.9.2 ("When two or more requests with the same priority are due then starting the execution shall happen in the order with which the requests arrived in the EP request storage."), TC18.txt L3265-3266

requirements.title: rcp_sched_split_frame_members() reports every member's byte offset in an ACF payload stream
requirements.text: For a well-formed ACF payload stream (every member's declared acf_msg_type/acf_msg_length correctly delimiting a header-plus-payload region that fits within the stream), rcp_sched_split_frame_members() shall return the number of members found and write each member's starting byte offset, in order, into out_offsets (up to out_cap entries).
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("An RCP frame may include multiple ACF-types (requests). An RC Server shall support to handle multiple requests in one frame and check each of them individually if to be processed or not"), TC18.txt L3220-3224; request_type identifiers per §11.2.2 Table 5, TC18.txt L1186-1199; ACF message length is a quadlet count per §11.2.1 Table 4, established ACF basis

requirements.title: rcp_sched_split_frame_members() returns 0 on a malformed stream
requirements.text: rcp_sched_split_frame_members() shall return 0 when the first byte is neither RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB nor RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB, or when any member's own declared header-plus-payload length would run past len, without writing a partial member to out_offsets.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("An RCP frame may include multiple ACF-types (requests). An RC Server shall support to handle multiple requests in one frame and check each of them individually if to be processed or not"), TC18.txt L3220-3224; request_type identifiers per §11.2.2 Table 5, TC18.txt L1186-1199

requirements.title: rcp_sched_split_frame_members() returns 0 for an empty stream
requirements.text: rcp_sched_split_frame_members() shall return 0 when len == 0.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("An RCP frame may include multiple ACF-types (requests). An RC Server shall support to handle multiple requests in one frame and check each of them individually if to be processed or not"), TC18.txt L3220-3224; request_type identifiers per §11.2.2 Table 5, TC18.txt L1186-1199

requirements.title: rcp_sched_frame_timing_consistent() is trivially true for NTSCF frames and empty member lists
requirements.text: rcp_sched_frame_timing_consistent() shall return true whenever is_tscf is false, and shall return true whenever count == 0, regardless of member_is_timed's contents.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("As the AVTPDU has either a TSCF or NTSCF header a mixture of requests with and without presentation time in a single frame is not possible. A presentation time from a TSCF header will be applied to all ACFtypes within the frame."), TC18.txt L3224-3226

requirements.title: rcp_sched_frame_timing_consistent() rejects a TSCF frame mixing timed and untimed members
requirements.text: For is_tscf == true and count > 0, rcp_sched_frame_timing_consistent() shall return true iff every entry in member_is_timed[0..count) equals member_is_timed[0], and false otherwise.
