requirements.text: rcp_fragment_plan() shall return RCP_FRAGMENT_ERR_DISABLED or RCP_FRAGMENT_ERR_TOO_MANY_SEGMENTS under the same conditions rcp_fragment_plan_count() returns 0 for, and shall return RCP_FRAGMENT_ERR_BAD_SEGMENT_COUNT when segment_count does not match rcp_fragment_plan_count()'s answer for the same payload_len/max_fragment_payload.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reasm_result_string() never returns NULL and gives every result value a distinct message
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reasm_result_string() shall return a non-NULL string for every rcp_fragment_reasm_result_t value, including unrecognized ones, with each defined value mapped to a distinct message.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_init() initializes a reassembler to the empty, not-collecting state
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_init() shall leave the reassembler not collecting, with an empty reassembled buffer, and with max_total_len set to the caller-supplied value.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_reset() discards in-progress state while preserving max_total_len
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_reset() shall discard any in-progress reassembly and any previously reassembled payload, leaving the reassembler in the same state rcp_fragment_reassembler_init() would with the same max_total_len it already had.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_destroy() releases the reassembler's internal storage
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_destroy() shall free the reassembler's internal buffer and leave it in a state that does not leak memory when the reassembler is discarded.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() completes immediately for a never-fragmented (ms=false) first fragment
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() shall, when fed a single ms=false fragment on a freshly-initialized-or-reset reassembler, return RCP_FRAGMENT_REASM_COMPLETE with that fragment's payload as the reassembled result, without entering the collecting state.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() requires the first ms=true fragment of a sequence to carry segment_num 0
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() shall return RCP_FRAGMENT_REASM_ERR_OUT_OF_ORDER, without appending the fragment, when the first ms=true fragment fed to a freshly-initialized-or-reset reassembler carries a segment_num other than 0.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() requires each subsequent ms=true fragment's segment_num to be exactly one more than the previous
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() shall return RCP_FRAGMENT_REASM_ERR_OUT_OF_ORDER, without appending the fragment and without disturbing already-collected state, when an ms=true fragment's segment_num is not exactly one more than the previously accepted fragment's segment_num.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() completes a sequence on any ms=false fragment regardless of its own segment_num field value
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() shall return RCP_FRAGMENT_REASM_COMPLETE and append the fragment's payload when fed an ms=false fragment while collecting, without validating or consulting that fragment's segment_num argument.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() rejects a fragment that would exceed max_total_len without mutating state
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() shall return RCP_FRAGMENT_REASM_ERR_TOO_LARGE, leaving the reassembler's already-collected state unchanged, when appending the fed fragment's payload would cause the reassembled total to exceed max_total_len.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() reports an allocation failure distinctly from every other failure mode
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() shall return RCP_FRAGMENT_REASM_ERR_ALLOC, leaving the reassembler's already-collected state unchanged, when its internal buffer growth fails, and this value shall be distinct from every other rcp_fragment_reasm_result_t value.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_is_collecting() reports whether a fragment sequence is currently in progress
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_is_collecting() shall return true iff the reassembler has accepted at least one ms=true fragment since the last completed reassembly or reset, and false otherwise, without mutating the reassembler.

requirements.title: rcp_fragment_reassembler_get() returns the reassembled payload and its length after a completed reassembly
requirements.text: rcp_fragment_reassembler_get(), called immediately after rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed() has returned RCP_FRAGMENT_REASM_COMPLETE, shall report a payload pointer and length equal to the concatenation, in segment_num order, of every fragment's payload accepted for that sequence.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_frame_response_fragment_count() reports 0 under the same preconditions the unfragmented response encoder fails for, and delegates the fragment count to fragment.h otherwise
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_frame_response_fragment_count() shall return 0 when frame_format/arbitration_id/xl_header/rx_len fail the same preconditions rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_response() validates, and shall otherwise return rcp_fragment_plan_count()'s answer for the combined prefix-then-data payload length and max_fragment_payload.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("...which requires segmentation, which is supported by the fields 'ms' and 'segment_num'."), TC18.txt L5443-5446

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_response_fragmented() splits a CAN frame response's combined payload into correctly-numbered ACF fragments
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_response_fragmented() shall encode rcp_ep_can_frame_response_fragment_count() ACF frames whose ms/read_size_or_segment_num fields follow fragment.h's rcp_fragment_plan() and whose byte_bus_id/evt/op/transaction_num/timed/timestamp match rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_response()'s own single-frame encoding, producing exactly one frame identical to that single-frame encoding when the combined payload already fits in one fragment.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("...which requires segmentation, which is supported by the fields 'ms' and 'segment_num'."), TC18.txt L5443-5446

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response_fragment() surfaces a fragment's ms bit, segment_num, and raw ACF payload without stripping this module's own prefix
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response_fragment() shall, on RCP_EP_CAN_OK, populate out_ms and out_segment_num from the decoded ACF header's ms and read_size_or_segment_num fields and out_payload/out_payload_len as a borrowed view of the full, unstripped ACF payload.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("...which requires segmentation, which is supported by the fields 'ms' and 'segment_num'."), TC18.txt L5443-5446; §13.7.11.3 Figure 39, TC18.txt L5426-5446

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response_fragment() validates byte_bus_id, message type, and evt the same way the unfragmented response decoder does
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response_fragment() shall return the same RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_SHORT_FRAME/_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE/_ERR_WRONG_BUS/_ERR_BAD_EVT error codes, under the same conditions, that rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response() returns them for. It does NOT validate or output frame_format: frame_format lives in the combined payload's own leading quadlet (TC18 §13.7.11.3 Figure 39), not per-fragment header state, so it is only recoverable after reassembly -- see REQ-CANEP-027. FIXED (v0.109.0): this function previously validated and output frame_format derived from evt[2:0], the same non-conformant design corrected across this module.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_decode_reassembled_frame_response() parses a fully reassembled combined payload into frame_format/arbitration_id/xl_header/rx_data
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_decode_reassembled_frame_response() shall, given a reassembled buffer of at least 4 bytes, read frame_format from its leading quadlet's top 3 bits (TC18 §13.7.11.3 Figure 39), returning RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_SHORT_FRAME if the buffer is shorter than that format's own full prefix length, RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_FRAME_FORMAT if it is not rcp_ep_can_frame_format_valid(), or RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_ARBITRATION_ID if the leading quadlet's low 29 bits are not rcp_ep_can_arbitration_id_valid() for that format; otherwise populate out_frame_format, out_arbitration_id, out_xl_header (only when the format is a CAN XL variant), and out_rx_data/out_rx_len identically to how rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response() would have for the same original, unfragmented payload. FIXED (v0.109.0): frame_format was previously a caller-supplied input (sourced from a per-fragment evt[2:0], REQ-CANEP-026's now-corrected design); it is now derived from the reassembled payload itself, the only place it is actually carried.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_read_response_fragment_count() delegates its answer to fragment.h's rcp_fragment_plan_count()
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_read_response_fragment_count() shall return rcp_fragment_plan_count(rx_len, max_fragment_payload)'s answer for every input.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("...the response is fragmented. To support fragmentation properly it is essential that the uart_rx_fifo_size is chosen such that it is slightly bigger than the maximum byte_msg_payload to be generated within a single AVTPDU..."), TC18.txt L4886-4889

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_response_fragmented() splits a UART read response's payload into correctly-numbered ACF fragments
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_response_fragmented() shall encode rcp_ep_uart_read_response_fragment_count() ACF frames whose ms/read_size_or_segment_num fields follow fragment.h's rcp_fragment_plan() and whose byte_bus_id/op/transaction_num/timed/timestamp match rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_response()'s own single-frame encoding, producing exactly one frame identical to that single-frame encoding when rx_len already fits in one fragment.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("...the response is fragmented."), TC18.txt L4886

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_response_fragment() surfaces a fragment's ms bit, segment_num, and raw payload, validated the same way the unfragmented response decoder is
requirements.text: rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_response_fragment() shall, on RCP_EP_UART_OK, populate out_ms and out_segment_num from the decoded ACF header's ms and read_size_or_segment_num fields and out_payload/out_payload_len as a borrowed view of the ACF payload, and shall return the same RCP_EP_UART_ERR_SHORT_FRAME/_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE/_ERR_WRONG_BUS error codes, under the same conditions, that rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_response() returns them for.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30 (ADC/PWM_IN/I²C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO row), TC18.txt L3684-3693

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_response_fragment_count() delegates its answer to fragment.h's rcp_fragment_plan_count()
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_response_fragment_count() shall return rcp_fragment_plan_count((size_t)read_size, max_fragment_payload)'s answer for every input.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 Table 17 ("Acf_msg_length: ≤ read_size of discovery request, limited to max size of register map"), TC18.txt L2422-2423

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_encode_response_fragmented() splits the discovery general-register-slice payload into correctly-numbered NTSCF-framed ACF fragments
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_encode_response_fragmented() shall encode rcp_discovery_response_fragment_count() full NTSCF-framed ACF_ABB frames whose ms/read_size_or_segment_num fields follow fragment.h's rcp_fragment_plan() (the final fragment carrying read_size itself) and whose byte_bus_id/op/transaction_num/server_stream_id match rcp_discovery_encode_response()'s own single-frame encoding, producing exactly one frame identical to that single-frame encoding when read_size already fits in one fragment.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 Table 17 ("Acf_msg_length: ≤ read_size of discovery request, limited to max size of register map"), TC18.txt L2422-2423

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_decode_response_fragment() surfaces a fragment's ms bit, segment_num, server_stream_id, and raw payload, validated the same way the unfragmented response decoder is
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_decode_response_fragment() shall, on RCP_DISCOVERY_OK, populate out_server_stream_id, out_ms, and out_segment_num from the decoded frame, and out_payload/out_payload_len as a borrowed view of the ACF payload, applying the same AVTP/ACF-level validation rcp_discovery_decode_response() applies.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 Table 17 ("Discovery response": subtype=NTSCF, acf_msg_type=ACF_ABB, Byte_bus_id=00000000000b, op=1b/read, byte_msg_payload=RC Server's register map content starting from address 0x00000), TC18.txt L2402-2427

requirements.title: rcp_discovery_decode_reassembled_response() parses a fully reassembled general-register-slice payload into a discovery result
requirements.text: rcp_discovery_decode_reassembled_response() shall, given a reassembled buffer of at least RCP_DISCOVERY_GENERAL_SLICE_LEN octets, populate out_result identically to how rcp_discovery_decode_response() would have for the same original, unfragmented response payload, and shall return RCP_DISCOVERY_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a shorter buffer.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.2 Table 17 ("Discovery response": subtype=NTSCF, acf_msg_type=ACF_ABB, Byte_bus_id=00000000000b, op=1b/read, byte_msg_payload=RC Server's register map content starting from address 0x00000), TC18.txt L2402-2427

requirements.title: rcp_mock_strerror() never returns NULL
requirements.text: rcp_mock_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, human-readable string for every rcp_mock_errc_t value, including one outside the defined enum.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_new() starts HW_UNCONFIGURED with an initialized, empty register map
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_new() shall return a server whose rcp_mock_server_state() is RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED and whose rcp_mock_server_regmap() has been initialized via rcp_regmap_general_init() (svr_ep_count 0, svr_root_client_index RCP_REGMAP_NO_ROOT_CLIENT), with no endpoints registered.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_destroy() frees every endpoint's queued requests and is NULL-safe
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_destroy() shall free every registered endpoint's queued (undelivered) requests and srv itself, and shall be a no-op when srv is NULL.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_state() reports the server's current lifecycle state
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_state() shall return srv's own current rcp_lifecycle_state_t, reflecting the most recent successful rcp_mock_server_transition().

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_transition() is a thin passthrough to rcp_lifecycle_transition()
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_transition() shall apply lifecycle.h's own rcp_lifecycle_transition() rules to srv's own state, leaving srv's state unchanged and returning the same error code rcp_lifecycle_transition() would for a rejected transition.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_regmap() exposes srv's own register map for direct mutation
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_regmap() shall return a non-NULL pointer to srv's own rcp_regmap_general_t, valid for srv's lifetime, through which a caller may freely read and write every field.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_add_endpoint() registers a new endpoint slot and updates svr_ep_count
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_add_endpoint() shall, on success, add a slot addressed at byte_bus_id with generic config ep_type/ep_used=true and a queue starting at the given ep_enable, and shall update rcp_mock_server_regmap()'s own svr_ep_count to the new total registered-endpoint count.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_add_endpoint() rejects a duplicate byte_bus_id or a full endpoint table
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_add_endpoint() shall return RCP_MOCK_ERR_DUPLICATE_BUS_ID, without adding a slot, when byte_bus_id is already registered, and RCP_MOCK_ERR_CAPACITY when srv already holds RCP_MOCK_MAX_ENDPOINTS endpoints.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_remove_endpoint() removes a registered slot and updates svr_ep_count, or reports not-found
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_remove_endpoint() shall, for a registered byte_bus_id, free its queued requests, remove its slot, decrement svr_ep_count, and return true; for an unregistered byte_bus_id it shall leave srv unchanged and return false.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_set_endpoint_enable() sets a registered endpoint's ep_enable, or reports not-found
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_set_endpoint_enable() shall set the ep_enable flag of the endpoint at a registered byte_bus_id and return true, or return false without effect for an unregistered byte_bus_id.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_endpoint_queue_len() returns a registered endpoint's queue length, or 0
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_endpoint_queue_len() shall return the number of requests currently queued on the endpoint at a registered byte_bus_id, or 0 for an unregistered byte_bus_id.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() consults rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() before anything else
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() shall call lifecycle.h's rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() with srv's own state and the given time_sync_supported/avtp_subtype/acf_msg_type/byte_bus_id, and shall return RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_DROPPED with *out_response left zeroed whenever it returns false, without consulting any endpoint slot.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() reports an unregistered byte_bus_id once admission succeeds
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() shall return RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_ERR_UNKNOWN_BUS, with *out_response left zeroed, when rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() accepts the frame but byte_bus_id names no registered endpoint.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() runs the endpoint's handler immediately when its queue is enabled
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() shall, for a registered and ep_enable=true endpoint, invoke its registered rcp_mock_endpoint_handler_fn synchronously with the given request/request_len and that endpoint's own user_data, populate *out_response from it, and return RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_OK.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() queues the request without running the handler when the endpoint is disabled
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() shall, for a registered and ep_enable=false endpoint, append the request to that endpoint's queue without invoking its handler, leave *out_response zeroed, and return RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_QUEUED.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_drain_endpoint() runs the oldest queued request's handler once re-enabled
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_drain_endpoint() shall, for a registered endpoint with ep_enable=true and a non-empty queue, dequeue its oldest request, invoke its registered handler with that request, populate *out_response from it, and return true.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_drain_endpoint() reports nothing to drain without invoking the handler
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_drain_endpoint() shall return false, with *out_response left zeroed and without invoking any handler, when the addressed endpoint's queue is empty or its ep_enable is false.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_drain_endpoint() reports an unregistered byte_bus_id
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_drain_endpoint() shall return false, with *out_response left zeroed, when byte_bus_id names no registered endpoint.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() splits and dispatches every member of a multi-request frame
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() shall split frame into its constituent ACF messages (scheduler.h rcp_sched_split_frame_members()) and dispatch each one individually via rcp_mock_server_dispatch(), addressed to its own decoded byte_bus_id, writing each member's outcome into out_results in frame order and returning the count dispatched.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("An RCP frame may include multiple ACF-types (requests)"), TC18.txt L3220

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() fails safe on an unparseable frame or an undecodable member
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() shall return 0 without dispatching anything when frame does not parse as a well-formed sequence of ACF messages, and shall report RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_ERR_UNKNOWN_BUS for any individual member whose byte_message_info header fails to decode, without invoking any handler for that member.

requirements.title: parse_json parses the optional server object plus zero or more entry-list sections
requirements.text: rcp_config_parse_json() shall populate out->server from an optional top-level server object's vendor_id/device_id/magic/svr_implemented_options fields, and shall parse an arbitrary number of hw_pin_map/endpoints/streams entries (each recognized by its own required key) from anywhere in the document, succeeding (RCP_OK) for an empty object.

requirements.title: apply_to_mock sets the mock server's regmap general fields from the manifest
requirements.text: rcp_config_apply_to_mock() shall set srv's own rcp_mock_server_regmap() vendor_id/device_id fields, OR its svr_implemented_options field, from m->server, leaving magic unchanged when m->server.magic is 0.

requirements.title: apply_to_mock registers one mock endpoint per manifest endpoint entry
requirements.text: rcp_config_apply_to_mock() shall call rcp_mock_server_add_endpoint() once per m->endpoints entry (byte_bus_id/ep_type/ep_enable, handler NULL) and shall return the first non-RCP_MOCK_OK result encountered without registering any later entry.

requirements.title: load() parses then applies a manifest document in one call
requirements.text: rcp_config_load() shall parse json with rcp_config_parse_json() and, on success, apply the result to srv with rcp_config_apply_to_mock(), returning RCP_CFG_ERR_PARSE (with err_msg filled) for a parse failure or the apply step's own rcp_mock_errc_t (cast to int) otherwise.

requirements.title: rcp_bytes_dup() heap-copies a byte buffer
requirements.text: rcp_bytes_dup() shall heap-allocate a copy of the given [data, data+len) range and return an rcp_bytes_t referencing the copy. It shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data=NULL, len=0) when len==0 or when allocation fails, rather than a partially-initialized result.

requirements.title: rcp_bytes_free() releases and zeroes a byte buffer
requirements.text: rcp_bytes_free() shall free the buffer referenced by an rcp_bytes_t (if any) and zero the struct's data/len fields, and shall be safe to call on an already-zeroed or NULL rcp_bytes_t pointer.

requirements.title: Mutex/condvar primitives provide mutual exclusion and signaling
requirements.text: rcp_mutex_init/lock/unlock/destroy() and rcp_cond_init/wait/timedwait_until/signal/broadcast/destroy() shall provide standard mutual-exclusion and condition-variable signaling semantics on every supported platform (POSIX pthreads and Win32), used by every module that needs cross-thread synchronization.

requirements.title: rcp_thread_start()/rcp_thread_start_detached() launch a new thread
requirements.text: rcp_thread_start() and rcp_thread_start_detached() shall start a new OS thread running the given function with the given argument, on every supported platform, with rcp_thread_start_detached() releasing any OS resources needed to join it later since the caller will never join it.

requirements.title: rcp_monotonic_ms() returns a monotonically non-decreasing clock reading
requirements.text: rcp_monotonic_ms() shall return a millisecond-resolution timestamp from a monotonic clock source (unaffected by wall-clock adjustments) on every supported platform, used codebase-wide for deadline/timeout computation.

requirements.title: rcp_wire_error_t assigns the governing spec's own numbered wire error codes
requirements.text: rcp_wire_error_t shall assign each of the seventeen numbered error codes 1-17 the exact numeric value the governing TC18 Remote Control Protocol Specification's own error-code table assigns it, plus a value-0 RCP_ERROR_NONE sentinel (this implementation's own addition, not part of the spec's table) for "no applicable wire code".

requirements.title: rcp_wire_error_string() returns a unique, non-empty message per code
requirements.text: rcp_wire_error_string() shall return a unique, non-empty, human-readable description for every defined rcp_wire_error_t constant, and a non-NULL, non-empty generic message for any other value.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wire_error() maps a CRC mismatch to POCI_FAILURE
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wire_error() shall return RCP_ERROR_POCI_FAILURE for RCP_E2E_ERR_CRC_MISMATCH -- the code the governing spec's own numbered error-code table assigns a CRC mismatch -- and RCP_ERROR_NONE for every other rcp_e2e_errc_t value, since neither RCP_E2E_OK nor RCP_E2E_ERR_SHORT_FRAME has a wire-error-code counterpart.

requirements.title: rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error() distinguishes LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS (state-locked) from UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS (writer-denied)
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error() shall return RCP_ERROR_NONE when rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(state, kind, writer) is true; RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS when the denial is state-driven (a maximally-privileged writer for the same state/kind would also be denied) -- the code closest in meaning to TC18 Figure 16's own diagram-only "LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS" transition, which names no numbered wire error code exactly but unambiguously matches LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS (4), the only numbered code with a semantically corresponding name; and RCP_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS when the denial is specific to this writer or frame on top of an otherwise-permitting state -- TC18 §13.7.1.2's own separate, narrower concrete example (REQ-LIFECYCLE-024).

requirements.title: rcp_udp_annexj_wrap() prepends a 4-octet big-endian sequence number
requirements.text: rcp_udp_annexj_wrap() shall heap-allocate a buffer holding a 4-octet big-endian encapsulation sequence number followed by the given AVTPDU bytes, and return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data=NULL) on allocation failure.

requirements.title: rcp_udp_annexj_unwrap() strips the sequence number and borrows the AVTPDU
requirements.text: rcp_udp_annexj_unwrap() shall read the leading 4-octet big-endian sequence number from a wrap()-produced buffer and point the caller at the AVTPDU bytes that follow (borrowed, not copied), returning false without touching any output parameter when the supplied buffer is shorter than RCP_UDP_ANNEX_J_SEQ_LEN.

requirements.title: send() applies the Annex J encapsulation sequence number automatically
requirements.text: A UDP AVTP transport's send() shall prepend its own per-connection monotonically-incrementing sequence number (via rcp_udp_annexj_wrap()) to every AVTPDU before it reaches the socket, transparently to the rcp_avtp_transport_t caller.

requirements.title: recv() strips the Annex J encapsulation sequence number automatically
requirements.text: A UDP AVTP transport's recv() shall strip the leading Annex J encapsulation sequence number (via rcp_udp_annexj_unwrap()) before returning a received AVTPDU to the caller, dropping (and continuing to wait for the next datagram on) any received datagram shorter than the sequence number field itself; rcp_udp_avtp_transport_last_recv_seq() shall report the sequence number of the most recently successfully received datagram, or 0 if none has been received yet.

requirements.title: dial()/bind()_default_port() target the Annex J control port
requirements.text: rcp_udp_avtp_transport_dial_default_port() and rcp_udp_avtp_transport_bind_default_port() shall behave exactly as rcp_udp_avtp_transport_dial()/_bind() called with port == RCP_UDP_ANNEX_J_CONTROL_PORT (17221).

requirements.title: rcp_l2_frame_encode() builds dst+src+EtherType+AVTPDU framing
requirements.text: rcp_l2_frame_encode() shall heap-allocate a buffer holding the given destination MAC (6 octets), source MAC (6 octets), RCP_L2_ETHERTYPE (2 octets, big-endian), and the given AVTPDU bytes, in that order, and return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data=NULL) on allocation failure.

requirements.title: rcp_l2_frame_decode() validates EtherType and borrows the AVTPDU
requirements.text: rcp_l2_frame_decode() shall return false, leaving every output parameter untouched, when the supplied frame is shorter than RCP_L2_HEADER_LEN or its EtherType field is not RCP_L2_ETHERTYPE; otherwise it shall populate the destination/source MAC outputs and point the caller at the AVTPDU bytes that follow (borrowed, not copied).

requirements.title: rcp_l2_avtp_transport_new() never returns NULL except on allocation failure
requirements.text: rcp_l2_avtp_transport_new() shall return a non-NULL rcp_avtp_transport_t on any failure to open/bind the underlying raw socket or read the interface's own hardware address, with ok() reporting false in that case; it shall return NULL only on this module's own allocation failure.

requirements.title: ok() distinguishes a successful open from a socket/bind/ioctl failure
requirements.text: rcp_l2_avtp_transport_ok() shall return true only for a transport whose underlying raw socket was created, bound to its interface, and had that interface's own hardware address successfully read, all successfully.

requirements.title: local_mac() reports the transport's own interface-derived source MAC
requirements.text: rcp_l2_avtp_transport_local_mac() shall write the network interface's own hardware address (read once at construction time, never caller-supplied) into the caller's buffer and return true for an ok() transport, or return false without writing anything for a transport that is not ok().

requirements.title: send() frames outgoing AVTPDUs with the caller-supplied destination MAC
requirements.text: An L2 AVTP transport's send() shall wrap each AVTPDU via rcp_l2_frame_encode() using the transport's own caller-supplied destination MAC and interface-derived source MAC before transmitting it on the underlying raw socket, and shall return RCP_ERR_CLOSED once close() has been called.

requirements.title: recv() decodes AVTP-over-Ethernet frames and ignores its own transmitted copies
requirements.text: An L2 AVTP transport's recv() shall decode each received frame via rcp_l2_frame_decode(), returning only its AVTPDU bytes to the caller, and shall ignore (continue waiting past) any frame the underlying raw socket reports as this same socket's own locally-transmitted outgoing copy rather than a frame genuinely received from the wire.

requirements.title: close() unblocks a concurrent in-progress recv() without invalidating the fd
requirements.text: Calling close() on an L2 transport while a different thread is blocked inside that same transport's recv() shall cause that recv() call to return RCP_ERR_CLOSED within one poll slice, without the underlying raw socket being invalidated out from under it; the fd itself shall only be closed once destroy() runs.

requirements.title: Non-Linux stub: ok() false and every operation fails without crashing
requirements.text: On a non-Linux platform, rcp_l2_avtp_transport_new() shall return a non-NULL transport whose ok() reports false and whose send()/recv() return RCP_ERR_CLOSED without crashing, exactly matching udp.c's own Windows stub convention.

requirements.title: Missing CAP_NET_RAW/root leaves the transport cleanly not-ok()
requirements.text: When the calling process lacks CAP_NET_RAW (and is not root), rcp_l2_avtp_transport_new()'s underlying raw-socket open shall fail and the returned transport's ok() shall report false, without crashing or requiring the caller to pre-check its own privilege level.

requirements.title: rcp_l2_mac_is_unicast() classifies a destination MAC by its I/G bit
requirements.text: rcp_l2_mac_is_unicast() shall return true iff the least-significant bit of the MAC's first octet (the IEEE 802.3 individual/group bit) is clear, and false otherwise -- including for the all-ones broadcast address, which is itself a special case of multicast under this same bit test. This is the primitive an integrator uses to classify a real frame's destination MAC (from rcp_l2_frame_decode()'s out_dst_mac or the transport-specific equivalent) before constructing an rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t's via_non_unicast_frame member, closing REQ-LIFECYCLE-027's write-request-unicast-only gap.

requirements.title: rcp_compound_start_condition_met() implements the "any state" start_state sentinel
requirements.text: rcp_compound_start_condition_met() shall return true iff step->sequencer_index is rcp_sequencer_index_valid() for table and either step->start_state is zero (the request starts in whatever state the sequencer currently holds) or table's current state at that index equals step->start_state, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.1 ("If cmp_start_state = 0 then the request shall be started in any state unless the sequencer is disabled"). It shall return false for an index the table does not hold, including when start_state is zero.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.1 ("If cmp_start_state = 0 then the request shall be started in any state unless the sequencer is disabled which will prohibit the execution of the compound request."), TC18.txt L1212-1214; same rule for compound-wait, §11.2.2.2, TC18.txt L1311-1314

requirements.title: rcp_compound_encode_request() packs evt into the shared byte_message_info header, not one of step's repurposed sub-fields
requirements.text: rcp_compound_encode_request() shall write its evt parameter into the encoded frame's byte_message_info.evt field (Table 4 octet 4 bits 7:4) via acf.h's rcp_acf_pack_header(), independently of every rcp_compound_step_t sub-field packed into the repurposed message_timestamp region. For a compound-wait request this is the TC18 §13.5.1 comparison-mode selector; a plain compound request has no comparison of its own.

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_request() surfaces the decoded byte_message_info.evt field
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_request() shall, on RCP_COMPOUND_OK, populate *out_evt with the decoded byte_message_info.evt field, independently of every recovered rcp_compound_step_t sub-field.

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_clear_non_safestate() rejects a nonzero reserved message_timestamp octet
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_clear_non_safestate() shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO when any of message_timestamp's 7 trailing octets (every octet after the leading request_type byte) carries a set bit, since clear-non-safestate carries no sub-field of its own. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): the decode function previously read only the leading request_type byte and never validated the remaining 7 octets TC18 Table 12 marks reserved.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 12 ("reserved: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected"), TC18.txt L1759-1775

requirements.title: rcp_compound_decode_clear_non_safestate() rejects nonzero evt[2:0], hs, or cs
requirements.text: rcp_compound_decode_clear_non_safestate() shall return RCP_COMPOUND_ERR_EVT_HS_CS_NONZERO when the decoded ACF byte_message_info header's evt[2:0], hs, or cs is nonzero, per TC18 Table 12's explicit prose ("evt[2:0], hs, cs: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"). Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): this ACF-header-level field was entirely unvalidated before this milestone -- Table 12 is the only one of the three cancel-family tables (11/12/13) to name a specific TC18 Table 27 wire error code for this violation, which a caller wiring this into a real response should reuse (RCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD, errors.h) rather than inventing its own mapping.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 12 ("evt[2:0], hs, cs: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L1759-1775

requirements.title: rcp_timed_decode_request() rejects a non-zero reserved octet
requirements.text: rcp_timed_decode_request() shall return RCP_TIMED_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO when the reserved octet at offset 1 of the repurposed message_timestamp region carries any set bit, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected").
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (reserved bits must be 0), TC18.txt L1613-1616

requirements.title: rcp_timed_decode_request() rejects a timed request with hs or cs set
requirements.text: rcp_timed_decode_request() shall return RCP_TIMED_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD when the decoded byte_message_info hs or cs bit is set, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("hs, cs -- All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD").
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (hs and cs shall both be 0b), TC18.txt L1618-1619,1628-1629

requirements.title: rcp_timed_due() reports whether a presentation_time has arrived
requirements.text: rcp_timed_due() shall return true iff presentation_time is at or before now in the same wrapping 48-bit domain rcp_timed_too_far() uses, i.e. iff the request's execution condition is satisfied.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 ("In any case the presentation_time is the earliest point in time, when the request shall be executed."), TC18.txt L1648-1649

requirements.title: rcp_chained_exec_delay_elapsed() compares elapsed against chain_exec_delay
requirements.text: rcp_chained_exec_delay_elapsed() shall return true iff elapsed >= chain_exec_delay, both expressed in multiples of the addressed endpoint's configured ep_delay_time and measured from the moment the member's predecessor finalized (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 Table 9).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 ("chain_exec_delay: Execution delay in multiples of ep_delay_time... for the request execution after the previous request has been finalized."), TC18.txt L1550-1551

requirements.title: rcp_chained_decode_member() rejects a non-zero reserved sub-field octet
requirements.text: rcp_chained_decode_member() shall return RCP_CHAINED_ERR_RESERVED_NONZERO when any of octets 1-3 or 6-7 of the repurposed message_timestamp region carries a set bit, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 Table 9.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 ("reserved: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request will be rejected" / "...shall be rejected"), TC18.txt L1549, L1552

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() routes each request by its own request_type
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() shall classify each arriving ACF message by peeking its repurposed request_type opcode and passing it to rcp_sched_classify(), and shall route it accordingly: a message that is not a repurposed-timestamp ACF_GBB, or whose opcode this build does not recognize, shall take the rcp_server_endpoint_submit() path unchanged and report RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_EXECUTE_NOW or RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_QUEUED; a cancellation opcode shall report RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_CANCELLATION without being stored; every other conditional kind shall be decoded and stored, reporting RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_PENDING. *out_request_type shall always be written -- the opcode byte for a conditional or cancellation request, 0 otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("An RC Server shall support to handle multiple requests in one frame and check each of them individually if to be processed or not"), TC18.txt L3221-3224; request_type identifiers per §11.2.2 Table 5, TC18.txt L1186-1199

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() rejects an undecodable or unstorable conditional request
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() shall return RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_REJECTED, storing nothing and leaving the request store's occupancy unchanged, when a message whose opcode claims a conditional request kind fails that kind's own decode_* validation, or when the store already holds RCP_SERVER_MAX_PENDING requests.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("An RC Server shall support to handle multiple requests in one frame and check each of them individually if to be processed or not"), TC18.txt L3221-3224; request_type identifiers per §11.2.2 Table 5, TC18.txt L1186-1199; UNSUPPORTED_CMD error-code basis per §11.2.2.1/.2's own optional-feature-not-supported rule, TC18.txt L1204-1205, L1300-1301

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() evaluates each stored request against its own execution condition, including the compound-request idle gate
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() shall report a stored request as due only when that request kind's own condition holds: a compound request requires rcp_compound_start_condition_met() against ctx->sequencers, rcp_compound_exec_delay_elapsed() since it first held, AND ctx->endpoint_idle -- TC18 Table 26's Compound row applies the same idle-and-no-higher-priority gate as Triggered/Chained, distinct from compound-wait's own row, which has none; a compound-wait request requires rcp_compound_start_condition_met(), rcp_compound_exec_delay_elapsed(), and ctx->wait_condition_met, with no idle gate; a triggered request requires rcp_triggered_threshold_reached(), rcp_triggered_exec_delay_elapsed() since the threshold was reached, and ctx->endpoint_idle; a timed request requires ctx->gptp_locked and rcp_timed_due() against ctx->gptp_now; a chained request requires its predecessor to have finalized, rcp_chained_exec_delay_elapsed() since that instant, and ctx->endpoint_idle. It shall report no request as due when none qualifies. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): this entry's own text previously omitted ctx->endpoint_idle from the compound case entirely, matching a real bug in auxiliary_condition_met() (src/server.c), which grouped RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND with COMPOUND_WAIT's own idle-gate-free default case -- a Compound request could execute while its endpoint was busy with another request, until this fix.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("Whenever an Endpoint is able to start a new request, it shall check for all requests in the EP request storage whether they are due for execution" ... priority list: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard), TC18.txt L3248-3266; §12.9.3 Table 26, Compound row ("the state advances to RE as soon as the EP is idle and no request with higher priority is pending"), TC18.txt L3300-3303 -- corrected citation for the idle-gate's own basis

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() holds safety-tagged requests back until the safe state is reached
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() shall report a stored request whose request_type is safety-tagged (MSB set, 0x8x) as due only when rcp_e2e_request_may_execute(request_type, ctx->in_safe_state) permits it, i.e. only once ctx->in_safe_state is true, regardless of whether that request's own execution condition is otherwise satisfied. A non-safety-tagged request shall be unaffected by ctx->in_safe_state.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("Whenever an Endpoint is able to start a new request, it shall check for all requests in the EP request storage whether they are due for execution" ... priority list: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard), TC18.txt L3248-3266; safety-tagged (MSB-set) requests staying in the store until the endpoint's safe state per §11.2.2, TC18.txt L1189-1191 (already implemented as REQ-E2E-012/013's e2e.h gate, rcp_e2e_request_may_execute())

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() returns the highest-priority due request
requirements.text: When more than one stored request is due at once, rcp_server_endpoint_select_due() shall return the one that rcp_sched_compare() orders first over {kind, arrival sequence}: the higher rcp_sched_kind_rank() first, and among requests of equal rank the earliest admitted.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("When two or more requests with the same priority are due then starting the execution shall happen in the order with which the requests arrived in the EP request storage."), TC18.txt L3265-3266

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_complete() applies the executed request's own completion action
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_complete() shall, for a compound request, apply rcp_compound_tick() and, for a compound-wait request, rcp_compound_wait_tick() against ctx->sequencers, so that the sequencer is advanced only when the advance guard still holds. It shall not advance any sequencer for a triggered, timed, or chained request.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 26 (execution procedure per request type -- compound/compound-wait sequencer-state advance and repeat_count decrement, triggered request's exec_delay-from-threshold timing), TC18.txt L3282-3341

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_complete() applies the repetition rule
requirements.text: After the completion action, rcp_server_endpoint_complete() shall leave a request whose repeat_count is the all-ones infinite sentinel in the store with its repeat_count unchanged, shall remove a request whose repeat_count is zero, and shall otherwise decrement repeat_count by one and leave the request in the store re-armed (its start condition to be satisfied afresh before it may run again). Timed and chained requests carry no repetition sub-field and shall always be removed. It shall return true iff the request remains in the store.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 26 (execution procedure per request type -- compound/compound-wait sequencer-state advance and repeat_count decrement, triggered request's exec_delay-from-threshold timing), TC18.txt L3282-3341 -- repeat_count 0xFFFF-infinite / zero-removes-on-finalize rule shared with Table 6/7, TC18.txt L1268-1271, L1385-1388

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_notify_trigger() routes an occurrence to every matching stored request
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_notify_trigger() shall offer the observed (source_ep, signal_nr) occurrence to every stored triggered request via rcp_triggered_runtime_record_occurrence(), so that only requests whose own trigger_source_ep/trigger_signal_nr match count it, and shall return how many counted it.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 26 (execution procedure per request type -- compound/compound-wait sequencer-state advance and repeat_count decrement, triggered request's exec_delay-from-threshold timing), TC18.txt L3282-3341 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero"), TC18.txt L3298-3300

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_chain_predecessor_done() starts a chained request's delay at the predecessor's finalization
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_chain_predecessor_done() shall mark the stored chained request at index as having its predecessor finalized and record now as the instant its chain_exec_delay is measured from, and shall not restart that timer on any later evaluation. It shall return false, changing nothing, when index does not name a stored chained request.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 ("the second and following requests always wait on the predecessor request to finish its execution"), TC18.txt L3283-3286 (chapter reference); worked description at TC18.txt L1514-1516

requirements.title: The cancellation functions remove exactly the requests their own opcode names, but rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_single() does not cascade to chained successors
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_all() shall remove every stored conditional request and return how many; rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_single() shall report rcp_cancel_attempt()'s outcome and remove the stored request whose transaction_num equals clear_transaction_num only when that outcome is RCP_CANCEL_RESULT_CANCELED; rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_non_safestate() shall remove every stored request that is not safety-tagged, leaving the safety-tagged ones in place, and return how many were removed. Each shall free the byte copy of every request it removes. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): TC18 §11.2.3's general cancellation rule additionally requires that cancelling a request also cancel any request chained to it, but rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_single() does not implement this cascade -- it removes only the single matching transaction_num. rcp_cancel_chain_should_cascade() (REQ-CANCEL-012) already implements the correct cascade *decision* but has zero callers anywhere in src/, a known, separately-tracked gap (see REQ-CANCEL-012's own entry, status: partial). This entry's own claim about what the three cancellation functions remove remains accurate as written; the chain-cascade gap is additional, not a contradiction of it.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1/.2 clear-all/clear-single cancellation request handling, TC18.txt L1681, L1735-1738, L1794 (established Phase 1 basis, issue #163); §11.2.3 chain-cascade rule, TC18.txt L1674-1675 (see REQ-CANCEL-012)

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_watchdog_purge() keeps only the safety sequence
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_watchdog_purge() shall remove from the request store exactly those requests rcp_e2e_watchdog_purge_should_keep() does not keep -- i.e. every non-safety-tagged one -- and return how many were removed, so that only the safety sequence survives a watchdog overflow to drive the endpoint into its configured safe state.
requirements.tc18: watch-dog-overflow queue-clearing rule for non-safety-tagged conditional requests ("compound requests with 0x0F will be cleared from the queue while the requests with 0x8F remain active after watch-dog overflow"), TC18.txt L1231-1234, L1330-1332 (compound-wait analogue)

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() routes a request through the request_type-aware admission path
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() shall, after rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() admission and endpoint lookup, route the request through rcp_server_endpoint_admit() and map its outcome onto RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_OK (running the endpoint's handler synchronously), _QUEUED, _PENDING, _CANCELLED (having applied the named cancellation against that endpoint's request store), or _REJECTED. A standard request shall behave exactly as before: executed immediately when the endpoint is enabled, queued when it is not.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_t owns the sequencer-state table compound requests read
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_set_sequencer_count() shall replace and free any sequencer table the server already held with a freshly allocated rcp_sequencer_table_new(count), and rcp_mock_server_sequencers() shall return that table. A server whose table is the unsupported ({NULL,0}) one shall never report a compound or compound-wait request as due.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_tick() executes at most one due conditional request
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_tick() shall select the highest-priority due stored request on the addressed endpoint via rcp_server_endpoint_select_due(), run that request's own stored frame through that endpoint's registered handler, finalize it via rcp_server_endpoint_complete(), and return true. It shall return false, leaving *out_response zeroed and executing nothing, when the byte_bus_id names no endpoint or no stored request is due.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_tick() evaluates conditions against the server's own sequencer table
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_tick() shall evaluate execution conditions against the server's own sequencer table, ignoring and overwriting any sequencers pointer the caller supplied in ctx, so a caller cannot have a request evaluated against a table the server does not own.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_notify_trigger() reaches every endpoint
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_notify_trigger() shall offer the observed (source_ep, signal_nr) occurrence to every registered endpoint's request store, since a triggered request stored on one endpoint routinely waits on a different endpoint's trigger signal, and shall return the total number of stored requests that counted it.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() applies chain sequencing across a frame's members in order
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() shall, for each chained member it encounters, call rcp_chained_advance() with whether any request precedes it in this frame, whether that predecessor finalized with an error, and that member's own cs bit -- reporting RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_CHAIN_ERROR for a chained member with no predecessor and RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_CHAIN_ABORTED for one the chain state excludes, in both cases without dispatching that member to its endpoint. rcp_mock_server_watchdog_purge() shall apply rcp_server_endpoint_watchdog_purge() to the addressed endpoint and return how many requests it purged.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_pending_count() reports an endpoint's conditional-request store occupancy, 0 if unknown
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_pending_count(srv, byte_bus_id) shall return the number of conditional requests currently pending in that endpoint's request store, or 0 if byte_bus_id names no registered endpoint.

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() sends REQUEST_NOT_FOUND when a clear-single target is not found
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch(), when a decoded clear-single cancellation's target clear_transaction_num is not found in the addressed endpoint's request store (rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_single() reports RCP_CANCEL_RESULT_NOT_FOUND), shall populate out_response with a real TC18 error response (rcp_acf_build_error_response()) carrying RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, the addressed byte_bus_id, and the cancellation request's own transaction_num (not the not-found target's).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 ("The request initiating the cancellation will create an error response with the error code = REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, when the clear_transaction_num was not found."), TC18.txt L1837-1838

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() sends a per-member CHAIN_ERROR/CHAIN_ABORTED error response
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame() shall, for each frame member rcp_chained_advance() reports RCP_CHAINED_MEMBER_CHAIN_ERROR or RCP_CHAINED_MEMBER_CHAIN_ABORTED, populate that member's own out_results[].response with a real TC18 error response (rcp_acf_build_error_response()) carrying the corresponding RCP_ERROR_CHAIN_ERROR/RCP_ERROR_CHAIN_ABORTED code, that member's own byte_bus_id, and that member's own transaction_num -- one independent response per affected member, not a single shared response for the whole broken chain.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.4 ("An error response with the error code ‘CHAIN_ERROR’ to each request will be generated by the respective EPs"; “the request send an error response with error code = CHAIN_ABORTED”), TC18.txt L1518-1520,L1556-1560

requirements.title: rcp_mock_server_dispatch() drops a request silently when byte_bus_id names no registered endpoint
requirements.text: rcp_mock_server_dispatch(), when byte_bus_id names no registered endpoint (find_slot() returns NULL), shall leave out_response zeroed (no response sent) and return RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_ERR_UNKNOWN_BUS. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): this entry previously required a wire EP_NOT_FOUND error response for this case, a real conformance bug introduced by an earlier milestone (issue #163 Phase 1) that misapplied TC18 Table 27's EP_NOT_FOUND (8) code -- that code's own Table 27 description is scoped to "if a Trigger request refers to a nonexisting EP" (a Trigger request's own trigger_source_ep sub-field naming a nonexistent EP, a case this codebase does not implement at all, per ROADMAP.md milestone 120's own note), not to the addressed endpoint of the request itself. TC18 §12.9.1 explicitly and unambiguously requires the opposite of what this entry previously claimed: an unregistered byte_bus_id is dropped with no response. RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_ERR_UNKNOWN_BUS's own internal dispatch-result semantics (distinguishing this case for chained-request cascade purposes in rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame()) are unaffected -- only the wire response this function used to send has been removed.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1 ("If the lookup of the byte_bus_id in the context of the stream_id does not point to an Endpoint, the request is dropped without further notification."), TC18.txt L3195-3197 -- Table 27's EP_NOT_FOUND (8) row (TC18.txt L3425-3426), previously miscited here, describes a different, unimplemented scenario (a Trigger request's own trigger_source_ep naming a nonexistent EP)

requirements.title: acf_msg_type constants carry the specification's own numeric values
requirements.text: RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB shall equal 0x0E and RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB shall equal 0x0D, the acf_msg_type values TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4 and §11.2.2.1 Table 6 assign to the abbreviated byte bus (ACF_ABB) and generic byte bus (ACF_GBB) message formats respectively.

requirements.title: read_size/segment_num interpretation is selected by the op bit
requirements.text: The 12-bit read_size_or_segment_num field of byte_message_info shall be interpreted as read_size when the op bit is 0 (RCP_ACF_OP_READ, a request expecting a data response) and as segment_num otherwise, per TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4 and §11.2.2.1 Table 6. c-RCP shall expose that selection to callers rather than leaving the field an uninterpreted round-tripped slot.

requirements.title: The 3-state rcp_acf_op_t maps onto the specification's single op bit
requirements.text: rcp_acf_encode_abb()/rcp_acf_encode_gbb() shall encode op as the single wire bit TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4 defines -- 0b when the sender expects a response with data (RCP_ACF_OP_READ) and 1b when it does not (RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE and the encode-only convenience value RCP_ACF_OP_NONE, which is indistinguishable from RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE on the wire) -- and rcp_acf_decode_abb()/rcp_acf_decode_gbb() shall therefore never produce RCP_ACF_OP_NONE from decoded input.

requirements.title: byte_bus_id is 11 bits on the wire; c-RCP now represents the full range
requirements.text: byte_message_info's byte_bus_id field is 11 bits wide on the wire (byte_bus_id[10:8] in octet 2 bits 2:0 and byte_bus_id[7:0] in octet 3), per TC18 §11.2.1 Figure 7 / Table 4. Fixed: rcp_byte_bus_id_t (avtp.h) is now uint16_t, wide enough to hold the full 0-2047 range, so rcp_acf_pack_header()/rcp_acf_unpack_header() (acf.c) encode and decode every bit of the field -- endpoint identifiers 0-2047 are all addressable and representable. rcp_acf_unpack_header() no longer returns an overflow error for a high byte_bus_id: RCP_ACF_ERR_BUS_ID_OVERFLOW is retired outright (removed from rcp_acf_errc_t), since the condition it represented -- a decoded value the type couldn't hold -- can no longer occur (the wire field's own 3-bit-plus-8-bit extraction is mathematically bounded to 0x7FF, a value the widened type always represents).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1, TC18.txt L1142 (Figure 7) and L1158 (Table 4)

requirements.title: A request carries rsv=00b, hs=0b, cs=0b, rsp=0b and err=0b unless its own kind assigns the bit a meaning
requirements.text: An encoded RCP request shall carry rsv = 00b, hs = 0b, err = 0b, and rsp = 0b (rsp = 0b is what identifies an ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB message as a request rather than a response), and cs = 0b except where the request kind assigns cs its own meaning (compound-wait per TC18 §11.2.2.2 Table 7, chained per §11.2.2.4 Table 9); a received message whose rsp bit is set shall not be admitted as a request. c-RCP currently forces only rsv to zero and round-trips hs, cs, rsp and err without constraint.

requirements.title: Every response sets rsp=1b, identifying it as a response per TC18
requirements.text: TC18 §11.3 (TC18.txt L1885): "rsp 1b -- identifies this ABB or GBB message as response" (the corresponding request-side tables at L1165/L1276/L1384/etc. state rsp=0b identifies a request). FIXED: every rcp_ep_*_encode_response()/rcp_discovery_encode_response*() function across all 13 endpoint modules now sets rsp=1 on the ACF header it builds, instead of leaving it at its zero-initialized default -- previously every response was wire-indistinguishable from a request by this bit.

requirements.title: rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain() implements Table 30's shared ADC/PWM_IN/I2C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO rule
requirements.text: rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain(evt) shall return true iff (evt & 0x7) == 0, per TC18 §13.5 Table 30's rule for the {ADC, PWM_IN, I2C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO} endpoint-type row: evt[2:0] = 000b is the only value a plain (non-configuration) request in this row may carry; every other value is either reserved (001b-110b, reject with UNSUPPORTED_CMD) or selects a configuration-write-shaped request instead (111b, §12.7.1). RESOLVED AMBIGUITY (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group A): Table 30's own literal text groups evt[2:0]=000b together with 001b-110b as a single "reserved -- reject" range, which read in isolation would make evt=000b illegal too. That reading is directly contradicted by TC18's own §13.7.9.3 Figure 33 ("RC Client sends a standard read request"), a labeled, bit-level worked example for the ADC endpoint (a member of this exact row) showing evt[2:0]=000b used in a request the spec's own next figure (34) shows succeeding normally, not being rejected. Table 30's prose and the spec's own concrete worked example directly conflict for the same endpoint type -- a genuine internal inconsistency in this Release Candidate draft. This implementation follows the worked example (evt=000b is the ordinary, successful case), since a reading that made every plain request illegal for eight endpoint types would leave those endpoints permanently unusable for normal operation, which the spec's own examples contradict. An earlier full-catalog audit pass (issue #256) flagged this function as non-conformant based on Table 30's prose alone, without cross-checking Figure 33; that finding is refuted by this evidence and no code change was made.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 30, TC18.txt L3666-3710 (the reserved-range wording); §13.7.9.3 Figure 33/34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request" / ADC response with 8 measurements), the corroborating worked example resolving the ambiguity in Table 30's own favor for evt=000b

requirements.title: rcp_acf_compound_wait_evt_valid() rejects exactly the reserved 011b value
requirements.text: rcp_acf_compound_wait_evt_valid(evt) shall return true iff (evt & 0x7) != 0x3, per TC18 §13.5.1: a compound-wait request's evt[2:0] selects one of eight comparison modes, of which 011b is reserved -- a request carrying it shall be ignored and an err-response with error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD sent. This rule is endpoint-type-independent, unlike Table 30's per-row rule (rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain()).

requirements.title: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() applies the shared status-length rule before any mode-specific comparison
requirements.text: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() shall return false, regardless of comparison mode or buffer contents, when status_len < payload_len (the wait condition never comes true if the interface status has fewer bytes than byte_msg_payload); otherwise it shall compare against only status's own first payload_len bytes, ignoring any bytes beyond that -- e.g. only the first four out of a 20-byte SPI status report are checked when byte_msg_payload has four bytes. rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() shall also return false for evt[2:0] = 0x3 (reserved); callers must reject that value with UNSUPPORTED_CMD via rcp_acf_compound_wait_evt_valid() rather than relying on this fallback.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1, TC18.txt L3735-3741 (length-capping rule and its own SPI example)

requirements.title: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() evt[2:0]=000b: exact match
requirements.text: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() shall, for evt[2:0] = 000b, return true iff byte_msg_payload matches the (length-capped) current interface status exactly, byte for byte.

requirements.title: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() evt[2:0]=001b: AND-with-1s-mask
requirements.text: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() shall, for evt[2:0] = 001b, return true iff every bit position set to 1 in byte_msg_payload is also set to 1 in the (length-capped) current interface status -- equivalently, for every covered byte i, (payload[i] AND status[i]) OR NOT(payload[i]) == 0xFF.

requirements.title: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() evt[2:0]=010b: AND-with-0s-mask
requirements.text: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() shall, for evt[2:0] = 010b, return true iff every bit position set to 1 in byte_msg_payload is set to 0 in the (length-capped) current interface status -- equivalently, for every covered byte i, payload[i] AND status[i] == 0x00.

requirements.title: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() evt[2:0]=100b/101b: leading-quadlet high-word >=/<=
requirements.text: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() shall, for evt[2:0] = 100b, return true iff the first two bytes of byte_msg_payload's own leading quadlet, read big-endian, are >= the same two bytes of the current interface status, and for evt[2:0] = 101b the <= counterpart; both shall return false (never read out of bounds) when payload_len < 4.

requirements.title: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() evt[2:0]=110b/111b: leading-quadlet low-word >=/<=
requirements.text: rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() shall, for evt[2:0] = 110b, return true iff the last two bytes of byte_msg_payload's own leading quadlet, read big-endian, are >= the same two bytes of the current interface status, and for evt[2:0] = 111b the <= counterpart; both shall return false (never read out of bounds) when payload_len < 4.

requirements.title: rcp_acf_build_error_response() builds a TC18 §12.9.6 error response
requirements.text: rcp_acf_build_error_response() shall build an ACF_ABB message carrying the given byte_bus_id and transaction_num, err = 1, rsp = 1, evt != RCP_ACF_EVT_ACKNOWLEDGE (so rcp_acf_classify_response() reports RCP_ACF_RESP_ERROR), and a one-octet byte_msg_payload equal to the given rcp_wire_error_t code's numeric value.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.6 ("The error response shall contain the byte_bus_id and transaction number of the request. The error response shall contain a byte_msg_payload with an error code."), TC18.txt L3406-3411; §11.3.4, TC18.txt L1924-1926

requirements.title: The evt[2:0]=111b EP_func configuration request is implemented for PWM_OUT, PWM_IN, GPIO, SPI, I2C, UART, LIN, ADC, ISELED, MDIO, and WakeUp only
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial; narrowed 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I, REQ-MDIO-020/023): TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request — evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data — usable against EVERY endpoint type either through the RC Server (EP0) register map or directly by byte_bus_id. c-RCP now implements this shape for nine of the eleven endpoint types (ten modules, since PWM_OUT and PWM_IN share src/ep_pwm.c): rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_reconfig() and rcp_ep_pwm_in_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_pwm.c — PWM_IN corrected 2026-08-11: this endpoint type had been silently uncounted, since the pwm.c module's own slot in this tally was marked done once PWM_OUT's earlier fix landed, without separately checking whether PWM_IN — a functionally distinct endpoint type with its own TC18 table, sharing only the source file — needed the identical fix; it did, including a real live conformance bug: rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_read_request() never validated evt[2:0] at all before this fix, so an evt=111b configuration request would have been silently misinterpreted as an ordinary read, see REQ-PWM-059), rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_gpio.c), rcp_ep_spi_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_spi.c), rcp_ep_i2c_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_i2c.c), rcp_ep_uart_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_uart.c), rcp_ep_lin_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_lin.c), rcp_ep_adc_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_adc.c — ADC's own decode_read_request() already correctly rejected evt=111b as RCP_EP_ADC_ERR_BAD_EVT via acf.h's rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain(), but had no counterpart implementing that path at all), rcp_ep_iseled_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_iseled.c — ISELED's own decode_command_request() already correctly rejected evt=111b as RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_BAD_EVT, but had no counterpart implementing that path at all; TC18 §13.7.12.2 Table 55's own address-collision editorial defect, the fourth of this class found this audit, is corrected the same way ep_pwm.h's/ep_gpio.h's/ep_i2c.h's own were — see REQ-ISELED-029), and rcp_ep_mdio_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_mdio.c, new — MDIO's own decode_read_request()/decode_write_request() already correctly rejected evt=111b as RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_EVT, but had no counterpart implementing that path at all; TC18 §13.7.13.2 Table 56's own address-collision editorial defect, the fifth of this class found this audit, is corrected the same way — see REQ-MDIO-020/023. Note this endpoint type's own register block is one register width narrower than every other's, since Table 56 defines no base_clk row at all.) and rcp_ep_wakeup_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_wakeup.c, new, 2026-08-11, task #95 dedicated investigation -- TC18 §13.7.2.2 Table 36 has a genuine, literal address collision between wup_status and the wake-source array's own first entry (wup_io_scr1), both printed at the same relative address, confirmed via the rendered page image on both the 0.5.1_RC baseline and the 0.5.1_RC5 revision; resolved via this session's own established cross-table pattern -- wup_status keeps its own printed address, the source array shifts to start immediately after it. Two further gaps are handled conservatively rather than with a from-scratch redesign, and remain honestly disclosed as partial, not fully implemented: wup_status renders/parses only its own pre-existing single-aggregate-latch bit, not TC18's own full 16-bit per-source bitmask; and each wup_io_scrN register renders/parses only 3 of Table 37's 6 IO_SRC values (inactive/high level/low level), since this module's own pre-existing rcp_ep_wakeup_source_asserted() predicate is level-only and was left unchanged rather than redesigned to add edge-triggering -- see REQ-WAKEUP-021/022's own updated text.) CAN was investigated and deliberately deferred: TC18 §13.7.11.2 Table 53 defines three opaque 32-bit 'CAN bit time register' fields with no sub-field bit-layout given in the extraction, so mapping the existing rcp_ep_can_bit_timing_t (prescaler/prop_seg/phase_seg1/phase_seg2/sync_jump_width) onto them is not derivable without inventing an unverified bit-packing scheme; Table 53 also has its own genuine address collision (acceptance filter 3/4 both printed at 0x002C) requiring dedicated investigation, matching the same precedent. Only CAN still exposes no EP_func addressed-write path, and no server-side dispatcher classifies an incoming evt==7 request as a configuration request and routes it to the addressed endpoint. Consequence: endpoint functional configuration is unreachable over the wire for 1 of 11 endpoint types.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 18, TC18.txt L2464-2466, L2473-2479

requirements.title: Every endpoint must publish EP_LEN at EP_func offset 0x00 and ignore a write overrunning it
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partial; narrowed 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I, REQ-WAKEUP-021/022): TC18 §12.7.1 requires that every endpoint publish its EP_LEN parameter at EP_func relative start_address 0x00, and that any byte_msg_payload whose length plus start_address exceeds EP_LEN be ignored in its entirety. c-RCP now satisfies this for PWM_OUT, PWM_IN, GPIO, SPI, I2C, UART, LIN, ADC, ISELED, MDIO, and WakeUp — RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_REG_EP_LEN and RCP_EP_PWM_IN_REG_EP_LEN both at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_pwm.h — PWM_IN corrected 2026-08-11, see REQ-CFG-011's own note), RCP_EP_GPIO_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_gpio.h), RCP_EP_SPI_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_spi.h), RCP_EP_I2C_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_i2c.h), RCP_EP_UART_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_uart.h), RCP_EP_LIN_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_lin.h), RCP_EP_ADC_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_adc.h), RCP_EP_ISELED_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_iseled.h), RCP_EP_MDIO_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_mdio.h), RCP_EP_WAKEUP_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_wakeup.h, new), with the out-of-range rejection in each module's own apply_reconfig(). Only CAN still has no EP_LEN register or overrun-rejection path at all, because it has no addressed EP_func write path at all (see REQ-CFG-011). Consequence: the specification's one universal bounds check on configuration writes exists at 10 of the eleven endpoint types.

requirements.title: rcp_config_manifest_free() releases every owned array and zeroes the manifest
requirements.text: rcp_config_manifest_free(m) shall free m's hw_pin_map, endpoints, and streams arrays and then zero *m in place, leaving it safe to reuse or discard.

requirements.title: A discovery request while the discovery stream is already claimed is answered with a stream-occupied error
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_discovery_claim_note_request() (discovery.h/discovery.c) now returns bool -- true when the discovery claim was open and granted, false when refused because it was already held by an unlapsed claimant (TC18 §12.3, Figure 16's own two "Discovery request received" transitions, applied uniformly regardless of requester identity: a different client or the current claimant re-requesting are both refused). A caller now has a real signal to act on instead of an unreportable silent decline. STILL OPEN: DISCOVERY_STREAM_OCCUPIED is a Figure-16-diagram-only label with no corresponding numbered code in TC18 §12.9.6 Table 27 (rcp_wire_error_t stops at RCP_ERROR_CHAIN_ERROR, 17) -- unlike LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS (which cleanly maps onto RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS, the only numbered code with a semantically matching name), no numbered code here has an obviously corresponding meaning, so this codebase does not invent one; which wire error code (if any) a caller should send for the false case remains a genuine, unresolved ambiguity (same class as REQ-ACF-012's RCP_ACF_MTV_UNCERTAIN).

requirements.title: per-stream sequence-number enforcement (rx_enforce_seq)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x000D bit 1 (rx_enforce_seq, 1 bit, R/W*), requires that a request only be filed for execution if the sequence number carried in its AVTPDU has increased relative to the previously accepted request on that stream. c-RCP now implements the comparison as a pure, directly-testable primitive: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t carries the rx_enforce_seq config bit, and rcp_e2e_seq_evaluate() (e2e.h/e2e.c), given a caller-owned rcp_e2e_seq_tracker_t, decides accept/reject using RFC 1982 serial-number comparison so the 8-bit AVTPDU sequence_num's wraparound (0xFF -> 0x00) is treated as a valid single increment rather than a rejection. What remains not implemented: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() itself has no sequence_num input at all -- the AVTPDU header is decoded and discarded by whatever caller demultiplexes a frame before handing admit() the ACF payload (e.g. mock.c's rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame()) -- so no caller in this codebase actually calls rcp_e2e_seq_evaluate() yet. A replayed or reordered AVTPDU is still filed and executed exactly like a fresh one until that integration exists.

requirements.title: sequence-error safe-state escalation (rx_seq_safestate_enable)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x000D bit 2 (rx_seq_safestate_enable, 1 bit, R/W*), requires that a detected sequence-number discontinuity (a Sequence_Nr that did not advance by exactly one increment) bring all endpoints bound to that request stream into their configured safe state. c-RCP now implements the detection: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t carries the rx_seq_safestate_enable config bit, and rcp_e2e_seq_evaluate()'s result.enter_safe_state field is true exactly when a discontinuity is detected and rx_seq_safestate_enable is set -- independent of, and can be true even when, result.accept is also true (an out-of-order-but-forward gap is still filed, per rx_enforce_seq's own rule, while also being flagged as unsafe). What remains not implemented, and architecturally cannot be performed from inside this decision alone: (1) nothing in this codebase calls rcp_e2e_seq_evaluate() yet -- see REQ-E2E-028's own text for why; (2) even once wired, the actual cross-endpoint escalation this field signals -- bringing every OTHER endpoint bound to the same request stream to its safe state -- is the same architecture boundary already documented for rcp_e2e_overflow_should_enter_safe_state() (REQ-E2E-030): this library's rcp_server_endpoint_t is scoped to one endpoint, with no type representing "all endpoints on a stream" to reach across into.

requirements.title: request-storage-overflow safe-state escalation (rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: c-RCP now reports rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable's (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x000D bit 5, 1 bit, R/W*) triggering condition conformantly at the single-endpoint scope it owns -- rcp_server_endpoint_admit() sets *out_error = RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_STORAGE_OVERFLOW on a request-store-full admission outcome (src/server.c), which mock.c's finish_admission() (and any caller following the same pattern) turns into a real Table 27 error response via rcp_acf_build_error_response(). rcp_e2e_overflow_should_enter_safe_state() (include/rcp/e2e.h, src/e2e.c) is the pure rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable decision such escalation would be gated on. What remains not implemented: the stream-wide half of the rule -- bringing every OTHER endpoint bound to the same request stream into its configured safe state -- which rcp_server_endpoint_t's single-endpoint scope has no way to perform from inside admit() itself; TC18 §13.6's per-stream rcp_server_endpoint_t model has no type representing "all endpoints on a stream" for this or any other module to reach across into. That escalation needs a caller-owned, cross-endpoint orchestrator that does not yet exist in this codebase.

requirements.title: GPIO request payload is exactly four bytes, mapped LSB-first for endpoints with fewer than 32 pins
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_decode_write_request() and rcp_ep_gpio_decode_request() shall reject any GPIO request whose byte_msg_payload is not exactly RCP_EP_GPIO_PAYLOAD_LEN (4) octets with RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_BAD_PAYLOAD_LEN -- the condition TC18 13.7.4.1 answers on the wire with error code INVALID_PARAMETER -- and an endpoint supporting fewer than RCP_EP_GPIO_MAX_PINS (32) pins shall map its pins onto the least-significant bits of that 32-bit payload.

requirements.title: GPIO trigger signal numbering (Table 40)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP implements the three GPIO trigger conditions (rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() for change, rising and falling edges) but assigns them no trigger signal numbers, so TC18 Table 40's numbering -- signal 0 'GPIO EP request execution done' and, for each pin IOn, signal 3n+1 change / 3n+2 rising / 3n+3 falling up to signal 96 for IO31 falling -- is not represented. A triggered request naming a Table 40 signal number cannot be resolved by this library.

requirements.title: GPIO functional-config registers: base clock, divider and per-pin debounce (Table 41)
