requirements.text: PARTIAL (corrected 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group G, REQ-GPIO-013): rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_t now carries ep_status, clk_divider, and a 32-entry debounce[] array, wire-addressable via the real evt[2:0]=111b EP_func mechanism rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig()/rcp_ep_gpio_render_registers() now implement -- TC18 Table 41's gpio_ep_status (0x0006), gpio_clk_divider (0x0008), and the 32 per-pin gpio_debounce_IOn registers (0x0009..0x0028; see ep_gpio.h's own file header for the resolved 0x0024-labelled editorial defect in the source table) all have real storage a caller can read and write over the wire. What remains NOT IMPLEMENTED: gpio_base_clk (0x0004) is read-only and always renders 0 -- this module defines no real GPIO clock source; and no debounce FILTERING logic exists anywhere -- the rule that n>0 requires n consecutive equal samples, taken off the divided base clock independently of requests, before an input value changes is not enforced. The debounce registers are storage only; the sampling state machine they would configure is a separate, still-open gap.

requirements.title: GPIO response timing: immediate for a pure read, post-debounce otherwise
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 13.7.4.3's GPIO response-timing rule -- a read request carrying no byte_msg_payload generates its response immediately on execution, while a payload-bearing read or any write first changes the pin drive and only then, after the configured debounce time has elapsed, produces its response. Debounce is not modeled (see the Table 41 gap), so both cases respond identically.

requirements.title: A write to a pin configured as input leaves that pin's value unchanged
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_masked_write() shall, for every evt, commit rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write()'s combined result to a bit position only when pins[i] has RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_OUTPUT set, and shall leave that bit position's value from current unchanged when pins[i] does not, regardless of what request or the combinator's result specify for that position.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.3 ("A write request to an input pin is ignored for this input pin"), TC18.txt L4481

requirements.title: I2C functional-config registers beyond i2c_mode, and the Ultra-fast preset, are now modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): c-RCP's rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_t now carries i2c_clock_divider, i2c_trail (minimum trail time between two transactions in I2C clock cycles), and i2c_ep_status alongside i2c_mode (i2c_base_clk is not itself stored -- it has no setter and always renders 0, the same "no real clock source modelled" honesty ep_gpio.h's own gpio_base_clk already commits to); rcp_ep_i2c_mode_valid() now accepts Ultra-fast mode (value 4, 5 Mbit/s). rcp_ep_i2c_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() implement the whole Table 46 block at corrected addresses: Table 46's own printed relative-address column collides i2c_ep_enable&clr (0x0002) with i2c_base_clk (also printed at 0x0002) and i2c_base_clk's second octet with i2c_ep_status (both printed at 0x0004) -- confirmed via direct visual inspection of the source PDF (physical page 99), not a text-extraction artifact. PWM_OUT's, GPIO's, and SPI's own common EP_func prefixes all place the same five conceptual fields (EP_LEN / a reserved-or-count octet / enable&clr / options / a 16-bit read-only base-clock register) at the identical address sequence 0x0000/0x0001/0x0002/0x0003/0x0004-0x0005, followed by a 16-bit ep_status at 0x0006-0x0007 -- that cross-table pattern is authoritative here too, so i2c_base_clk is placed at 0x0004-0x0005 (not the table's own printed 0x0002), pushing i2c_ep_status to 0x0006-0x0007, i2c_clock_divider to 0x0008, i2c_mode to 0x0009, and i2c_trail to 0x000A (RCP_EP_I2C_EP_FUNC_LEN = 0x000B, 11 octets total). Table 46 still numbers two distinct rows '3' (High-speed 1.7 and 3.4 Mbit/s), an ambiguity ep_i2c.h resolves conservatively in favour of the lower numbering -- this remains unresolved pending spec errata, unrelated to the fixes above.

requirements.title: I2C payload carries the address and the endpoint stays address-format agnostic
requirements.text: The I2C endpoint's request codec shall treat the byte_msg_payload as the complete I2C payload INCLUDING the target address and shall not interpret, validate or rewrite that address -- remaining transparent to whether the transfer uses a 7-bit or a 10-bit address, per TC18 13.7.7.3.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_render_registers()/_encode_reconfig_request() implement the generic §12.7.1 configuration request for I2C
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request -- evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data -- usable against every endpoint type. rcp_ep_i2c_decode_transfer_request() already correctly rejected evt[2:0] = 111b as not a plain transfer (RCP_EP_I2C_ERR_BAD_EVT, via acf.h's rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain()), but no counterpart function implemented that path at all. rcp_ep_i2c_render_registers() serializes cfg's whole (corrected-address) Table 46 block; rcp_ep_i2c_encode_reconfig_request() encodes an ACF_ABB write request (op=WRITE, evt=111b) carrying a 16-bit big-endian start address followed by data, matching PWM_OUT's/GPIO's/SPI's own encode_reconfig_request() shape.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 18, TC18.txt L2463-2484

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror() apply the addressed configuration write and never return NULL for a status message
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_i2c_apply_reconfig() decodes the address+data payload TC18 §12.7.1 defines and patches cfg's Table 46 register block at octet granularity, then adopts the whole block atomically -- a write whose start_address+length exceeds RCP_EP_I2C_EP_FUNC_LEN is rejected and cfg left entirely unchanged (RCP_EP_I2C_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE), matching §12.7.1's own 'such a payload is to be ignored' rule; octets landing on a read-only register (EP_LEN, the reserved octet, or base_clk) are silently skipped while the rest of the span is still applied. rcp_ep_i2c_reconfig_strerror() never returns NULL, including for an unrecognized error code.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints, TC18.txt L2463-2484

requirements.title: A lifecycle-state change is refused with EPs_NOT_IDLE while any other endpoint is busy
requirements.text: PARTIAL: verified directly against the primary-source PDF's own Figure 16 image (not just the pre-existing text extraction, which renders this diagram too poorly to trust for a design decision) -- confirms the EPs_NOT_IDLE gate applies to exactly two transitions: the HW_UNCONFIGURED -> HW_CONFIGURED advance ("...& all other EPs are Idle -> send positive response") and either reset-to-HW_UNCONFIGURED transition ("...& other EPs are not Idle -> send error response EPs_NOT_IDLE"); the HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED advance's own label makes no mention of idleness and is correctly NOT gated. rcp_lifecycle_transition() now takes an all_other_eps_idle parameter and rejects with the new RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_EPS_NOT_IDLE for both gated transitions when false. Not fully IMPLEMENTED: TC18's own diagram names this outcome "EPs_NOT_IDLE" but that name maps to none of the seventeen numbered wire error codes errors.h models (§12.9.6's own table) -- a genuine TC18 inconsistency (the diagram-only name has no corresponding numbered code anywhere in the specification) this library cannot resolve by inventing a mapping, so RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_EPS_NOT_IDLE remains a local-only lifecycle error code, not yet wired to a wire response.
requirements.tc18: §12.3, TC18.txt L2117-L2120 and L2129-L2131 (Figure 16, verified against primary-source PDF page 42's own image)

requirements.title: Endpoint-generic and response-queue configuration are locked alongside HW_config in HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: verified directly against the primary-source PDF's own Figure 16 image (page 42) -- the diagram groups HW_CONFIG, QUEUE_CFG and EP_GEN_CFG under one identical transition: "Request on discovery stream or known stream/bb_id for configuration to HW_CONFIG or QUEUE_CFG or EP_GEN_CFG -> send error response LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS". RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC's own pre-existing writability rule (writable only in HW_UNCONFIGURED, for any writer) is already exactly this rule -- no new rcp_lifecycle_field_kind_t value or behavior change was needed, only recognizing (now documented directly in that enum's own doc comment) that its scope already covers the endpoint-generic (rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_t) and response-queue/request-stream (rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t / rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t, where not already covered by Table 22's own separate FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR legend) blocks, not just HW pin-mapping. A future caller wiring up write access to either block should classify it as RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC.
requirements.tc18: §12.3, TC18.txt L2110-L2113 (Figure 16, verified against primary-source PDF page 42's own image)

requirements.title: A denied configuration write is answered with LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS (state-locked) or UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS (writer-denied)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED, corrected a second time after a closer primary-source re-reading: this entry's text previously (a) cited RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS as the sole expected code, then (b) after checking only TC18 §13.7.1.2's prose, concluded the opposite -- that every denial maps to RCP_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS uniformly. Both were incomplete: checking Figure 16's own diagram (page 42) in addition to the prose reveals TC18 actually specifies two distinct cases. Figure 16's HW_CONFIGURED-box transition -- "Request on discovery stream or known stream/bb_id for configuration to HW_CONFIG or QUEUE_CFG or EP_GEN_CFG -> send error response LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS" -- covers an otherwise-authorized request denied purely because the target block is state-locked (every RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC denial, and a FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR denial once RCP_CONFIGURED); LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS does not literally match any of the seventeen numbered wire error codes' own strings, but is unambiguously RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS (4), the only numbered code with a semantically matching name (the same prose-vs-table naming variance already documented for POCI_FAILURE). §13.7.1.2's own prose -- "Writing to a write prohibited register (e.g. lock bit for map set) creates a response with err=1 and an error code UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS" -- is the separate, narrower case: a writer/frame-specific denial on top of an otherwise-permitting state. rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error() now distinguishes these (comparing the real writer's verdict against a maximally-privileged writer's verdict for the same state/kind, to isolate which case applies) rather than collapsing them to one code.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2, TC18.txt L4039-L4041; Figure 16, TC18.txt L2110-L2113 (verified against primary-source PDF page 42's own image)

requirements.title: Requests on an unknown stream/byte_bus_id are ignored in HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: PARTIAL: verified directly against the primary-source PDF's own Figure 16 image (page 42; the pre-existing text extraction renders this diagram too poorly to trust for a design decision). Finding: HW_CONFIGURED's own box shows an explicit self-loop -- "Non discovery request & discovery stream assigned or unknown stream/bb_id -> ignore" -- which REQ-LIFECYCLE-032's already-merged fix (HW_CONFIGURED admits only byte_bus_id == EP0) substantively satisfies for the unknown-byte_bus_id half: any non-EP0 byte_bus_id is now dropped, matching this rule's intent, though not with full precision to the diagram's own "non discovery request" / "discovery stream already assigned" distinctions, which rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() still does not model separately. RCP_CONFIGURED's own box, by contrast, shows NO equivalent "unknown stream/bb_id -> ignore" transition anywhere in the diagram -- every one of its four transitions/self-loops is phrased as a positive "Request via stream_id/bb_id..." precondition, with no corresponding negative/ignore case drawn the way HW_UNCONFIGURED's and HW_CONFIGURED's boxes both have. This is genuine spec silence (Figure 16 itself does not specify RCP_CONFIGURED's unknown-association behavior), not a straightforward c-RCP gap to close by inference -- inventing behavior TC18 does not actually specify would risk introducing non-conformant behavior rather than fixing one. Tracked as an open architecture question, same underlying "no wire-level concept of a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id association" limitation as REQ-LIFECYCLE-034.
requirements.tc18: §12.3, TC18.txt L2101-L2105 (Figure 16, verified against primary-source PDF page 42's own image)

requirements.title: In HW_UNCONFIGURED only the discovery claimant's stream may configure the server
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: primary-source re-verification found the enforcement point this entry originally named was wrong -- rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() is a frame-admission filter (subtype/msg-type/byte_bus_id only), not where TC18's own write-authorization rules live in this codebase (that is rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(), the same layering REQ-LIFECYCLE-027/030/036 already established). The real gap was RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC's HW_UNCONFIGURED branch admitting any writer unconditionally, with no authorization concept at all. Fixed: HW_GENERIC is now writable in HW_UNCONFIGURED only when writer.via_discovery_stream is set, matching TC18 §12.3.1.1's "All configurations must be run via the stream which was used for discovery." Deriving via_discovery_stream from a real frame's stream_id against rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant() (src/discovery.c) is caller composition, per discovery.h's own documented architecture -- the same division of responsibility REQ-LIFECYCLE-027's via_non_unicast_frame member already established for this library.

requirements.title: Write requests are accepted only from unicast frames
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.3.1.1, §12.3.1.2 and §12.3.1.3 each state (once per lifecycle state) that a write request is accepted only when carried in a unicast frame. rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t gained a via_non_unicast_frame member (l2.h's new rcp_l2_mac_is_unicast() -- REQ-L2-011 -- is the primitive an integrator uses to classify a real frame's destination MAC into it), and rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() now ANDs !writer.via_non_unicast_frame into every kind/state that would otherwise be writable, uniformly across HW_GENERIC, FUNCTIONAL_W and FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR. rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() gained a matching via_unicast parameter so its one real derivation path plumbs the same classification through. rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() deliberately still takes no destination-MAC input: TC18's rule is scoped to write requests specifically, not general frame admission, so gating happens only at the field_writable() layer where the write path already lives, not at should_accept()'s frame-admission layer.

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED drops TSCF-headed AVTPDUs regardless of time-sync support
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.3.1.2 (whose own printed heading confusingly repeats "HW_UNCONFIGURED" -- verified against the primary-source PDF directly to rule out an extraction artifact; the section's actual content is unambiguously about HW_CONFIGURED, distinct from the correctly-labeled §12.3.1.1 immediately preceding it) requires TSCF-headed AVTPDUs to be dropped in HW_CONFIGURED without further response, unconditionally. rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() now drops a TSCF-headed frame in HW_CONFIGURED regardless of time_sync_supported, the same unconditional rule already applied to HW_UNCONFIGURED.

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED drops ACF_GBB-format requests without response
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (resolved differently than originally scoped): this entry's own remaining exposure -- a conditional (ACF_GBB) request literally addressed to EP0 in HW_CONFIGURED, the one case REQ-LIFECYCLE-032's byte_bus_id restriction did not already cover -- turned out to directly conflict with TC18 §12.7's own text once REQ-LIFECYCLE-033 was scoped: §12.7 requires EP0-addressed non-STANDARD requests to be answered with REQUEST_REJECTED, not silently dropped as this entry's own §12.3.1.2 citation demands. Resolved by reading §12.3.1.2's "requests in ACF_GBB format[are dropped]" as the general, non-EP0-scoped rule (still correctly enforced -- any non-EP0 byte_bus_id is dropped by REQ-LIFECYCLE-032's own restriction, unconditionally of acf_msg_type) and §12.7's REQUEST_REJECTED rule as the more specific, EP0-scoped override that governs for exactly this residual case. rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() now returns RCP_LIFECYCLE_REJECT (not RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP) for a non-ABB message addressed to EP0 in HW_CONFIGURED -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-033's own entry for the implementation detail, and that function's own header doc comment for the full reconciliation between the two TC18 sections.

requirements.title: In HW_CONFIGURED, EP0 write access to another endpoint's configuration requires the root client or the discovery stream
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.3.1.2 permits cross-endpoint write access via EP0 in HW_CONFIGURED only for a configured root client or via the discovery stream. rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() now gates RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W's HW_CONFIGURED branch on `authorized || writer.via_discovery_stream`, where authorized is the same via_root_client_ep0 || via_owning_stream formula already used for RCP_CONFIGURED, and via_discovery_stream is a new rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t member (REQ-LIFECYCLE-036 closed the same gate for FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR in the same change, since both requirements reduce to the identical HW_CONFIGURED authorization condition).

requirements.title: A lifecycle-state write is accepted only from the discovery stream, the root client, or (with no root client) any valid stream
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_lifecycle_transition() now takes an rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t and rejects an unauthorized writer's request (RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_UNAUTHORIZED) for both the HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED advance and either reset-to-HW_UNCONFIGURED transition, requiring writer.via_discovery_stream or writer.via_root_client_ep0 (the new via_discovery_stream member added to rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t in the same change). Not fully closed: TC18 §12.3.1.2's exact text further narrows the non-discovery-stream case -- "If a root client is configured only the root client's stream_id/byte_bus_id is accepted" -- implying any valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination should suffice when no root client is configured at all, a distinction this library cannot yet express (no wire-level concept of "a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination" independent of a specific endpoint's own owning stream exists for a server-level field like svr_lifecycle_state; same underlying architecture gap as REQ-LIFECYCLE-025/034). This function conservatively requires via_root_client_ep0 in both cases until that classification exists, rather than accepting an unqualified stream it cannot actually validate.

requirements.title: In HW_CONFIGURED, non-configuration requests to endpoints other than EP0 are dropped
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP has no wire-level encode/decode pair for a functional-configuration read/write request at all, for any endpoint type -- regmap.h's own file header documents this as deliberately deferred ("wiring them to an actual byte_message_info read/write exchange is later phases' job"), confirmed by grepping the whole codebase for any regmap encode/decode pair and finding none outside discovery.c's own read-only discovery-response encoder. Every wire request this library can currently decode for a non-EP0 endpoint is therefore, by construction, operational -- so rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() now restricts HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID (EP0) only, the honestly-achievable form of TC18 §12.3.1.2's "requests to EPs other than EP0 that are not config requests will be ignored and dropped without response" given this library's real current wire-format scope. Migrating this restriction into rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() required moving test_mock.c's and test_conditional_dispatch.c's own dispatch fixtures from HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_CONFIGURED (both files' fixtures dispatch to non-EP0 endpoints as their normal, unremarkable test setup, not gap-specific behavior).

requirements.title: Non-STANDARD requests to EP0 before full configuration must be answered with REQUEST_REJECTED, not dropped
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: primary-source re-verification found the RCP_SCHED_KIND_* input this entry's own text said was needed is unnecessary machinery -- STANDARD-vs-conditional is already fully determined by the acf_msg_type parameter rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() already receives (ACF_ABB is this codebase's wire encoding for STANDARD requests; ACF_GBB is the encoding for every conditional request kind -- compound/compound-wait/triggered/chained/timed/cancel -- unconditionally, per request_compound.h and siblings' own mtv-repurposing scheme). Fixed: rcp_lifecycle_should_accept()'s bool return widened to a three-way rcp_lifecycle_accept_t (ACCEPT/DROP/REJECT); a non-ABB message type addressed to EP0 (RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID) while HW_UNCONFIGURED, or while HW_CONFIGURED (this library's own architecture makes TC18's "no valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations have been defined" condition permanently true throughout HW_CONFIGURED, since no wire-level regmap read/write exists yet to ever establish one), now returns REJECT instead of the prior silent DROP. rcp_mock_server_dispatch() answers a REJECT with RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_REJECTED (wire code 11) via the same rcp_acf_build_error_response() convention find_slot()'s own EP_NOT_FOUND path already used, and returns the pre-existing RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_REJECTED result. This also resolves REQ-LIFECYCLE-029's own residual (see that entry) by treating §12.7's EP0-scoped REJECT as the more specific rule overriding §12.3.1.2's general ACF_GBB-drop rule for exactly this case.
requirements.tc18: §12.7 Configuration, TC18.txt L2454-2457

requirements.title: A direct-to-EP configuration request without a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id association must be dropped
requirements.text: PARTIAL: re-verified TC18.txt L2458-2459's exact wording directly against the primary-source PDF: "Configuration requests directly to EPs are only allowed In RCP_CONFIGURED or in HW_CONFIGURED with valid stream_id/byte_bus_id configuration. If the condition is not fulfilled, the request is dropped." Two distinct cases, read precisely: (a) in RCP_CONFIGURED, direct-to-EP configuration requests are allowed unconditionally by this sentence -- no per-request stream_id/byte_bus_id validity check is required here at all, so this requirement's own RCP_CONFIGURED half was mis-scoped in its original text; (b) in HW_CONFIGURED, a valid association is required. REQ-LIFECYCLE-032's already-merged fix (HW_CONFIGURED admits only byte_bus_id == EP0) satisfies (b) conservatively -- more strictly than §12.7 literally asks for (a properly-associated non-EP0 request would also now be dropped, not just an unassociated one), but this library has no wire-level regmap encode/decode for a functional-configuration request at all yet (regmap.h's own file header defers this), so no such properly-associated non-EP0 traffic can exist in this codebase's current scope regardless -- the over-restriction has no practical effect today and is the safe, conservative choice pending that missing capability. Genuinely open only for the theoretical future case once wire-level configuration requests exist; not an active gap given current scope.
requirements.tc18: §12.7 Configuration, TC18.txt L2458-2459 (re-verified against primary-source PDF)

requirements.title: In HW_UNCONFIGURED only the claimed discovery stream may configure the server
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: the same underlying gap as REQ-LIFECYCLE-026 (this entry's own "claimed discovery stream" framing and that entry's "discovery claimant's stream" framing describe one code path, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC's HW_UNCONFIGURED writability), closed by the same fix -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-026's own text for the full correction (the enforcement point is rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(), not rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() as originally assumed here too). rcp_discovery_claim_note_request()/rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant() (src/discovery.c) remain pure primitives a caller composes into writer.via_discovery_stream, per discovery.h's own documented architecture -- unchanged by this fix, and correctly so.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.2 Configuration in HW_UNCONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2488-2489

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED configuration access is restricted to the discovery stream or a known stream_id/byte_bus_id pair
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.3 permits configuration access in HW_CONFIGURED only (a) via a discovery request on the discovery stream, or (b) via a KNOWN stream_id/byte_bus_id combination addressed directly to the endpoint. rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() now gates both RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W and RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR's HW_CONFIGURED branches on `authorized || writer.via_discovery_stream` -- via_owning_stream (already-modeled) is (b)'s "known stream_id/byte_bus_id pair addressed directly to the endpoint", and the new via_discovery_stream member is (a). rcp_lifecycle_should_accept()'s own byte_bus_id acceptance is unaffected -- this requirement's substance is about write authorization, which is field_writable()'s layer, matching REQ-LIFECYCLE-030's identical HW_CONFIGURED condition (both closed in the same change).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.3 Configuration in HW_CONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2493-2494

requirements.title: Once RCP_CONFIGURED, a discovery request may no longer change configuration although it is still answered
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: primary-source re-verification found this entry had actually conflated two different things -- rcp_lifecycle_field_writable()'s FUNCTIONAL_W RCP_CONFIGURED branch already correctly excluded via_discovery_stream before this fix (authorized there is via_root_client_ep0 || via_owning_stream only), so field WRITES were never actually leaking discovery-stream authority into RCP_CONFIGURED. The real, confirmed gap was in rcp_lifecycle_transition()'s own RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset path: it shared one `authorized` (via_discovery_stream || via_root_client_ep0) computation with the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset, so a bare discovery-stream writer could still demote a fully RCP_CONFIGURED server -- itself a configuration change TC18 §12.7.4's "Changes in configuration via a discovery request are no longer allowed" forbids. Fixed: the RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset now requires writer.via_root_client_ep0 specifically (the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset keeps the wider rule, since §12.7.3 still permits the discovery stream while HW_CONFIGURED). rcp_discovery_claim_note_config_write()/rcp_discovery_claim_release() (src/discovery.c) remain pure claim-bookkeeping primitives that deliberately do not consult lifecycle state, per discovery.h's own documented architecture -- the claim primitive still refreshes for the claimant regardless of state, but that no longer translates into actual write or transition authority once RCP_CONFIGURED, since both real gates (field_writable() and transition()) now independently close that door.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.4 Configuration in RCP_CONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2498-2500

requirements.title: NOT IMPLEMENTED: RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT's own third plausibility bullet -- every configured request stream has at least one endpoint using it
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §12.3.1.2's RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT plausibility check names three bullets for the HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED transition: (1) "Each EP used has at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id association" -- REQ-LIFECYCLE-005/007; (2) "For each configured stream at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id is configured" -- the mirror-image completeness check, that no request stream is left configured with zero endpoints actually using it; (3) "Each response stream configured is assigned to at least one request stream" -- REQ-LIFECYCLE-006. Bullet 2 has no counterpart in rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg() at all: rcp_lifecycle_request_stream_plausibility_t carries only `configured` and `has_response_stream`, with no field representing whether any endpoint actually references that specific stream. A request stream marked `configured = true` with zero endpoints bound to it -- an orphaned, unused stream slot -- passes rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg() today exactly as if it were legitimately in use. Implementing this needs a new per-request-stream field (e.g. `has_bound_endpoint`) and a caller-supplied snapshot that actually cross-references endpoint-to-stream bindings, which this library's current single-flat-array snapshot model does not construct anywhere.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Only if the configuration so far is plausible the state will be advanced. Plausibility check contains a check that: ... For each configured stream at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id is configured ... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSITENT"), TC18.txt L2190-2196

requirements.title: PWM_OUT trigger events are derived from the skew-delayed signal and fire at 0% duty
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP enumerates the three TC18 Table 42 PWM_OUT trigger events (rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_t: DONE, CYCLE_START, MID_PULSE) and carries the pwmo_skew register, but implements neither of the two rules governing them -- that trigger signals are generated from the SKEW-DELAYED output rather than the undelayed one (TC18 13.7.5.1, the break-before-make provision for half/full-bridge drivers), and that the mid-active-pulse trigger fires even when the duty cycle is 0%.

requirements.title: PWM_OUT duty-cycle limits cap the requested active time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP stores pwmo_duty_cycle_min (0x000A) and pwmo_duty_cycle_max (0x000C) in rcp_ep_pwm_out_functional_cfg_t but applies neither -- TC18 Table 43 requires a request whose active time falls below the minimum or exceeds the maximum to be CAPPED to that limit (not rejected, and not applied verbatim). rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() computes the new (period, active_duration) pair without consulting either register.

requirements.title: PWM_OUT request semantics: stop on period 0, output-off on active 0, phase shift, readback check
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP applies none of TC18 13.7.5.3's four PWM_OUT request rules -- a request with PWM_Period == 0 shall stop signal generation; a request with PWM_active == 0 and PWM_Period > 0 shall keep the endpoint running with the output disabled while still generating trigger signals; a request that is a trigger configuration shall have its first two payload octets read as a PHASE SHIFT rather than a period (for fixed-phase synchronisation to another PWM_OUT endpoint); and during generation the output pin shall be read back and an error signaled if it does not actually toggle. rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() stores both fields verbatim.

requirements.title: PWM_IN functional-config register block (Table 45)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (FIXED 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): c-RCP's rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_t now models every TC18 Table 45 PWM_IN register -- pwmi_polarity, pwmi_err_on_max_period, pwmi_continuous_mode (packed into a new flags octet at 0x0009, RCP_EP_PWM_IN_FLAG_* masks), pwmi_max_period (0x000A-0x000B), pwmi_base_clk (0x0004-0x0005, read-only), pwmi_clk_divider (0x0008), and pwmi_ep_status (0x0006-0x0007) -- reachable via the same generic evt[2:0]=111b TC18 §12.7.1 register-block mechanism every other endpoint type now has: rcp_ep_pwm_in_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror()/_encode_reconfig_request(). This endpoint type had been silently omitted from every prior batch's own 'N of 11 endpoint types' accounting (REQ-CFG-011/REQ-CFG-012's own text counted the pwm.c module as fully done once PWM_OUT's own fix landed, without separately checking PWM_IN); see REQ-CFG-011's own corrected text. `trigger` remains a non-wire, module-own field; the measurement-timeout sentinel RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL is unrelated to the register block.

requirements.title: PWM_IN read-request decode validates evt[2:0]
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (FIXED 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_read_request() shall reject a frame whose evt[2:0] is not one of the plain-request values rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain() accepts, returning RCP_EP_PWM_IN_ERR_BAD_EVT -- matching the check every other endpoint type in this Table 30 grouping (ADC/I2C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO) already performs. Before this fix, this endpoint type never checked evt[2:0] at all: a real evt=111b configuration-write request from a conforming peer would have been silently misinterpreted as an ordinary read request rather than being rejected or routed to rcp_ep_pwm_in_apply_reconfig() -- a live conformance bug, distinct from (and worse than) every prior Group I register-block finding, which found only an unreachable path, never a misinterpreted one.

requirements.title: A cold start restores the configured lifecycle state, not always HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_cold_start_lifecycle_target() takes a required recovered_state parameter -- the caller's own already-recovered fact (this module owns no NVM access or default-configuration table of its own, the same convention as network_available) -- and returns it unchanged when it is one of lifecycle.h's three valid states, so a server that reached RCP_CONFIGURED before a power cycle no longer silently loses it; RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED remains the fail-safe default for a genuinely unconfigured device or a corrupt/unrecognized recovered_state.

requirements.title: Configuration data and wake sources survive StandBy
requirements.text: power.h owns no register-map or wake-source storage of its own (regmap.c/ep_wakeup.c do) -- the guarantee this library actually provides, and the only one it architecturally can, is that rcp_pwrmode_transition() correctly and always classifies Normal<->StandBy RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT, now stated explicitly as a retention obligation on RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT's own doc comment: a caller withholding re-init on HOT (per that documented contract) never has a reason to touch either structure, so both survive by construction, not merely by omission.

requirements.title: Hot start checks network availability before sending a WakeUp
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled() now takes a network_available bool (this codebase's established "caller supplies already-classified inputs" convention -- this module reads no hardware itself, e.g. BEACON detection). A false network_available leaves hs at RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_NOT_STARTED (a cheap, uncounted "not yet" a caller polls again, not a failure) and does not advance the handshake, so rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt() -- which requires RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_IFACE_REENABLED -- cannot be driven, and its own wakeup_repeat_limit budget is never touched, until the network is actually available. rcp_powerstate_manager_handshake_begin() (powerstate.c, the client-side convenience wrapper) threads the same network_available parameter through to its own caller.

requirements.title: The wake response is sent on the responder stream configured for the original sleep/standby request
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: rcp_powerstate_manager_handshake_begin() (powerstate.c) now takes a required resp_stream_id parameter (this codebase's established "caller supplies already-classified inputs" convention -- this module owns no register-map instance and no transport of its own, so it cannot itself resolve which response stream regmap.h's request_stream_cfg/response_queue_cfg pairing designates; the caller, which does have that access, resolves and supplies it). Recorded per-addr alongside the handshake itself; a new rcp_powerstate_manager_wake_response_stream_id() getter returns it so a caller transmits rcp_powerstate_manager_encode_wakeup_probe()'s own output (and the eventual wake notification) on the correct stream rather than assuming addr's own request stream, which TC18 does not guarantee are the same stream.

requirements.title: WakeUp repetition stops on any valid AVTPDU from the sleep-request client
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (documentation/citation correction, no logic change needed): re-verification found rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt()'s own `echoed` bool was already sufficiently generic -- it is a plain caller-supplied bool, not itself hardwired to rcp_ep_wakeup_is_wakeup_echo(). powerstate.c's rcp_powerstate_manager_apply_wakeup_echo() is the ONE caller that narrows it to a literal WakeUp echo, but that function's own scope was always meant to be a specific convenience wrapper, not the sole way to satisfy step (b) -- a caller recognizing some other valid, already-demultiplexed frame from the sleep-request client may call rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt() directly with echoed=true for that case instead, matching TC18 §12.4.1's actual "a valid AVTPDU from the sleep request Client" termination condition exactly. Both functions' own doc comments now state this explicitly. The repeat-limit framing this entry's own text already asked for was already correct and unchanged: wakeup_repeat_limit/RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_FAILED are this implementation's own added safety bound, not spec-derived -- TC18 itself defines no limit.

requirements.title: Completing the wake handshake re-enables every used endpoint and response queue
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_resume_queues() (power.h) deliberately advances only a state enum -- power.h's own file header states it never touches server.h at all, matching this codebase's established "pure primitive, caller composes" layering (lifecycle.h/discovery.h use the identical pattern). The composition this requirement actually needs now lives at mock.h's new rcp_mock_server_pwrmode_resume(srv, hs): calls resume_queues(hs) first, then (iff it succeeds) calls rcp_server_endpoint_set_enable() on every registered endpoint, closing TC18 §12.4.1's "all used endpoints... will be enabled" for this test double. Still not modeled anywhere in this codebase: response-queue objects (rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t is inert, no STREAM_UID/queue_size/storage -- see test_response_queue_has_no_identity_size_or_storage()) and heartbeat-stream re-emission (see test_flush_triggers_and_heartbeat_are_absent()) -- both separate, already-tracked architecture gaps this fix cannot close, so "response queue"/heartbeat resumption remains genuinely unimplemented.

requirements.title: A network wake runs the same hot-start handshake a pin wake does, not a bypass
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: rcp_pwrmode_hotstart_required() (REQ-PWRMODE-005) now returns true unconditionally, so rcp_pwrmode_wake_from_sleep() classifies RCP_PWRMODE_WAKE_VIA_NETWORK by the same handshake-completion rule RCP_PWRMODE_WAKE_VIA_PIN already used, matching TC18 §12.4.1's own "proceed as before" text -- a network-woken server now runs the WakeUp-repetition exchange (steps b/c) and is no longer classified hot before the sleeping client has actually been told it is awake. power.h's own state machine still requires a step-(a) rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled() call before step (b) can run for either path, unchanged -- the spec's own nuance (a network wake's network-availability check is trivially satisfied, since the wake arrived via the network in the first place) does not need separate modeling here: no literal hardware action is implied by that call for either path, only a state-machine precondition. A second call site, powerstate.c's rcp_powerstate_manager_wake_via_network() (the legacy client-side convenience wrapper's own "always hot for network" contract), now synthesizes and immediately completes a handshake locally to preserve that documented contract against power.h's corrected primitive -- see that function's own doc comment.

requirements.title: StandBy is entered only in response to an RCP request, never from a network signal
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_network_sleep() is the sole entry point a caller integrating a real TC14/TC10 network signal uses, and it has no target-mode parameter at all -- unlike rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry(), which the SleepCMD (RCP-request) path uses. The only power mode a network trigger can ever produce is RCP_PWRMODE_SLEEP, making the StandBy exclusivity impossible to violate by construction rather than merely true by omission (there being no network path modelled at all, the prior state).

requirements.title: Sleep can also be initiated by a valid network TC14/TC10 sleep request
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_network_sleep(mode, gate, response_sent, out_start_kind) delegates to the same rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry() a normal (RCP-request) sleep entry uses, target fixed to RCP_PWRMODE_SLEEP -- 'the same conditions apply as for a normal sleep request' (TC18's own text). TC14/TC10 sleep signaling is PHY/MAC-level out-of-band control, not an RCP/ACF wire message this library's decode layer could ever parse; matching rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled()'s own network_available convention, a caller supplies 'a valid TC14/TC10 sleep request was received' as an already-classified fact simply by calling this function, with no frame/byte-buffer parameter to give since none exists for this library to inspect.

requirements.title: A sleep/standby request from an authorized client applies to the entire RC Server
requirements.text: c-RCP gates SleepCMD admission on client authorization via ep_wakeup.h's rcp_ep_wakeup_sleepcmd_writable() (true iff writer.via_root_client_ep0, mirroring rcp_lifecycle_transition()'s own RCP_CONFIGURED-state root-client rule) before power.h's rcp_pwrmode_check_entry()/rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry() is ever consulted. Those two functions operate on a single rcp_pwrmode_t, this module's existing whole-server mode representation, not a per-endpoint one -- a real server-side composition points *mode at its own one server-wide variable, satisfying TC18's 'entire RC Server implementation' wording by construction. rcp_powerstate_manager_t's own per-addr mode tracking (unchanged) is this library's CLIENT-side bookkeeping of multiple distinct remote peers, not a per-endpoint model of one server's own state.

requirements.title: A wake-source event during sleep-request processing aborts the sleep entry
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry() re-validates a freshly re-sampled rcp_pwrmode_entry_gate_t (via rcp_pwrmode_check_entry() internally) immediately before the mode actually changes -- a caller that admitted the request against a gate sampled at arrival time and re-samples it again just before committing sees any wake-source event that occurred in between, refuses the entry (RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_ENTRY_REFUSED), and leaves the mode unchanged, closing the lost-wakeup race a single up-front rcp_pwrmode_check_entry() call would leave open.

requirements.title: The sleep/standby refusal conditions are evaluated server-wide, across every EP and every responder queue
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_entry_gate_t.endpoint_idle/.response_queue_empty are documented as server-wide aggregates -- true iff EVERY endpoint/responder queue on the RC Server is idle/empty, not just the endpoint the request arrived on -- matching TC18 §12.5's 'AT LEAST ONE EP is not idle' / 'AT LEAST ONE responder queue' refusal conditions. Both fields were always caller-supplied opaque bools with no code-level scope restriction; the pre-fix reading of their doc comments (worded around a single wake-up endpoint) was the actual gap, not rcp_pwrmode_check_entry()'s own logic, which already ANDs whatever the caller supplies.

requirements.title: The mode change happens only after the sleep/standby response has been transmitted
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry() takes a required response_sent bool and refuses the entry (RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_ENTRY_REFUSED, mode left unchanged) unless it is true, mirroring rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled()'s own network_available convention -- this library does no I/O of its own and cannot observe transmission completion directly, so response_sent is the caller's own proof that the sleep/standby response has actually been transmitted before the mode transition it gates is permitted to run.

requirements.title: A refused network sleep request suppresses the TC14/TC10 LPS confirmation
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_network_sleep() has no PHY-signalling surface of its own (this library never touches hardware, the same scoping precedent as network_available), so its RCP_PWRMODE_OK vs. RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_ENTRY_REFUSED return value IS the confirmation signal: a caller integrating a real TC14/TC10 PHY asserts LPS only on RCP_PWRMODE_OK, never on RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_ENTRY_REFUSED, honouring 'the network PHY shall not signal a TC14/TC10 LPS as confirmation' when the go-to-sleep conditions are not fulfilled.

requirements.title: Sleep-request processing order: stop admitting requests, drain, then acknowledge
requirements.text: server.h's rcp_server_endpoint_t gains an admission_suspended flag (default false, additive) and rcp_server_endpoint_set_admission_suspended() setter; rcp_server_endpoint_admit() checks it first, before inspecting the arriving frame at all, and returns the new RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_SUSPENDED outcome -- neither queued nor executed -- implementing TC18 13.7.2.3 step 1 ("stop entering incoming requests into endpoint queues") ahead of step 3's preconditions (rcp_pwrmode_check_entry()/rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry(), REQ-PWRMODE-024/026), which a caller already evaluates during the same drain.

requirements.title: The lifecycle state is exposed as the svr_lifecycle_state register-map entry
requirements.text: PARTIAL: the lifecycle state must be exposed as a register-map entry (TC18 §12.3.1.1, §12.3.1.2, §12.4.1). rcp_regmap_general_t now carries a svr_lifecycle_state field (content modeling only), kept in sync with the authoritative rcp_lifecycle_state_t by rcp_mock_server_transition() -- the one caller today composing rcp_lifecycle_transition() with a regmap.h general block -- on every transition attempt, success or failure. What remains open: REQ-RMAP-024 (the general Table 18 register map's own wire-reachability gap) is now CLOSED, but that closure deliberately does not reach this field -- svr_lifecycle_state has no genuine TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 address at all (confirmed directly against the primary source), so rcp_regmap_general_render() never serializes it. Its real home is TC18 §13.7.1.2 Table 33 (the RC Server's own EP_FUNC_config block, a separate register space), still unimplemented (REQ-RMAP-067). A remote client therefore still cannot read this server's readiness or drive a transition by writing it over the wire -- only in-process consumers of the field can.

requirements.title: The RC Server general register map's full Table 18 extent is now reachable on the wire, not just the first 14 octets
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP now exposes the RC Server general register map's full TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 extent (RCP_REGMAP_GENERAL_LEN, 0x0000..0x003F) over ACF_ABB via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response()/_decode_read_response() (include/rcp/regmap.h, src/regmap.c) -- the same read mechanism rcp_discovery_encode_response() already used for its own narrower, still-unchanged 14-octet identity slice (RCP_DISCOVERY_GENERAL_SLICE_LEN), generalized to serve every field at its own TC18-documented address; a read_size shorter than the full extent still works, carrying only a prefix (matching every other register-block decoder's own partial-population convention). Two struct fields, svr_lifecycle_state and svr_root_client_index, have no genuine Table 18 address (confirmed directly against the primary source: Table 18's own address sequence has no room for either) and are deliberately excluded from this render/decode pair, not force-mapped onto an invented address -- their real home is TC18 §13.7.1.2 Table 33 (the RC Server's own EP_FUNC_config block, a separate register space reached via §12.7.1's own pointer-addressed mechanism), still unimplemented (REQ-RMAP-023, REQ-RMAP-067). Write access is also now dispatched: rcp_regmap_general_decode_write_request() recognizes any ACF_ABB WRITE addressed to EP0 and reports RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS every time, via lifecycle.h's already-proven RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_READ_ONLY primitive (REQ-RMAP-025). EP0 is now a genuinely addressable, read/write-dispatched register space for its Table 18 extent, closing this requirement's own scope.
requirements.tc18: §12.7 Configuration, TC18.txt L2452-2453

requirements.title: Every register in the RC Server static part is read-only to a remote client
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 marks every register of the RC Server general (static) part with access type R — a remote write to any of them must not take effect. rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() (src/lifecycle.c) models this as its own explicit kind, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_READ_ONLY: unconditionally unwritable in every lifecycle state, by every writer (proven for a maximally-privileged writer too, not just an unprivileged one), and rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error() correctly reports RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS for it (never RCP_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS, since no writer condition is ever consulted). A real wire write path now exists and consults it: rcp_regmap_general_decode_write_request() (regmap.h/regmap.c) recognizes any ACF_ABB WRITE addressed to EP0 targeting the general register map and reports RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS every time, reusing (not duplicating) this same primitive -- closing the live-enforcement gap this requirement previously left open. rcp_mock_server_regmap() itself still hands back a directly mutable in-process pointer, a deliberate, separate design choice for that test double's own convenience API, not a remaining conformance gap: no code path routes a real wire write through it.

requirements.title: svr_req_stream_max (0x000E) is the wrong width and svr_responder_streams_max (0x000F) is missing
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_req_stream_max as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x000E (maximum number of request streams usable to access this RC Server) and svr_responder_streams_max as an 8-bit read-only register at 0x000F (maximum number of supported responder queues for response and acknowledge traffic). rcp_regmap_general_t declares both at the correct width: svr_req_stream_max (uint8_t, renamed from this field's own former name svr_max_request_streams to match TC18's own register name) and the previously-missing svr_responder_streams_max (uint8_t). A value neither register's own 8-bit width could hold on the wire can no longer be constructed in the first place, and both are now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response() at their own TC18-cited addresses.

requirements.title: The two memory-capacity registers svr_responder_mem_size (0x0010) and svr_req_mem_size (0x0012) are missing
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines two distinct 16-bit read-only capacity registers, both counted in 32-bit words: svr_responder_mem_size at absolute address 0x0010 (maximum responder-queue memory) and svr_req_mem_size at 0x0012 (maximum memory for EP request queues). rcp_regmap_general_t models both distinctly, replacing the former undifferentiated 32-bit svr_memory_capacity field that conflated them into one unaddressed field with no unit, and both are now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response() at their own TC18-cited addresses.

requirements.title: svr_sequencers_max (0x0014) is 16-bit and its 0-means-unsupported encoding is unenforced
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_sequencers_max as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0014 whose value 0 means sequencer operation is not supported and whose values 1..n give the number of available sequencer state registers. rcp_regmap_general_t declares svr_sequencers_max at the correct 8-bit width (renamed from this field's own former name svr_max_sequencers), and mock.c's rcp_mock_server_set_sequencer_count() keeps it synced with the actual rcp_sequencer_table_t.count it allocates -- request_sequencer.h's own rcp_sequencer_table_unsupported() (table->count == 0) already implements the "0 means unsupported" rule this register describes, so once synced, the register correctly reflects that same rule by construction, and the address (0x0014) is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response().

requirements.title: svr_configuration_lock (0x0015) is entirely missing, so R/W+ writes are never lock-gated
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_configuration_lock as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0015 whose value 0x00 permits write access to "R/W+" type parameters and whose every other value causes such write access to be rejected. rcp_regmap_general_t declares this field (content modeling), zero-initializing to 0x00 (the correct unlocked default), and it is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). This requirement's own scope is the register's existence, default, and wire-reachability, all now satisfied. What remains open, tracked separately: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() (src/lifecycle.c) still grants or denies RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR writes purely from lifecycle state and writer context, with no lock input, so a device that has latched its configuration still cannot have that latch actually enforced -- deliberately deferred to REQ-RMAP-055 (issue #200 Group 3), this codebase's own already-identified "shared plumbing, implement once" home for the W+ lockable-access-type primitive Table 23's EP_ID_config rows and Table 24's queue registers also need identically, rather than building a redundant, table-specific check here ahead of that shared work.

requirements.title: svr_implemented_options (0x0016) is now 8-bit, five independent bits, matching Table 18 exactly (formerly an invented 32-bit, six-bit, three-pair design)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_implemented_options as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0016 with one independent bit per optional feature: a = compound & wait requests, b = trigger requests, c = chained requests, d = time synch and timed requests, e = enhanced request cancellation (bits f/g/h reserved). rcp_regmap_general_t declares this field at its correct 8-bit width, with RCP_REGMAP_OPT_COMPOUND_WAIT/_TRIGGER/_CHAINED/_TIME_SYNC/_ENH_CANCEL (include/rcp/regmap.h) at bit values 0x01/0x02/0x04/0x08/0x10 -- five independent bits, verified directly against the primary-source PDF (OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf, Table 18, page 51). This replaces a prior 32-bit field carrying six bits of this project's own invention, grouped into three all-or-nothing pairs and enforced by rcp_regmap_options_group_consistent() (both removed outright; see REQ-RMAP-004..008's own retirement text for the primary-source finding that invalidated their shared citation). This also closed a real, previously-unadvertised capability gap: c-RCP has always implemented both trigger requests (src/request_triggered.c) and chained requests (src/request_chained.c) in full, but the prior design had no bit for either -- a conforming client had no way to learn c-RCP supports them. All three real consumers use the new bits: rcp_timed_feature_enabled() (src/request_timed.c, checks RCP_REGMAP_OPT_TIME_SYNC), the CLI's capabilities_json() "features" array (src/cli.c, RCP_CLI_IMPLEMENTED_OPTIONS macro), and the config manifest parser's "svr_implemented_options" array (src/config.c, OPTION_BIT_NAMES table, now including "trigger"/"chained" names). This address (0x0016) is now wire-reachable too (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response().
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 18, TC18.txt L2554-2560 -- primary-source-verified against OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf Table 18, page 51, and §12.9.1.1, page 64 (this milestone)

requirements.title: The reserved octet at 0x0017 is now explicitly modeled and reads 0x00
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 reserves the 8-bit register at absolute address 0x0017 and requires it to read 0x00. rcp_regmap_general_t declares an explicit reserved_0x17 field for this octet, zero-initializing for free via the existing memset in rcp_regmap_general_init(); no setter exists anywhere in this codebase to construct a nonzero value. This documents the octet as deliberately reserved (not merely forgotten), and this address (0x0017) is now genuinely wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed): rcp_regmap_general_render() writes 0x00 there for real, dispatched via rcp_regmap_general_encode_read_response(), not merely produced by a generic zero-filled buffer beyond a truncated slice.

requirements.title: svr_io_pin_count (0x0018) is now explicitly modeled, so the HW_config table has a declared extent
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_io_pin_count as a 16-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0018 giving the number of assignable I/O pins, and §12.7.6 makes it the authoritative source for how many IO-pin entries the HW_config table (Table 19) contains. rcp_regmap_general_t declares this field, and it is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). What remains open: nothing in this codebase yet allocates or bounds a real HW_config table against this count -- that is Group 2's own still-open scope (issue #200 items REQ-RMAP-040 through REQ-RMAP-045), so this register is wire-readable but has nothing real to describe yet.

requirements.title: svr_hw_cfg_ptr (0x001A) is now correctly shaped, a bare 16-bit pointer with no spurious capacity
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_hw_cfg_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer register at absolute address 0x001A, giving the address of the HW_config register map of §12.7.6. rcp_regmap_general_t declares this field as svr_hw_cfg_ptr, a bare uint16_t matching TC18's own width exactly -- replacing the former rcp_regmap_table_ref_t representation, whose offset member was a 32-bit value expressed in this implementation's own "register words" rather than a 16-bit register-map address, and which carried an extra capacity member that TC18 does not define for this table (HW_config's extent is svr_io_pin_count at 0x0018, REQ-RMAP-032). This address (0x001A) is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). What remains open: this codebase has no real HW_config table storage anywhere yet for this pointer to meaningfully address (Group 2's own separate, still-open scope, REQ-RMAP-040 through REQ-RMAP-045) -- the pointer is wire-readable but currently always reads 0.

requirements.title: The request/response stream config pointer and capacity registers are now correctly sized and separately addressed
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines four separate registers for the stream-configuration sub-tables — svr_request_stream_cfg_capacity (8 bit, 0x001C), svr_response_stream_cfg_capacity (8 bit, 0x001D), svr_request_stream_cfg_ptr (16 bit, 0x001E) and svr_response_stream_cfg_ptr (16 bit, 0x0020). rcp_regmap_general_t declares these as four correctly-sized scalar fields, replacing the former request_stream_cfg/response_queue_cfg pair (each an rcp_regmap_table_ref_t, the shared pointer/capacity type most sub-table refs still use) whose 32-bit word-unit offset and 16-bit capacity could not represent TC18's own narrower widths or be encoded into their real wire slots without an unwritten unit conversion — the same class of fix REQ-RMAP-033 applied to svr_hw_cfg_ptr, here doubled across both stream directions. This address range (0x001C-0x0021) is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). What remains open: this codebase has no real request-stream or response/ack-stream config table storage anywhere yet for these pointers to meaningfully address -- they are wire-readable but currently always read 0.

requirements.title: The reserved 16-bit register at 0x0022 is now explicitly modeled and preserved as reserved
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 reserves the 16-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0022. rcp_regmap_general_t declares an explicit reserved_0x22 field for this span, zero-initializing for free via the existing memset in rcp_regmap_general_init(); no setter exists anywhere in this codebase to construct a nonzero value. This documents the span as deliberately reserved (not merely forgotten), matching the reserved_0x17 precedent (REQ-RMAP-031), and this address (0x0022) is now genuinely wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed): rcp_regmap_general_render() writes 0x00 there for real, dispatched via rcp_regmap_general_encode_read_response(), not merely produced by a generic zero-filled buffer beyond a truncated slice.

requirements.title: svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr/_capacity are now correctly sized, addressed, and unit-correct
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at absolute address 0x0024 to the generic endpoint register map (§13.2), and svr_ep_generic_cfg_capacity as a 16-bit read-only register at 0x0026 giving the LENGTH OF THE EP CONFIG REGISTER SECTION IN BYTES (re-verified directly against the primary-source PDF, Table 18 page 52, per this requirement's own flagged need for careful re-reading before fixing). rcp_regmap_general_t declares both as correctly-sized, correctly-UNITED scalar fields, replacing the former ep_generic_cfg field (rcp_regmap_table_ref_t, the shared pointer/capacity type most remaining sub-table refs still use) whose capacity member was documented as an ENTRY COUNT -- the exact opposite unit from what 0x0026 actually is. This was a genuine semantic contradiction, not merely a width/address mismatch like REQ-RMAP-033/-034. This address range (0x0024-0x0027) is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). What remains open: this codebase has no real EP_config table storage anywhere yet for this pointer to meaningfully address -- it is wire-readable but currently always reads 0.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 18, TC18.txt L2600-2603 -- primary-source-verified against OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf Table 18, page 52

requirements.title: svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr/_capacity are now correctly sized and separately addressed
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at absolute address 0x0028 to the EP-to-byte_bus_id mapping table, and svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_capacity as an 8-bit read-only register at 0x002A giving that table's maximum entry count (re-verified directly against the primary-source PDF, Table 18 page 52, during REQ-RMAP-036's own batch). rcp_regmap_general_t declares both as correctly-sized scalar fields, replacing the former ep_id_bus_map field (rcp_regmap_table_ref_t, the shared pointer/capacity type most remaining sub-table refs still use) whose 32-bit word-unit offset and 16-bit capacity could not represent TC18's own narrower widths or be encoded into their real wire slots without an unwritten unit conversion -- the same class of fix REQ-RMAP-033/-034 already applied (unlike REQ-RMAP-036, this capacity really is an entry count, matching the former shared field's own documented meaning -- no semantic contradiction to resolve here). This address range (0x0028-0x002A) is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). What remains open: this codebase has no real EP-byte_bus_id mapping table storage anywhere yet for this pointer to meaningfully address -- it is wire-readable but currently always reads 0.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 18, TC18.txt L2604-2609 -- primary-source-verified against OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf Table 18, page 52

requirements.title: svr_ep_functional_cfg_ptr/svr_sequencer_state_ptr are now correctly sized and separately addressed
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 defines svr_ep_functional_cfg_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at absolute address 0x002C to the EP_FUNC_config register map, and svr_sequencer_state_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at 0x002E to the sequencer state registers (§12.7.10) -- both lone pointers, with no adjacent capacity register defined for either (re-verified directly against the primary-source PDF, Table 18 page 52, during REQ-RMAP-036's own batch). rcp_regmap_general_t declares both as bare, correctly-sized scalar fields, replacing the former ep_functional_cfg/sequencer_state fields (rcp_regmap_table_ref_t, the shared pointer/capacity type -- now unused by any field in this struct, since every one of the seven original sub-table refs has been retyped across REQ-RMAP-033/-034/-036/-037/-038) whose 32-bit offset and spurious capacity member had no TC18 basis for either register -- the same class of fix REQ-RMAP-033 already established for svr_hw_cfg_ptr. This address range (0x002C-0x002F) is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). What remains open: this codebase has no real EP_FUNC_config or Sequencer_config table storage anywhere yet for either pointer to meaningfully address -- both are wire-readable but currently always read 0.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 18, TC18.txt L2610-2615 -- primary-source-verified against OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf Table 18, page 52

requirements.title: All four optional-subsystem pointer/capacity register pairs (network, physical layer, time synch, security) are now declared
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18's continued part defines four further 16-bit read-only pointer/capacity register pairs in the RC Server general register map — svr_network_interface_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.11), svr_physical_layer_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.12), svr_time_synch_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.13) and svr_security_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.14) — where a pointer value of 0 is the defined encoding for "this subsystem is not supported" for the physical-layer, time-synch and security pointers (TC18's own table gives no such note for the network-interface pointer). rcp_regmap_general_t declares all eight registers, closing Group 1's last item (issue #200); each pair is its own independent 16-bit ptr/capacity scalar pair, not the shared rcp_regmap_table_ref_t type (already unused elsewhere in this struct as of REQ-RMAP-038). Re-verified directly against the primary-source PDF a second time for this batch specifically (Table 18, page 53 of OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf): the table's own "Absolute address" column is genuinely BLANK for all eight registers on this continuation page — a real gap in the primary source itself, not an extraction failure — so this codebase's own relative addresses (0x0030 through 0x003F) are INFERRED (from the visible 0x0030 continuation marker after svr_sequencer_state_ptr's own 0x002E-0x002F, plus this table's consistent, gap-free sequential-address convention observed without exception everywhere else), not directly read; flagged honestly in the field comments rather than presented as spec-confirmed. This address range (0x0030-0x003F) is now wire-reachable at those inferred addresses (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). What remains open: this codebase has no real Network_config/physical-layer/PTP_config/security-configuration table storage anywhere yet for any of the four pointers to meaningfully address -- all four are wire-readable but currently always read 0.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 18 (continued), TC18.txt L2635-2659 -- primary-source-verified against OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf Table 18, page 53 (address column confirmed blank in the primary source itself; relative addresses INFERRED, not directly read)

requirements.title: No HW_config table exists to hold per-IO-pin endpoint-signal assignments
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.6 requires a table holding, for each used physical IO-pin, its mapping to an endpoint signal and its IO-pin properties, defaulting at the factory to no assignment at all. Real server-side storage exists (rcp_mock_server_t's own bounded rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_entry_t table, mock.h/mock.c). RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301): the addressing question this entry's own prior text called genuinely unresolved is now answered -- direct verification of the current RC5 baseline PDF (page 61) shows Table 18's own address column is headed "Absolute address", confirming svr_hw_cfg_ptr's own value is an absolute address in the same EP0-scoped space Table 18 itself lives in; a client reaches HW_config via an ordinary evt[2:0]=111b request to byte_bus_id=0 with start_address = svr_hw_cfg_ptr's current value plus an offset. rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() (regmap.h/regmap.c) now implements exactly this: it routes an incoming write by absolute address across Table 18's own extent (always denied, reusing REQ-RMAP-025's own logic) and HW_config's own extent (applied via the new rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_apply_reconfig(), the parse-side inverse of rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_render()). READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() (regmap.h/regmap.c) is the read-side counterpart to the write dispatcher, routing an incoming read's own address across the identical extents and reusing rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_render() directly -- a client can now write AND read HW_config over the wire. STILL OPEN: this dispatcher (both directions) does not itself consult rcp_lifecycle_field_writable()/RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC (TC18's own "only changeable in HW_UNCONFIGURED" rule) -- that authorization gate remains deferred to whatever caller eventually owns lifecycle-state context, matching REQ-RMAP-025's own established precedent for the general map's own write path.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 HW pin mapping configuration, TC18.txt L2691-2695

requirements.title: HW_config rows are 3 octets per IO pin at relative addresses 3*N, 3*N+1, 3*N+2
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.6 Table 19/21 (renumbered to Table 21 in the current RC5 baseline) lays the HW_config map out as three consecutive 8-bit R/W* registers per physical IO pin — hw_ep_nr, hw_ep_pin_nr, hw_pin_type — so that IO_Pin 1 occupies relative addresses 0x0000/0x0001/0x0002, IO_Pin 2 occupies 0x0003/0x0004/0x0005, IO_Pin 3 begins at 0x0006, and IO pin N begins at relative address 3*N (relative to HW_config's own start, i.e. to svr_hw_cfg_ptr's own current value -- confirmed correct against the current PDF's own "Relative Address" column header for this table, unlike Table 18's own, differently-headed column, see REQ-RMAP-040's own text). c-RCP's row already carried the three correctly-typed, correctly-named fields. rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_render() serializes a real table at exactly this 3*N stride. RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301): the ACF_ABB WRITE wrapper this entry's own prior text called missing now exists -- rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_apply_reconfig() (the parse-side inverse of render(), patch-then-reparse idiom matching every other endpoint type's own apply_reconfig()) plus rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()'s own address-routing to it. READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() serves this exact stride back over the wire, reusing rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_render() directly -- see REQ-RMAP-040's own text for the full read-side detail. STILL OPEN: no setter routes a write through rcp_lifecycle_field_writable()/RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC to enforce the R/W* (HW_unconfigured-only) access type -- see REQ-RMAP-040's own text for why that gate is deliberately deferred rather than added ad hoc.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 19: HW_config, TC18.txt L2698-2717

requirements.title: hw_pin_type now matches Table 20's own four-packed-sub-field bit layout
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 Table 20 defines the hw_pin_type octet as four packed sub-fields — Pull at bits 1:0 (00b float, 01b pull down, 10b pull up), Output stage at bits 3:2 (00b input, 01b open drain, 10b open source, 11b push pull), Drive strength at bits 5:4 (00b input, 01b low, 10b medium, 11b high), reserved bit 6 reading 0, and Schmitt-Trigger enable at bit 7. Fixed: rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_entry_t's own third field (renamed pin_property -> hw_pin_type, matching the wire register's own name) now uses a dedicated RCP_REGMAP_HW_PIN_* constant family at exactly these bit positions, primary-source verified directly against the TC18 v0.5.1_RC PDF (pdftotext -layout extraction, since no local TC18.txt was found this session). This is a distinct, separately-named family from RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_* (ep_gpio.h's own, differently-shaped, per-pin runtime-adjustable field, REQ-GPIO-013 -- deliberately left untouched by this fix, since they are two different registers that happened to share one set of bit-position constants, not one register two ways). config.h/config.c's manifest JSON schema updated to match (hw_pin_map entries now use "hw_pin_type": [...] with Table-20-derived string values -- pull_down/pull_up, open_drain/open_source/push_pull, low_drive/medium_drive/high_drive, schmitt_trigger -- rather than the old six one-hot names).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 20: IO-pin properties, TC18.txt L2738-2759

requirements.title: hw_pin_type's output stage has no separate, exclusive input flag to toggle away from
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 states that the pin direction/drive entry is split into exactly four sub-fields (pull resistor, output stage, drive strength, Schmitt-trigger) and that ALL OUTPUTS ARE ALWAYS ALSO AN INPUT — output and input are not mutually exclusive pin states. Fixed: hw_pin_type's own output-stage field (RCP_REGMAP_HW_PIN_STAGE_*, REQ-RMAP-042) selects one of four drive modes (input/open-drain/open-source/push-pull) rather than toggling a separate exclusive INPUT/OUTPUT flag pair the way the old shared RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_OUTPUT/_INPUT bits did -- there is structurally no "pure output, unreadable" state to represent, matching TC18's own prose exactly. Still open, and NOT resolved by this fix: ep_gpio.h's own, separate pin_property field and rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig()'s OUTPUT<->INPUT toggle (REQ-GPIO-013) still have this exact problem for GPIO's own runtime-adjustable per-pin state -- that is a different register (this table's own hw_pin_type has no runtime-write path of its own at all, REQ-RMAP-041) with its own separate architecture question, not resolved here; see this session's own investigation note on issue #200 for the full analysis, including the discovery that GPIO's evt[2:0]=111b write semantics (RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_RECONFIG) itself appears to deviate from TC18's own generic EP_func-block-write definition (§12.7.1/Figure 18), a larger, separate finding.

requirements.title: The EP_Signal_Nr enumeration now covers every endpoint type
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 Table 21 enumerates the EP_Signal_Nr values for every endpoint type — GPIO 0..31; SPI 0..8 (CLK, PICO, POCI, CS0..CS5); I2C 0..1 (SCL, SDA); UART 0..3 (TX, RX, RTS, CTS); LIN 0..2 (TXD, RXD, NSLP); PWM_OUT 0..1 (positive phase, inverted phase); PWM_IN 0; ADC 0 (ADC_IN); DAC 0 (DAC_OUT); CAN 0 RXD and 1 TXD; ISELED 0 ISP_P and 1 ISP_N; MDIO 0 MDC and 1 MDIO. Fixed: rcp_regmap_named_signal_t (include/rcp/regmap.h) now enumerates all eleven endpoint types, matching Table 21's own signal names and order (primary-source verified directly against the TC18 v0.5.1_RC PDF before implementing, per standing policy on trusting tooling/derived text over the primary spec). CAN's counter-intuitive ordering (RXD = 0, TXD = 1) is recorded. Still open: this is a content/naming fix only — no wire encode/decode path for the HW_config table exists yet (REQ-RMAP-040/-041, this Group's own remaining items) to actually validate a hw_ep_pin_nr value against this enumeration.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21: Enumeration of signals at endpoints, TC18.txt L2779-2820

requirements.title: EP_Signal_Nr restarts at 0 for each endpoint type; c-RCP now converts between the two numbering schemes
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 states the EP_Pin_Nr mapping is specific per endpoint type, and Table 21 accordingly restarts EP_Signal_Nr at 0 for every EP_Type — SPI_CLK is 0, I2C_SCL is 0, UART_TX is 0, CAN RXD is 0, and so on — so that hw_ep_pin_nr in a HW_config entry (Table 19, relative address 0x0001) is interpreted relative to the endpoint type named by hw_ep_nr. c-RCP's rcp_regmap_named_signal_t (include/rcp/regmap.h) is a flat global enumeration in which SPI_CLK and I2C_SCL do not sit at ordinal 0 (primary-source verified directly against the TC18 v0.5.1_RC PDF before implementing). Fixed: rcp_regmap_named_signal_ep_signal_nr() (src/regmap.c) converts this enum's own flat ordinal into TC18's per-type-relative wire value — SPI_CLK/I2C_SCL/UART_TX/CAN_RXD/etc. all correctly convert to 0, restarting per type exactly as Table 21 requires. Still open: this is a content/conversion fix only — no wire encode/decode path for the HW_config table exists yet (REQ-RMAP-040/-041) to actually write a converted value into a real hw_ep_pin_nr register.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21 + Table 19 row hw_ep_pin_nr, TC18.txt L2704, L2764, L2779-2820

requirements.title: RETIRED -- merged into REQ-RMAP-039, which already covers this
requirements.text: RETIRED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): this entry was a stale duplicate of REQ-RMAP-039. It described the same four product-specific configuration-section pointer/capacity pairs (network/physical-layer/time-synch/security, TC18 §12.7.11-.14) as "NOT IMPLEMENTED", but REQ-RMAP-039 (batch 22, this session) already declared all eight registers in rcp_regmap_general_t and marked the pair PARTIAL -- this entry's own text was simply never updated to match, leaving a requirement that flatly contradicted its own sibling entry about the identical fields. See REQ-RMAP-039 for the current, accurate status (registers declared; still no real config-table storage behind the pointers, and the address range is past the discovery response's own wire-reachability ceiling, REQ-RMAP-024). No code change from this retirement -- text-only correction.
requirements.tc18: see REQ-RMAP-039
