requirements.title: Request-stream config carries a per-stream secure-channel index selecting the MACsec channel
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t now carries rx_secure_channel_index (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x000C, 8 bit, R/W*), zero-initialized to TC18's own defined "no cyber security, MACsec uncontrolled port" default. WIRE DISPATCH CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #306, same finding as issue #301's own HW_config/EP_ID_config/response-queue-config): request-stream-cfg is a fourth pointed-to table sharing that same absolute-address finding -- svr_request_stream_cfg_ptr's own value is an absolute address in the same EP0-scoped space Table 18 itself lives in. New rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_render()/_apply_reconfig() (regmap.h/regmap.c) give this table its own wire codec (24-octet-per-row stride, confirmed via direct read of both the RC1 PDF pages 57-58 and the current RC5 PDF page 66); rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()/_encode_read_response() now route to it the identical way as the other three tables. A client can now write AND read rx_secure_channel_index over the wire. STILL PARTIAL: this library has no MACsec layer of its own that would act on a selected channel, and the write dispatcher does not itself consult rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() for this table's own R/W* access type (deferred to whatever caller eventually owns lifecycle-state context, matching REQ-RMAP-040/041's own established precedent).

requirements.title: request stream's acknowledge-stream pointer (rx_ack_stream_index)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t now carries rx_ack_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x0010, 8 bit, R/W*), the index of the stream on which endpoints bound to this request stream shall send their acknowledges, zero-initialized to TC18's own defined "no acknowledge is to be sent" default. WIRE DISPATCH CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #306): see REQ-RMAP-047's own text -- the identical wire codec now serves this field too; a client can now write AND read rx_ack_stream_index over the wire. STILL PARTIAL: no code path yet routes an acknowledgement to a selected response queue from this field -- a genuinely separate, still-open gap about runtime behavior consuming the field, not about wire reachability.

requirements.title: request stream's response-stream pointer and its discovery-enabling default of 1 (rx_resp_stream_index)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t now carries rx_resp_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x0011, 8 bit, R/W*), the index of the stream on which endpoints bound to this request stream shall send their responses, with 0 meaning "no response is to be sent". FIXED: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_init() now sets this one field to 1 (not 0), reproducing the specification's own bootstrap guarantee that a freshly reset server can answer a discovery request before any configuration has been written -- REQ-RMAP-018's own text was corrected to carve out this deliberate exception to its "zero everything" rule. WIRE DISPATCH CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #306): see REQ-RMAP-047's own text -- the identical wire codec now serves this field too; a client can now write AND read rx_resp_stream_index over the wire. STILL PARTIAL: rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg() still only checks a boolean has_response_stream (src/lifecycle.c:59), which records that some response stream exists but not which one, and no code path yet routes a response to the selected stream from this field -- a genuinely separate, still-open gap about runtime behavior consuming the field, not about wire reachability.

requirements.title: Watchdog timeout register width and unit deviate from Table 22's 16-bit clock-tick field
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t.rx_wd_timeout_ms shall represent TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22's rx_wd_timeout_intervall register (relative address 0x000A, 16 bit, R/W*, expressed in clock tics). c-RCP deliberately stores it as a 32-bit millisecond value and rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() compares it against elapsed_since_last_kick_ms, so a conversion between the server's clock-tick domain and milliseconds shall be applied at the register-write boundary, and a written value shall be rejected if it does not fit the register's 16-bit width. FIXED: rcp_regmap_wd_timeout_ms_to_ticks()/_ticks_to_ms() (regmap.h/.c) now perform that conversion and the 16-bit bounds check. TC18 names no fixed clock-tick rate for this register anywhere near its own definition, so, matching the established caller-supplies-already-classified-units convention (rcp_acf_reg_write_len(), rcp_respqueue_max_avtpdu_size_within_mtu()), both functions take the tick duration as a caller-supplied parameter rather than this library inventing a rate TC18 never specifies; ms-to-ticks rounds down so the enforced period is never longer than requested. STILL PARTIAL: no register-write code path in the codebase calls these functions yet -- the same deferred-wire-dispatch gap already tracked for the rest of Table 22's own fields (REQ-RMAP-047/048/049).

requirements.title: Table 22's W* fields are writable in both HW_UNCONFIGURED and HW_CONFIGURED and read-only in RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: Every field of the request-stream configuration table (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22) marked R/W* shall be classified RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR and shall be writable while the server is in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED or RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED and read-only in RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED. FIXED: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() (src/lifecycle.c) now returns true for FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR in both HW_UNCONFIGURED and HW_CONFIGURED, false only in RCP_CONFIGURED, matching Table 22's own legend exactly (TC18.txt L2929-L2931). STILL OPEN: no register-map write path in the codebase classifies the request-stream table as FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR at all, so this now-correct primitive is not yet wired to Table 22 anywhere -- a separate, still-open architecture gap.

requirements.title: EP_ID_config rows are now (Request_Stream_Index, EP_Nr, BBID) triples, not (EP_Nr, BBID) pairs
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t shall model one full row of the EP_ID_config table (TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23): a Request_Stream_Index (relative offset 0x0000 within the row, 8 bit, R/W+), an EP_Nr (0x0001, 8 bit, R/W+) and a BBID (0x0002, 16 bit, R/W+), so that the same byte_bus_id can be mapped to different endpoints on different request streams. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t declares request_stream_index, closing this field-content gap -- the specification's central addressing rule that a byte_bus_id is unique only within the stream_id it is paired with (include/rcp/avtp.h's own note) is now representable in this codebase's own in-memory model. Deliberately placed as this struct's LAST field (TC18's own row puts it first, at row offset 0x0000) so every existing positional-initializer test call site kept compiling unchanged -- this struct is content modeling only, not a wire-order layout, so C field order carries no TC18 conformance obligation. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render() (regmap.h/regmap.c) now serializes a real table at TC18's own exact 4-octet-per-row stride (row N at relative address 4*N), proven via a byte-offset test. RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301, same finding as REQ-RMAP-040's own text): the addressing question this entry's own prior text called genuinely unresolved is now answered -- direct verification of the current RC5 baseline PDF (page 61) shows Table 18's own address column is headed "Absolute address", confirming svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr's own value is an absolute address in the same EP0-scoped space Table 18 itself lives in; a client reaches EP_ID_config via an ordinary evt[2:0]=111b request to byte_bus_id=0 with start_address = svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr's current value plus an offset. rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() (regmap.h/regmap.c) now implements exactly this for EP_ID_config too: it routes an incoming write across svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr's own extent, applied via the new rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_apply_reconfig(), the parse-side inverse of rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render() (identical patch-then-reparse idiom to rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_apply_reconfig()). READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() routes to EP_ID_config's own extent too, reusing rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render() directly -- a client can now write AND read EP_ID_config over the wire. STILL OPEN: this dispatcher (both directions) does not itself consult rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() for EP_ID_config's own access type -- that authorization gate remains deferred to whatever caller eventually owns lifecycle-state context, matching REQ-RMAP-040/041's own established precedent for HW_config's own write path.

requirements.title: byte_bus_id is an 11-bit address; rcp_byte_bus_id_t now represents the full 0..2047 range
requirements.text: rcp_byte_bus_id_t shall be wide enough to hold the full 11-bit byte_bus_id the EP_ID_config table's BBID register carries (TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23, row offset 0x0002, 16 bit register, "Byte_bus_id [11bit]") and that the ACF byte_message_info header transports across octet 2 bits [2:0] and octet 3 (REQ-ACF-016). Fixed: rcp_byte_bus_id_t is now uint16_t (include/rcp/avtp.h), and byte_bus_id[10:8] is a real, encoded/decoded value on both the pack and unpack paths (src/acf.c) rather than structurally always zero. Full "read every consumer" investigation performed first (~55 files touching the type): every endpoint type module, the conditional-request layer, config.c, lifecycle.c, mock.c, and server.c were all confirmed to be simple pass-through consumers needing no logic changes; two real consumer-side fixes were needed and made alongside the type change -- adapt.c's byte_bus_id-to-string buffer (char[4], sized for "255"+NUL) was widened to char[6] ("2047"+NUL), and test_mock.c's own decode-failure test needed a new stimulus (an over-declared pad count) since its old one (a high byte_bus_id) no longer fails to decode. REQ-ACF-020's own companion requirement (the same underlying gap, viewed from the ACF wire layer) is fixed by the same change; RCP_ACF_ERR_BUS_ID_OVERFLOW is retired outright, not left as dead code, since the condition it represented can no longer occur. c-RCP can now address all 2048 endpoints per stream the protocol defines.

requirements.title: A Request_Stream_Index of 0 terminates the EP_ID_config table, and the power-on defaults address EP0
requirements.text: Every consumer of the EP_ID_config table shall stop scanning at the first row whose Request_Stream_Index is 0, that value denoting the end of the table rather than a valid stream index (TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23 / L2976), and the table's power-on default contents (Request_Stream_Index = 1, EP_Nr = 0, BBID = 0) shall permit access to EP0 before any configuration is written. Fixed: rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_effective_count() (src/regmap.c) is the dedicated, sentinel-aware consumer -- it scans entries[0..capacity) and returns the count of leading rows before the first row whose request_stream_index is 0, or capacity unchanged if no such row appears. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_row_init_default() supplies the power-on default row (request_stream_index=1, ep_id=RCP_REGMAP_EP0_INDEX, byte_bus_id=0), which permits EP0 access and, being nonzero in request_stream_index, does not itself look like the end-of-table sentinel. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_ascending() (REQ-RMAP-056) deliberately remains sentinel-unaware, since it is a generic ordering diagnostic, not a table iterator -- sentinel recognition is this pair's job specifically. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render() (regmap.h/regmap.c, REQ-RMAP-052) now serializes a real table at TC18's own exact 4-octet-per-row stride, so a table this pair scans is also wire-layout-correct when rendered. RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301, same finding as REQ-RMAP-052's own text): the ACF_ABB WRITE wrapper this entry's own prior text called missing now exists -- rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_apply_reconfig() (the parse-side inverse of render(), patch-then-reparse idiom matching every other pointed-to table's own apply_reconfig()) plus rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()'s own address-routing to it, targeted at svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr's own extent. READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() serves this exact stride back over the wire -- see REQ-RMAP-052's own text for the full read-side detail. STILL OPEN: no setter routes a write through rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() to enforce EP_ID_config's own access type -- see REQ-RMAP-040/041's own text for why that gate is deliberately deferred rather than added ad hoc.

requirements.title: the W+ lockable access type for EP_ID_config and the Table 24 W+ queue fields
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable_w_plus()/_write_error_w_plus() (lifecycle.h/lifecycle.c) now implement TC18's W+ (explicitly lockable) register access type -- EP_ID_config rows (§12.7.8 Table 23) and the STREAM_UID/flush_on_count/Flush_time queue registers (§12.7.9 Table 24) are both marked R/W+: the table may be locked by the configuring instance to protect against unwanted later modification, independently of the lifecycle state that governs W and W*. Deliberately a SEPARATE function rather than a new rcp_lifecycle_field_kind_t value threaded through rcp_lifecycle_field_writable()'s own signature -- that function has roughly 90 existing call sites across every endpoint type, 2 internal uses, and every test exercising any of them, none of which need a lock concept; a standalone function delivers the same primitive with zero blast radius to existing callers, reusing (not re-deriving) the existing FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR state/writer rule internally. STILL OPEN: no register-map write path in the codebase calls this new primitive yet -- EP_ID_config and the Table 24 queue registers are both still content-modeling-only (REQ-RMAP-052/054/061/065), the same deferred ACF_ABB-wire-wrapper gap as the rest of this phase, so a client still has no way to actually latch either table over the wire.

requirements.title: EP_ID_config ordering is ascending in (Request_Stream_Index, BBID), not BBID alone
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_ascending() reports whether the EP_ID_config table is ordered ascending in the composite key (Request_Stream_Index, BBID), the ordering TC18 §12.7.8 requires the configuring instance to maintain and whose violation the specification says can cause requests to be dropped because no endpoint is found. Fixed: the implementation (src/regmap.c) now compares request_stream_index first between consecutive rows — a decrease is always reported non-ascending, an increase is always reported ascending regardless of that row's own byte_bus_id (TC18 does not require byte_bus_id to reset or relate across different streams) — and falls back to the prior strict byte_bus_id comparison only when request_stream_index is unchanged between the two rows. A per-stream-ascending table that interleaves streams (e.g. stream 1 BBIDs 1,2 then stream 2 BBIDs 1,2 again) is now correctly reported ascending, and a table whose stream index goes backwards is correctly reported non-ascending regardless of BBID. UPDATED 2026-08-11 (spec rebaseline to TC18 0.5.1_RC5): see REQ-RMAP-020's own note -- the ordering requirement itself is deleted from TC18 as of spec revision 0.5.1_RC4; this function's own composite-key comparison logic remains correct and harmless (pure diagnostic, no server-side enforcement), but no longer traces to a live TC18 MUST.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.8, TC18.txt L2979-L2981 -- REMOVED in spec revision 0.5.1_RC4, TC18 PDF 0.5.1_RC5 p.68 (sentence shown struck through, 051RC4 tag)

requirements.title: single-RC-Client-per-endpoint recommendation is neither enforced nor diagnosed
requirements.text: c-RCP provides no ENFORCEMENT that an endpoint is mapped to at most one RC Client at a time, the arrangement TC18 §12.7.8 recommends for safety reasons -- rcp_regmap_ep_client_t.owning_stream_index (include/rcp/regmap.h) still exists solely to authorize functional-config writes (REQ-RMAP-011/012) and does not constrain which request streams may deliver requests to the endpoint. Fixed: a read-only DIAGNOSTIC, rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_has_single_client_per_ep() (src/regmap.c), now reports the condition -- true iff no ep_id in the table is associated with two different request_stream_index values; an endpoint reachable from several rows that all share one request_stream_index (multiple byte_bus_ids, one client) is correctly NOT flagged, only a genuine multi-stream (multi-client) mapping is. Matches rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_ascending()'s own established read-only-diagnostic, not-enforcement shape. Still open: no server-side rejection or correction of a multi-client table exists, matching this table's own standing "Known spec ambiguity" note -- TC18 itself defines no corrective action for a server that receives one.

requirements.title: endpoints sharing a byte_bus_id within one stream should be of the same ep_type
requirements.text: c-RCP provides no ENFORCEMENT that all endpoints mapped to the same byte_bus_id within a single request stream share an ep_type, as TC18 §12.7.8 recommends. A shared byte_bus_id is a deliberate multicast-within-a-stream mechanism, and a request broadcast to endpoints of differing ep_type is decoded differently by each. Fixed: a read-only DIAGNOSTIC, rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_shared_bus_homogeneous() (src/regmap.c), now reports the condition. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t itself still carries no ep_type (TC18's own EP_ID_config row doesn't have one -- ep_type lives on rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_t, looked up by ep_id), so the diagnostic takes a caller-supplied, index-parallel ep_types[] array rather than inventing a field this row doesn't have on the wire; it returns true iff every group of rows sharing one (request_stream_index, byte_bus_id) pair has an identical ep_types[] value throughout. Still open: no server-side rejection or correction of a heterogeneous shared-bus group exists, and nothing in this codebase yet calls this diagnostic with a real, live ep_types[] array sourced from the actual per-endpoint configuration table -- that wiring is real future work, not modeled here.

requirements.title: per-response/acknowledge-stream transmit queue and its queue_size register
requirements.text: regmap.h's rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t gains a queue_size register (TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0004, 16 bit, R/W*, "Queue N assigned memory in 32bit words"), and a new module, respqueue.h/respqueue.c, provides the actual transmit queue this codebase was missing entirely: rcp_respqueue_t, an octet-budgeted FIFO of framed response/acknowledge messages (rcp_respqueue_push()/_pop(), capacity enforced against queue_size x 4 octets, refusing a push that would exceed it and leaving the queue unchanged). Distinct from server.h's ep_enable pre-load queue, which holds inbound requests, not outbound responses. The remaining Group 4 behaviors this queue's own contents will need (Max_AVTPDUsize transmit enforcement/fragmentation REQ-RMAP-061/062, the flush_on_count packing trigger REQ-RMAP-063, the Flush_time timer and heartbeat REQ-RMAP-064/065) are deliberately not modeled here -- this closes the storage-and-capacity scope only.

requirements.title: response queue's STREAM_UID (the unique_id half of the queue's outgoing stream_id)
requirements.text: regmap.h's rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t gains a stream_uid field (TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0000, 16 bit, R/W+) and a new rcp_regmap_response_queue_stream_id(cfg, mac) helper that combines it with the interface's own mac exactly as rcp_stream_id_make() (avtp.h) would — a thin, directly-testable named wrapper, not new stream_id-construction logic. A response queue now has an identity rx_ack_stream_index/rx_resp_stream_index (Table 22) can point at.

requirements.title: Max_AVTPDUsize bounds every transmitted AVTPDU, is MTU-consistent, and is discoverable
requirements.text: PARTIAL: respqueue.h's rcp_respqueue_t enforces the transmit-bounding half -- rcp_respqueue_init() takes max_avtpdu_size_octets (regmap.h's rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t.max_avtpdu_size, quadlets x 4), and rcp_respqueue_push() refuses (queue unchanged) any single frame whose own length exceeds it. The MTU-consistency-check half is now also closed: rcp_respqueue_max_avtpdu_size_within_mtu() (respqueue.h/respqueue.c) is the config-time check TC18 §12.7.9 (TC18.txt L3010-3011, "the Max_AVTPDUsize shall always be configured such that the final network frame does not exceed the maximum transmit unit size of the network") requires -- a caller runs it before ever calling rcp_respqueue_init(); TC18 defines no fixed MTU value of its own, so mtu_budget_octets is the caller's own already-adjusted ceiling, matching this module's established "caller supplies already-classified units" convention. RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 3, same finding as REQ-RMAP-040/041 and REQ-RMAP-052/054's own text): the addressing question this entry's own prior text called genuinely unresolved is now answered -- svr_response_stream_cfg_ptr's own value is an absolute address in the same EP0-scoped space Table 18 itself lives in; a client reaches response-queue-config via an ordinary evt[2:0]=111b request to byte_bus_id=0 with start_address = svr_response_stream_cfg_ptr's current value plus an offset. Unlike HW_config/EP_ID_config, no render function existed for this table at all before this batch: rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_render() (regmap.h/regmap.c) is the first one, serializing TC18's own exact 10-octet-per-queue wire stride (STREAM_UID@0x0000, Max_AVTPDUsize@0x0002, queue_size@0x0004, flush_on_count@0x0006, Flush_time@0x0008). rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() now routes to it (via the new rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_apply_reconfig(), same patch-then-reparse idiom as the other two tables) the identical way. A genuine content/wire width mismatch was found and fixed in the same batch: rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t.flush_time_us is uint32_t, but Table 24's own Flush_time register is only 16 bits -- render() now saturates (never wraps) a value exceeding 0xFFFF, since wraparound could silently produce 0, TC18's own "flush only by count" encoding, inverting the field's own meaning. READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() (regmap.h/regmap.c) routes to all three pointed-to tables at once, reusing each table's own already-proven render() function -- a client can now write AND read response-queue-config (and HW_config and EP_ID_config) over the wire the same way. Deliberately does NOT compose data across more than one extent when a read's own address+read_size would span into a second one -- TC18 defines no rule for that, and inventing one would not be primary-source-derived; the existing "response spans exactly read_size octets, zero-filled past the source's own extent" convention (already established by rcp_regmap_general_encode_read_response() for Table 18 alone) answers what happens past the requested extent's own length instead. STILL OPEN: this dispatcher (both directions) does not itself consult rcp_lifecycle_field_writable()/rcp_lifecycle_field_writable_w_plus() for this table's own mixed R/W*/R/W+ access types (STREAM_UID/flush_on_count/Flush_time are R/W+, Max_AVTPDUsize/queue_size are R/W*) -- that authorization gate remains deferred to whatever caller eventually owns lifecycle-state context, matching REQ-RMAP-040/041's own established precedent. An earlier revision of this entry's own text described the remaining gap as "exposing the value in the discovery general-register slice" -- that framing predates this codebase's own later discovery that Table 24 was never part of the 14-octet discovery slice at all; corrected in an earlier batch.

requirements.title: A single ACF message exceeding Max_AVTPDUsize is fragmented via the ms bit
requirements.text: respqueue.h's rcp_respqueue_max_fragment_payload(max_avtpdu_size_octets, header_len) now derives the correct max_fragment_payload for fragment.h's existing rcp_fragment_plan_count()/rcp_fragment_plan() (REQ-FRAG-002..018, unchanged) from rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t.max_avtpdu_size (TC18 §12.7.9) -- converting the register's own quadlet unit to octets is the caller's job (this codebase's established 'caller supplies already-classified units' convention), and the helper conservatively reserves the fixed ACF header plus the worst-case 3 octets of trailing pad so the resulting budget is always safe. A caller with a payload too large for one AVTPDU derives this budget, plans the fragments, and pushes each one to rcp_respqueue_t individually (REQ-RMAP-061's own per-message enforcement then bounds each fragment independently).

requirements.title: flush_on_count triggers transmission of the whole queue packed into Max_AVTPDUsize-bounded AVTPDUs
requirements.text: respqueue.h's rcp_respqueue_should_flush(q, flush_on_count_octets) implements the trigger -- true once the queue's own running octet total reaches or exceeds the (caller-converted) threshold, matching this codebase's 'caller supplies already-classified units' convention. rcp_respqueue_plan_batch(q, max_avtpdu_size_octets) implements the packing: reports how many of the queue's FIFO-ordered entries fit together within one AVTPDU, so a caller drains exactly that many via rcp_respqueue_pop() and repeats until the queue is empty -- 'packed in a fitting number of AVTPDUs.' Both operate on the queue's own state alone; scheduler.h's rcp_sched_split_frame_members() (the inverse, decode-side split, unchanged) needed no changes.

requirements.title: Flush_time forces transmission once the configured interval since the last transmission elapses
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0008, 16 bit, R/W+, microseconds, 0 meaning "flush only by count": the server shall initiate transmission from a response queue whenever the time since that queue's last transmission is equal to or greater than Flush_time, independently of flush_on_count. rcp_respqueue_should_flush_by_time(elapsed_since_last_transmit_us, flush_time_us) (include/rcp/respqueue.h) implements the trigger as a pure, caller-timed check -- flush_time_us == 0 always false ("flush only by count"), otherwise true once elapsed_since_last_transmit_us reaches it -- mirroring e2e.h's own rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate(elapsed_since_last_kick_ms) convention of taking elapsed time as a caller-supplied input rather than reading a clock of its own. Deliberately independent of the queue's own entries_len, so it fires identically whether the queue is empty or not (REQ-RMAP-065's own precondition).

requirements.title: an empty response queue still emits a heartbeat AVTPDU on Flush_time expiry
requirements.text: PARTIAL: on Flush_time expiry the RC Server shall emit an AVTPDU from the queue even when that queue is empty, so the RC Client can observe that the server is alive (TC18 §12.7.9). rcp_respqueue_should_flush_by_time() (REQ-RMAP-064) already fires identically for an empty queue, rcp_respqueue_plan_batch() already reports 0 for an empty queue, and avtp.h's rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf(hdr, NULL, 0) already accepts a zero-length payload -- so the empty heartbeat AVTPDU is fully constructible from existing primitives (proven end to end by test_tc18_gaps_regmap.c's test_flush_time_trigger_and_empty_heartbeat_are_composable()). What remains open is the same boundary REQ-SRV-017 already states: c-RCP is a protocol library, not a scheduler, and ships no emitter that actually drives this composition against a real clock and a real transport -- that composition is left to the integrator.

requirements.title: svr_discovery_timeout register (Table 33/36, RC-Server-specific block, 16 bit, R/W*)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_svr_ep_cfg_t now carries svr_discovery_timeout (TC18 §13.7.1.2's own RC-Server functional-configuration table -- Table 33 in the RC1 baseline, renumbered Table 36 in the current RC5 baseline this project treats as authoritative, confirmed the same table via direct PDF page-image reads of both revisions; 16 bit, R/W*, microseconds), defaulting to TC18's own stated 20000 (20 ms) via rcp_regmap_svr_ep_cfg_init(). Content modeling only, same deferred ACF_ABB-wire-wrapper gap as HW_config/EP_ID_config/response-queue/Table 22 -- and this register is also NOT yet wired to rcp_discovery_claim_t's own Discovery_TimeOut (a separate, caller-supplied-milliseconds constructor argument), so the TC18 §12.6 rule that an unused discovery stream is dropped after Discovery_TimeOut is still not enforced from this register. This table's own relative-address column also carries a real, confirmed primary-source defect (see regmap.h's own file-header note) that does not affect this field, which sits outside the collision.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 Table 36 (Table 33 in RC1), TC18.txt L3990

requirements.title: RC Server endpoint functional-config block (Table 33/36) incl. svr_enable always 1 / read-only
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_svr_ep_cfg_t now carries svr_ep_status (TC18 §13.7.1.2's Table 33/36, RC-Server-specific block, 16 bit, R/W, no further bit-level breakdown given). DELIBERATELY STILL NOT MODELED: the table's own generic EP_FUNC-common-header fields (svr_ep_len 0x0000 R, reserved, svr_ep_enable&clr with svr_enable permanently 1 and read-only, svr_ep_options R/W*) -- §13.7.1.1's own prose, immediately preceding this table, states "the RC Server as endpoint is not included in the EP_FUNC_config register maps", directly contradicting the table listing these fields for the RC Server anyway. Modeling them would mean silently picking a side of a stated, unresolved spec self-contradiction (see regmap.h's own file-header note for the full investigation, including a real, confirmed-on-both-PDF-revisions address collision in this same table, independent of this contradiction). The shared rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t prefix continues to model those four fields generically for every OTHER endpoint type only, unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 Table 36 (Table 33 in RC1), TC18.txt L3980-3996

requirements.title: Register-write outcome: read-only register succeeds silently, write-prohibited register errors
requirements.text: PARTIAL, reassessed: TC18 §13.7.1.2's prose gives a state-vs-writer distinction ("Writing to a write prohibited register... creates a response with err=1 and error code UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS") that REQ-WIREERR-004/REQ-LIFECYCLE-024 (rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error(), src/lifecycle.c) already implement, correctly distinguishing RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS (state-locked, per TC18 Figure 16) from RCP_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS (writer-denied, per this same §13.7.1.2 passage) -- this requirement's own prior text ("no code path maps the two cases") was stale and is corrected. STILL OPEN: the SAME paragraph's immediately preceding sentence -- "Writing data to read only registers has no effect and request is confirmed normally" -- describes a THIRD outcome (err=0, silent no-op) that neither of the two implemented codes produce; every current denial in this codebase becomes an err=1 error response. UNCONFIRMED HYPOTHESIS, not coded as fact: this sentence most likely describes individual READ-ONLY BITS within an otherwise-writable register (the same paragraph's immediately preceding OR/AND/XOR/SET register-write-operation discussion, e.g. "byte_msg_payload 0x00000000 and evt=x001 (OR) results in no effect"), a bit-level masking concern distinct from REQ-RMAP-025's own whole-register-map, Figure-16-governed access-control case (already correctly LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS, twice independently verified, deliberately NOT changed here) -- not yet implementable since no register-write dispatch mechanism in this codebase currently operates at that bit level (every register-map write path today is whole-struct-field decode, not per-bit OR/AND/XOR against a live register image).

requirements.title: Effective register-write payload length = (acf_msg_length - 3) x 4 - pad - 2
requirements.text: acf.h's rcp_acf_reg_write_len(acf_msg_length, pad) computes the effective number of register-write data bytes exactly as (acf_msg_length - 3) x 4 - pad - 2 (TC18 13.7.1.2, formula corrected in spec revision 0.5.1_RC5), the quantity a server needs to know how many octets of an EP0 register write are data rather than address/CRC/padding -- distinct from rcp_acf_pad_len(), which computes the pad octet count only, and from the ACF decoder's own payload_len, which spans the whole payload including the address/CRC region. FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, spec rebaseline to 0.5.1_RC5): the 0.5.1_RC baseline this codebase originally read against omitted a trailing '- 2' term (for the 2-octet register start address that leads the payload, per RC5's own updated Figure 22); this function matched that omission exactly and has been corrected to match. Fail-safe on a malformed/adversarial frame: returns 0, never underflowing, if acf_msg_length is too small to hold the fixed 3-quadlet region or if pad plus the 2-octet address exceeds what remains.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2, TC18 spec PDF 0.5.1_RC5 p.92 (formula corrected, NXP_101/BE44 tracked-change; superseding TC18.txt L4035-4036 from the 0.5.1_RC baseline)

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() explicitly assigns every member of the returned writer_ctx, including via_discovery_stream
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() shall set via_discovery_stream to the caller-supplied, already-classified via_discovery_stream argument (pass-through, matching via_ep0/via_unicast's own convention), and every member of the returned rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t shall be explicitly assigned before return -- none left uninitialized. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H / REQ-RMAP-009): this function previously left via_discovery_stream unassigned, a genuine defect since its return value flows directly into ASIL-B write-authorization decisions (rcp_lifecycle_field_writable()/rcp_lifecycle_transition()) that read every member. Currently latent -- no production caller exists yet in src/*.c, only this function's own unit tests -- but the defect was real regardless of whether a caller happened to read the uninitialized field yet.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2, TC18.txt L2184 (same basis as REQ-RMAP-009 -- this entry covers the writer_ctx construction contract as a whole, not a new TC18 clause)

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t carries rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable, closing a gap this file's own terminology-drift note had already named but never added
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t shall carry rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22, relative address 0x000D bit 5, 1 bit, R/W*): true drives every endpoint bound to this stream toward its configured safe state if one endpoint's own request storage overflows. Found 2026-08-11 while implementing issue #306's own request-stream-cfg wire codec: regmap.h's own "TC18 0.5.1_RC5 terminology drift" section (added earlier, task #97) already NAMED rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable as one of this codebase's own eight independent 0x000D bits, but the struct itself never actually had the field -- a genuine, previously-unflagged content-modeling gap. rcp_e2e_overflow_should_enter_safe_state() (e2e.h/e2e.c, REQ-E2E-030) already existed as the pure decision function this field is the register-map source for, with no struct field to source it from until now. FIXED: the field is added, zero-initialized to false (matching TC18's own implied "not blocked upon EP overflow" default and every sibling boolean field's own zero-init convention), and is now part of rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_render()/_apply_reconfig()'s own wire codec (issue #306) at the same bit position. REQ-E2E-030's own separate, still-open cross-endpoint-orchestrator gap (bringing every OTHER endpoint on the stream into safe state, which rcp_server_endpoint_t's single-endpoint scope cannot perform) is unaffected by adding this field -- this entry closes the content-modeling/wire-reachability half only, not that orchestration gap.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 22, TC18.txt L2880-L2882 (same citation as REQ-E2E-030's own -- this entry covers the register-map content-modeling half, REQ-E2E-030 covers the runtime-decision half)

requirements.title: A sequencer whose state register is manually set to 0 is disabled
requirements.text: A sequencer whose Seq_state register has been manually written to 0 shall be treated as disabled (TC18 §12.7.10 Table 25, relative address 0x0000, 8 bit, R/W): no compound or compound-wait step conditioned on that sequencer shall become executable, and no advance shall move it out of 0 until it is explicitly rewritten to a nonzero state. NOT IMPLEMENTED: rcp_sequencer_set_state() treats 0 as an ordinary state value, so a step whose start_state happens to be 0 fires against a sequencer the client intended to disable, and rcp_e2e_endpoint_in_safe_state() (REQ-E2E-018) would report a disabled sequencer as "in safe state" if rx_safe_sequencer_state were configured to 0. Distinct from rcp_sequencer_table_unsupported() (REQ-SEQ-004), which is the table-wide "zero sequencers implemented" case.

requirements.title: each sequencer is owned by one request stream, and only that stream may access it
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP models no per-sequencer Request_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.10 Table 25, relative address 0x0001, 8 bit, R/W*), the register naming the one RC Client permitted to access that sequencer, and performs no access control on sequencer reads or writes. rcp_sequencer_table_t (include/rcp/request_sequencer.h:85-88) is an unowned array of state bytes and rcp_sequencer_set_state() takes no requester identity. Consequence: any RC Client that can reach the register map can advance or reset any other client's sequencer, including one another client has configured as its rx_safestate_sequencer — a client can therefore forge or clear another client's safe state, defeating the §12.7.7 safety-measure mechanism entirely.

requirements.title: svr_max_sequencers and the sequencer_state table expose sequencer availability and state through the register map
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_general_t.svr_max_sequencers shall equal the count of sequencers the server actually implements (rcp_sequencer_table_t.count), reporting 0 when sequencers are not implemented at all, and the sequencer_state sub-table referenced by rcp_regmap_general_t.sequencer_state shall expose each sequencer's current Seq_state value for reading over EP0 (TC18 §12.7.10). NOT IMPLEMENTED as a wired behavior: both register fields exist (include/rcp/regmap.h:209, 221) but neither is populated from or validated against the live table, and no byte_message_info read path serves the sequencer_state sub-table. Consequence: a client cannot discover how many sequencers a server has, and cannot read a sequencer's state to decide whether a queued conditional step has fired.

requirements.title: evt[2:0] selects which of the six SPI channel configurations a request uses
requirements.text: The SPI endpoint shall carry up to RCP_EP_SPI_MAX_CHANNELS (6) independently pre-configured channel configurations (rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_t::channels), and the configuration a given SPI request executes under shall be selected by that request's evt[2:0] field, per TC18 13.7.3.1/13.7.3.2.

requirements.title: SPI trigger output numbering (Table 38)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 Table 38's SPI trigger output numbering -- signal 0 'SPI execution done', signal 1 reserved, and signals 2..13 pairing each chip select CS0..CS5 with an asserted and a de-asserted event in ascending order. The endpoint models a per-channel trigger selector but derives no trigger signal from CS transitions.

requirements.title: SPI functional-config register block (Table 39/42) is fully modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_spi_channel_cfg_t now carries every Table 39 per-channel field this module previously omitted -- baud_rate_kbps (spi_baud_rateN, kbit/s), use_common_cs (spi_use_csN), cs_clk_leadtime/clk_cs_trailtime (spi_cs_clk_leadtimeN/spi_clk_cs_trailtimeN, in spi_clk cycles, distinct from this module's own pre-existing nanosecond-denominated inter_byte_delay_ns/inter_transfer_delay_ns), and bits_max (spi_bits_maxN); rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_t gained ep_status (spi_ep_status). CPOL/CPHA continue to round-trip losslessly through the pre-existing mode byte via rcp_ep_spi_mode_cpol()/_cpha() and a new inverse. rcp_ep_spi_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() (evt[2:0] == 111b, Table 30's SPI row + §12.7.1) now serialize/parse the whole block -- spi_ep_len and spi_nr_cs are rendered from RCP_EP_SPI_EP_FUNC_LEN/RCP_EP_SPI_MAX_CHANNELS and are read-only, matching PWM_OUT's/GPIO's own EP_LEN convention. UPDATED 2026-08-11 (spec rebaseline to TC18 0.5.1_RC5): spi_nr_cs (renumbered Table 39 -> Table 42) was narrowed from a plain 8-bit count to a 4-bit "(count - 1)" field (bits [3:0], upper nibble reserved) by spec revision RC4 -- rcp_ep_spi_render_registers() now renders (RCP_EP_SPI_MAX_CHANNELS - 1) & 0x0F (0x05) instead of the plain count (0x06). See REQ-SPI-040 for the new spi_deassert_cs_pauseN bit RC5 adds to the same block.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 39 (0.5.1_RC baseline)/Table 42 (0.5.1_RC5), TC18.txt L4246-4300; spi_nr_cs width corrected per RC5 PDF p.96 (051RC4 tag, ticket unlabeled -- "this standard limits the number of CS line per EP to 32")

requirements.title: SPI zero-fill when read_size exceeds the payload, full payload on PICO otherwise
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not apply TC18 13.7.3.3's transfer-length rule -- an SPI endpoint shall append zero octets when read_size exceeds the byte_msg_payload length (so the bus clocks read_size octets), and shall still present the whole byte_msg_payload on PICO when read_size is smaller than it. The library's SPI request codec carries payload and read_size as independent fields and derives no transfer length from their relation.

requirements.title: SPI error state resets the EP enable bit; a clamped pin flags every response
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 13.7.3.3's SPI fault latching -- an SPI endpoint that stops execution shall enter an error state recorded in the debug register with its EP_config enable bit reset, requiring the RC Client to clear the error status and re-enable the endpoint before operation continues, and a clamped (stuck-at) IO pin shall raise a flag in the server's diagnostic registers and set the err flag in every subsequent response of that endpoint.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_render_registers()/_encode_reconfig_request() implement the generic §12.7.1 configuration request for SPI
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request -- evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data -- usable against every endpoint type. SPI's own Table 30 row confirms 111b carries this exact meaning (distinct from evt[2:0] 000b-101b, which select one of SPI's six pre-configured channels, and 110b, which is reserved/UNSUPPORTED_CMD). rcp_ep_spi_render_registers() serializes cfg's whole Table 39 block (the 6-octet common prefix plus six 8-octet per-channel blocks); rcp_ep_spi_encode_reconfig_request() encodes an ACF_ABB write request (op=WRITE, evt=111b) carrying a 16-bit big-endian start address followed by data, matching PWM_OUT's/GPIO's own encode_reconfig_request() shape.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 18, TC18.txt L2463-2484; §13.5 Table 30 (SPI row), TC18.txt L3677-3684

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror() apply the addressed configuration write and never return NULL for a status message
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_spi_apply_reconfig() decodes the address+data payload TC18 §12.7.1 defines and patches cfg's Table 39 register block at octet granularity, then adopts the whole block atomically -- a write whose start_address+length exceeds RCP_EP_SPI_EP_FUNC_LEN is rejected and cfg left entirely unchanged (RCP_EP_SPI_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE), matching §12.7.1's own 'such a payload is to be ignored' rule; octets landing on a read-only register (EP_LEN, NR_CS, or a channel's own reserved octet) are silently skipped while the rest of the span is still applied. rcp_ep_spi_reconfig_strerror() never returns NULL, including for an unrecognized error code.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints, TC18.txt L2463-2484

requirements.title: spi_deassert_cs_pauseN (Table 42, new in spec revision 0.5.1_RC5) is modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, spec rebaseline to TC18 0.5.1_RC5): spi_deassert_cs_pauseN is a new configuration bit (bit 4 of a channel's own +0x02 cfg octet, ticket NXP_100) with no counterpart at all in the 0.5.1_RC baseline this module was originally built against -- "0b: no de-assertion during break / 1b: de-assertion during break" during the pause window spi_cs_clk_leadtimeN/spi_pause_minN/spi_clk_cs_trailtimeN define. rcp_ep_spi_channel_cfg_t gains a new deassert_cs_pause field (RCP_EP_SPI_CFG_BIT_DEASSERT_CS_PAUSE); rcp_ep_spi_render_registers()/parse_registers() (the rcp_ep_spi_apply_reconfig() inverse) render/parse it, leaving every pre-existing cfg bit (clk_polarity/clk_phase/cs_polarity/use_cs) untouched -- the same 'new field, existing fields left alone' rule already established for every prior Group I register-block fix this session.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 42, spec revision 0.5.1_RC5 PDF p.96 (ticket NXP_100, tags 051RC5 "new configuration, optional" + "added for clarification")

requirements.title: A disabled endpoint still executes configuration requests immediately
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP queues configuration requests submitted to a disabled endpoint (TC18 §12.3.1.3). rcp_server_endpoint_submit() branches only on ep->ep_enable and copies every frame into the pre-load queue when it is false, whereas the specification requires a disabled endpoint to keep executing configuration requests and to queue only operational ones. A client cannot configure an endpoint that is currently disabled -- including writing ep_enable itself.

requirements.title: Queuing a request on a disabled endpoint still emits the requested acknowledge
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not emit an acknowledge when a request is stored for a disabled endpoint (TC18 §12.3.1.3). rcp_server_endpoint_submit() copies the frame into the pre-load queue and returns false with no acknowledge, so a client that asked for an acknowledge receives nothing until the endpoint is enabled and the request eventually executes. The client cannot distinguish a stored request from a dropped one.

requirements.title: Cyclic heartbeat: empty NTSCF-only PDU on an empty response queue
requirements.text: PARTIAL: c-RCP models the response-queue periodicity register (rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t::flush_time_us) and, as of REQ-RMAP-064/065 (issue #200 Group 4), provides the primitives to recognize the trigger and construct the empty PDU -- rcp_respqueue_should_flush_by_time() (include/rcp/respqueue.h) fires identically whether the response queue is empty or not, and rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf(hdr, NULL, 0) already produces a valid empty PDU (an NTSCF header carrying no ACF messages at all), the exact case TC18 13.7.1.1 requires when the flush period elapses with an empty queue. c-RCP is a protocol library, not a scheduler; actually emitting the heartbeat -- scheduling this composition against a real clock and driving a real transport with it -- is still left to the integrator driving rcp_avtp_transport_t.

requirements.title: RC Server trigger signals 0/1: PTP time-sync established and lost (Table 34)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not issue the RC Server trigger signals of TC18 Table 34 -- signal 0 on PTP time-synch established and signal 1 on PTP time-synch lost (signal 2 being t.b.d. in the specification). gPTP lock state is modeled (rcp_timed_admit()'s gptp_locked input) but no trigger source is derived from its transitions, so a triggered request cannot be armed on time-sync events.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() stores each COMPOUND_WAIT request's own evt and byte_msg_payload, and rejects a reserved evt
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() shall, for a decoded RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND_WAIT request, reject it (RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_REJECTED) when rcp_acf_compound_wait_evt_valid() is false for its decoded evt (TC18 §13.5.1: evt[2:0] = 011b is reserved -- "request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"), and otherwise store that request's own decoded evt and an owned copy of its byte_msg_payload (rcp_server_pending_t's compound_wait_evt/compound_wait_target) independently of every other pending request on the same endpoint.

requirements.title: Each pending COMPOUND_WAIT request is evaluated against the caller-supplied current status independently of any other pending request
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due()/rcp_server_endpoint_complete() shall evaluate a pending RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND_WAIT request's execution condition via rcp_acf_compound_wait_match(), passing that specific request's own stored evt/byte_msg_payload (not any other pending request's) together with ctx->current_status/current_status_len; two requests pending on the same endpoint with different byte_msg_payload targets shall never be conflated by a single shared result.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_pending_count() reports the conditional-request store's current occupancy
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_pending_count(ep) shall return the number of conditional requests currently held in ep's request store.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("Each endpoint receives request via its dedicated EP request storage."), TC18.txt L3193

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() reports RCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD for a compound-wait request's reserved evt
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() shall, when rejecting a decoded RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND_WAIT request because rcp_acf_compound_wait_evt_valid() is false for its decoded evt, write RCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD to *out_error (when non-NULL) so a caller can build and send a real TC18 error response (rcp_acf_build_error_response()) for this case, per TC18 §13.5.1's explicit requirement that such a request's err-response carry error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1 ("request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"), TC18.txt L3735-3736

requirements.title: A request carried under a TSCF header is postponed until the header's presentation time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not postpone the execution of a request carried under a TSCF header until the header's avtp_timestamp presentation time (TC18 §11.2, §11.2.1). Only the ACF_GBB-embedded presentation_time of §11.2.2.5 is honoured (rcp_timed_due(), rcp_server_endpoint_select_due()); the TSCF header's own avtp_timestamp is used solely as CRC input by rcp_e2e_compute_crc() and never reaches the admission or due-selection path, so standard, conditional and cancel requests arriving under TSCF execute immediately. Consequence: time-scheduled execution via TSCF -- the specification's primary timed-request mechanism -- does not work.

requirements.title: Standard requests, and timed requests under a TSCF header, are sent as ACF_ABB
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_timed_encode_request_tscf() (request_timed.h/request_timed.c) now provides the ACF_ABB timed-request encoder TC18 §11.2/§11.2.1 requires: it encodes a plain ACF_ABB message (rcp_acf_encode_abb(), no request_type opcode, no repurposing trick, unlike rcp_timed_encode_request()'s own NTSCF-only path) wrapped in a TSCF header (avtp.h's rcp_avtp_encode_tscf()) whose own avtp_timestamp carries the presentation time and whose tv bit is set valid. A thin, named composition of two already-existing, independently tested primitives, matching request_timed.h's own file-header framing of the TSCF path as "the OTHER of TC18's two ways to time a request." STILL PARTIAL: the wire shape is now correctly produced, but nothing on the decode/admission side interprets it as a timed request yet -- rcp_tsn_classify_frame() (tsn.c) classifies a TSCF-wrapped ACF_ABB frame as RCP_SCHED_KIND_STANDARD (correctly, at the request-KIND level -- "timed" is an orthogonal AVTP-header-level property, not a distinct kind), and REQ-TIMED-012's own separate, larger gap (TSCF's avtp_timestamp never reaches the admission/due-selection path at all) means a server built on this library does not yet honour the presentation time this encoder now correctly transmits.

requirements.title: The WakeUp message carries the wake-up source that caused the wake
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's WakeUp message carries no wake-up source (TC18 §12.4.1). rcp_ep_wakeup_encode_wakeup_message() emits a single opcode byte and rcp_ep_wakeup_decode_wakeup_message() returns only the transaction number, whereas the specification requires the repetitive wake response to convey both a WakeUp message and the WakeUp source. The client that requested sleep cannot learn which configured wake source (which sources[] index, wakepin, or network) actually woke the server, which is exactly the diagnostic information the wake-up endpoint exists to provide.

requirements.title: The WakeUp endpoint's functional config carries the WakeUp repetition time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's wake-up endpoint has no configurable WakeUp repetition time (TC18 §12.4.1). rcp_ep_wakeup_functional_cfg_t exposes only the wake-source table, and the handshake in power.c counts attempts without any notion of an interval, so a client cannot configure how often the repetitive wake response is retransmitted. Repetition rate is left entirely to the caller and is neither discoverable nor settable over the protocol.

requirements.title: A refused sleep/standby request is answered with an error response carrying REQUEST_CANCELED
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP answers a refused sleep/standby request with a positive-form SleepCMD response carrying RCP_PWRMODE_ENTRY_REFUSED, not with an error response (TC18 §12.5). The specification requires the rejection to be signalled as an error message with error code REQUEST_CANCELED (RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_CANCELED, include/rcp/errors.h:55). A conformant RC Client watching for an error response never sees the refusal, and a c-RCP client peer is the only thing that can decode the refusal at all.

requirements.title: WakeUp endpoint is fixed to endpoint number 1
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not pin the WakeUp endpoint to endpoint number 1 as TC18 13.7.2.1 requires; rcp_ep_wakeup_* entry points accept any caller-supplied byte_bus_id and the library defines no constant for the fixed WakeUp endpoint index, so the 'only endpoint that stays active in Sleep mode' invariant is the integrator's to uphold.

requirements.title: WakeUp functional-config register block (Table 36) incl. write-1-to-clear wup_status
requirements.text: PARTIAL, FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I dedicated investigation, task #95): the register block is now implemented -- rcp_ep_wakeup_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() serialize/parse wup_ep_len, wup_nr_io_pins_max, wup_ep_status (new field), wup_status, and every wup_io_scrN slot, reachable via the generic §12.7.1 evt[2:0]==111b mechanism. This closes TC18 Table 36's own genuine address collision between wup_status and wup_io_scr1 (both printed at the same relative address on both the 0.5.1_RC baseline and the 0.5.1_RC5 revision, confirmed via the rendered page image, not an extraction artifact) -- resolved via this session's own established cross-table pattern: wup_status keeps its own printed address (0x0004), the source array shifts to start immediately after it (0x0006), one slot per RCP_EP_WAKEUP_MAX_SOURCES (this module's own pre-existing upper bound, matching wup_nr_io_pins_max exactly). Remains PARTIAL, not fully implemented, because wup_status still renders/parses only its own pre-existing single-aggregate-latch bit (rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_t, unchanged API/behavior), not TC18's own full 16-bit per-source bitmask -- see REQ-WAKEUP-022 for the wup_io_scrN content's own remaining gap.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 36, TC18.txt L4096-4113; address-collision resolution confirmed against both the 0.5.1_RC baseline PDF p.84 and the 0.5.1_RC5 revision PDF p.93 (identical, unfixed by the spec committee, unlike MDIO's own Table 56/59 collision)

requirements.title: Wake-up source pin behavior encoding (Table 37)
requirements.text: PARTIAL, UPDATED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I dedicated investigation, task #95): rcp_ep_wakeup_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() now render/parse a real IO_SRC[15:11] wire field (RCP_EP_WAKEUP_IO_SRC_INACTIVE/_HIGH_LEVEL/_LOW_LEVEL) alongside a new pin_number[10:0] field (rcp_ep_wakeup_source_cfg_t gained pin_number), reaching 3 of Table 37's 6 defined values. Remains PARTIAL: rcp_ep_wakeup_source_cfg_t's own (enabled, active_high) pair -- and rcp_ep_wakeup_source_asserted(), the level-only predicate built on it -- are deliberately left entirely unchanged (not redesigned), since edge-triggered detection would need previous-pin-level state this module's own existing, already-tested API doesn't carry, and would ripple into every caller's own calling convention. A configuration write encoding an edge-triggered (0x01-0x03) or reserved (0x06-0x1F) IO_SRC value leaves that slot's own enabled/active_high fields unchanged (an honest 'cannot apply' outcome) while its pin_number still updates, rather than silently misinterpreting the request as a level mode.

requirements.title: The per-stream watchdog is kicked by every request received on that stream
requirements.text: The RC Server's request-reception path shall call rcp_watchdog_keeper_kick() for a request stream's stream_id on every request successfully received on that stream, so that the per-stream watchdog measures the gap between consecutive requests from that RC Client (TC18 §12.7.7, "the watchdog is reset with each request received from this RC Client"). NOT IMPLEMENTED as a wired behavior: rcp_watchdog_keeper_kick() exists and is individually correct (REQ-WDG-003) but has no production call site — only tests call it. Consequence: in an integration built on this library the watchdog overflows on a fixed schedule regardless of client liveness unless the integrator remembers to kick it, which no requirement obliges them to do.

requirements.title: rcp_watchdog_default_config() returns the documented default
requirements.text: rcp_watchdog_default_config() shall return poll_interval_ms = 10.

requirements.title: rcp_watchdog_keeper_destroy() closes the poll thread and releases every owned resource
requirements.text: rcp_watchdog_keeper_destroy(k) shall be a safe no-op when k is NULL; otherwise it shall close k (joining the background poll thread if one was started) and then free its states, callbacks, and callback_ctx arrays and destroy its mutex before freeing k itself.

requirements.title: Plain versus safe command mode is selected per endpoint in the generic endpoint config and gates CRC enforcement
requirements.text: Each endpoint shall be addressable in exactly one of two modes selected by a bit in its server-owned generic endpoint configuration: plain command mode, in which requests carry no CRC32 trailer, and safe command mode, in which every request must carry a valid CRC32 trailer and a request without one, or with a mismatching one, shall not be executed (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: mock.c's rcp_mock_server_set_endpoint_req_crc_enable() sets this test double's own in-process gate (its type-erased dispatch layer has no way to read rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t's ep_req_crc_enable field generically across endpoint types, so it keeps its own copy -- the same reasoning every other config field this module models already follows), and rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e() consults it: plain mode executes an unprotected request unchanged, safe mode rejects one (RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_CRC_ERROR, request never even reaches rcp_server_endpoint_admit()).

requirements.title: Safe command mode changes nothing but the appended CRC trailer and the length accounting
requirements.text: A request in safe command mode shall be byte-identical to the same request in plain command mode in its AVTPDU header fields, its ACF message type, its byte_message_info header and its byte_msg_payload, differing only by the appended CRC32 trailer and by the length-accounting adaptation that trailer requires (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_e2e_wrap() copies acf_frame verbatim, adapts only acf_msg_length via its private adapt_acf_msg_length(), and appends four octets; rcp_e2e_unwrap() reverses exactly those two steps.

requirements.title: Each ACF message in a multi-ACF AVTPDU carries and is verified against its own CRC32
requirements.text: When an AVTPDU carries more than one ACF message, a separate CRC32 shall be computed, appended to and verified for each E2E-protected ACF message individually, never one CRC across the whole AVTPDU payload (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_e2e_wrap()/rcp_e2e_unwrap() already worked at this granularity; rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame_e2e() now composes that across a real multi-member frame -- each member, split via rcp_sched_split_frame_members(), is routed through rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e() independently, so a corrupted trailer on one member neither blocks nor is masked by another member's valid one.

requirements.title: CRC coverage begins with stream_id (8 octets) and avtp_timestamp (4 octets), big-endian
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_compute_crc() shall return the same value as rcp_e2e_crc32() over the concatenation of stream_id as 8 big-endian octets, avtp_timestamp as 4 big-endian octets (IEEE 1722's own field width), and acf_frame[0..acf_frame_len), in that order (TC18 §13.6).

requirements.title: An NTSCF-framed message contributes an all-zero avtp_timestamp to the CRC
requirements.text: When the enclosing AVTPDU carries an NTSCF header (which has no timestamp field of its own), the avtp_timestamp contribution to the CRC32 shall be four all-zero octets (TC18 §13.6). rcp_e2e_wrap_framed()/rcp_e2e_unwrap_framed() enforce this: a caller passes is_ntscf_framed=true and the wrapper forces the zero contribution regardless of what avtp_timestamp it was given. The lower-level rcp_e2e_compute_crc()/rcp_e2e_wrap()/rcp_e2e_unwrap() primitives remain general-purpose (a plain uint32_t avtp_timestamp, since they serve both TSCF- and NTSCF-framed callers) and still trust the caller to pass 0 for NTSCF traffic -- the framing-aware wrappers are the conformant entry point for a caller that already knows a message's framing.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wrap() adapts acf_msg_length by +1 quadlet before computing the CRC, and rcp_e2e_unwrap() reverses it
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wrap() shall increment the acf_msg_length field of the copy it returns by one quadlet before computing the CRC, so the CRC is computed over the length-adapted frame and a conformant receiver reads a length that already includes the trailer; it shall fail safe (data=NULL, len=0) when the frame is shorter than the two octets holding that field or when the adapted value would exceed the field's 9-bit maximum (0x1FF). rcp_e2e_unwrap() shall decrement it by one quadlet on the copy it returns, so the result is byte-identical to the frame the sender passed to rcp_e2e_wrap().

requirements.title: AVTPDU data length grows by 4 octets for every E2E-protected ACF message it carries
requirements.text: An AVTPDU carrying E2E-protected ACF messages shall have its ntscf_data_length (NTSCF header) or stream_data_length (TSCF header) increased by 4 octets for every ACF message in its payload that is E2E-protected (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf()/rcp_avtp_encode_tscf() already satisfied this correctly and automatically -- both recompute the length field from the actual payload buffer they are given (never from a caller-supplied value), so the adjustment is right whenever the caller concatenated rcp_e2e_wrap()'s own output per protected member first. As of this fix, that rule also has its own named, pure, directly-testable expression: rcp_e2e_data_length_for_protected_members(protected_member_count), returning protected_member_count * RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN (saturating on overflow) -- usable by a caller wanting to pre-size a buffer or independently cross-check a peer's own encoded length.

requirements.title: A fragmented message's CRC covers the first fragment's AVTPDU/ACF header plus every segment's payload
requirements.text: For a fragmented request or response the CRC32 shall be computed over the stream_id and avtp_timestamp of the FIRST AVTPDU and the FIRST fragment's ACF header, followed by the concatenated byte_msg_payload of ALL segments in order; the resulting CRC shall be appended only to the last segment's message, and only that last message's acf_msg_length and only that last AVTPDU's data-length field shall be adapted (TC18 §13.6). PARTIAL (was not-implemented): rcp_e2e_compute_fragmented_crc() (e2e.h/e2e.c) now computes exactly the required span -- stream_id + avtp_timestamp + the first fragment's ACF header + the full concatenated payload of every segment, the same running-CRC technique rcp_e2e_compute_crc() itself already uses for its own three regions. What remains not implemented: nothing in this codebase calls it yet. c-RCP's documented integration (fragment.h) still only ever wraps the final fragment's own encoded bytes via rcp_e2e_wrap(), and mock.c has no fragmented-message dispatch path at all (protected or not) to wire the new primitive into -- a materially larger, separate architecture item (building fragmented-message dispatch in mock.c from scratch) than adding this one CRC-arithmetic primitive.

requirements.title: The ms bit decides whether a message carries a CRC32 trailer in its last quadlet
requirements.text: A message whose ACF header ms bit is 0 shall carry the CRC32 in its last quadlet, and a message whose ms bit is 1 shall carry no CRC32 at all, the CRC appearing only on the final (ms=0) fragment of a multi-segment message (TC18 §13.6). ONLY A CALLER CONVENTION in c-RCP: rcp_e2e_fragment_carries_crc() takes an abstract is_last_fragment boolean and neither reads the ms bit itself nor is invoked anywhere in src/ — the ms-to-is_last_fragment binding lives only in fragment.h's file header prose.

requirements.title: Requests and responses use one identical CRC scheme
requirements.text: The CRC32 coverage span, parameterization, length adaptation and trailer placement shall be identical for requests and for responses: rcp_e2e_wrap() and rcp_e2e_unwrap() shall take no direction parameter and shall behave identically whichever direction a frame travels in (TC18 §13.6).

requirements.title: A CRC mismatch on a protected stream generates an error response as well as skipping execution
requirements.text: When a request arrives on an E2E-protected stream and its CRC32 does not match, the RC Server shall not execute the request AND shall generate an error response carrying the CRC-mismatch wire error code (RCP_ERROR_POCI_FAILURE, 12 — the code TC18 §12.9.6 Table 27 assigns a CRC mismatch, spelled CRC_ERROR in §13.6's prose) (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_e2e_unwrap() already reported RCP_E2E_ERR_CRC_MISMATCH and rcp_e2e_wire_error() already mapped it; rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e() is now the caller and error-response emitter that were missing -- on a mismatch it never calls rcp_server_endpoint_admit() at all (not admitted, not merely not-executed) and builds a genuine TC18 §12.9.6 Error Response (err=1, rsp=1, payload=RCP_ERROR_POCI_FAILURE, byte_bus_id/transaction_num carried through from the request) via rcp_acf_build_error_response().

requirements.title: CRC coverage includes the byte_msg_payload's pad octets and the trailer lands on a quadlet boundary
requirements.text: The CRC32 shall be computed over whole quadlets of the ACF message: the byte_message_info header quadlets and the byte_msg_payload including the 0x00 pad octets acf.h's rcp_acf_pad_len() appends, so that the CRC32 itself occupies the message's final whole quadlet (TC18 §13.6 Figures 19 and 20). rcp_e2e_wrap() enforces this by rejecting (zeroed rcp_bytes_t) any acf_frame_len that is not a whole quadlet, rather than appending a trailer that would straddle a quadlet boundary.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_init() starts a fault tracker in the not-faulted state
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_init(f) shall set f->faulted to false.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 22 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 0b: stream is not blocked..."), TC18.txt L2861-2864 -- the initial, not-yet-faulted state this register default implies

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_is_faulted() reports the tracker's current state
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_is_faulted(f) shall return f->faulted unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 22 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 1b: stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails."), TC18.txt L2865-2867

requirements.title: PARTIAL: rcp_e2e_crc_error_should_enter_safe_state() names rx_enforce_e2e's second consequence, but nothing drives the cross-endpoint escalation
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_e2e_crc_error_should_enter_safe_state() shall return rx_enforce_e2e unchanged. ADDED 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22's own 0x000D.0 rx_enforce_e2e description names two distinct consequences for its 1b value in the same sentence -- "stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails" (REQ-E2E-021's rcp_e2e_stream_fault_on_crc_error()/rcp_e2e_stream_fault_t) AND "Safe state will be entered" -- and only the first had a primitive at all before this entry; the second was entirely uncited and unimplemented. This function is the pure, directly-testable decision such an escalation would be gated on, matching REQ-E2E-030's own rcp_e2e_overflow_should_enter_safe_state() precedent exactly (rx_enforce_e2e carries no separate _safestate_enable bit of its own -- unlike rx_wd_safestate_enable/rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable/rx_seq_safestate_enable, the single rx_enforce_e2e bit gates both consequences at once, so this decision is simply rx_enforce_e2e's own value). What remains not implemented, identically to REQ-E2E-030's and REQ-E2E-021's own admissions: the stream-wide half of the rule -- bringing every OTHER endpoint bound to the same request stream into its configured safe state -- which this library's current single-endpoint-scoped data model has no type representing "all endpoints on a stream" to perform from inside any single endpoint's own admission/dispatch path. That escalation needs a caller-owned, cross-endpoint orchestrator that does not yet exist in this codebase.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 22 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 1b: stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails. Safe state will be entered."), TC18.txt L2865-2867

requirements.title: NOT IMPLEMENTED: rx_stream_status aggregate blocked-status bit (new in TC18 0.5.1_RC5)
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (spec rebaseline to TC18 0.5.1_RC5, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, task #97): TC18 0.5.1_RC5's own Table 24 (§12.7.7, renumbered from the 0.5.1_RC baseline's Table 22) adds a new read-only rx_stream_status bit at 0x000D.7 with no counterpart at all in the baseline this codebase was originally built against -- "0b: stream is active / 1b: stream is blocked, requests are rejected", set automatically as a reaction to a CRC error, sequence error, watchdog overflow, or EP request-storage overflow, whichever of those four is enabled. This is a genuinely new, passive, client-polled aggregate status covering all four fault classes uniformly -- distinct from, and not directly implementable by, this module's own existing per-cause primitives: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_t (e2e.h) already provides a persisted latch for the CRC case specifically, but sequence-number discontinuity (rcp_e2e_seq_evaluate()), watchdog overflow (rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate()), and request-storage overflow (rcp_e2e_overflow_should_enter_safe_state()) each currently report only a per-call "should enter safe state now" decision, with no equivalent persisted "stream is currently blocked" latch of their own to aggregate into one combined status bit. Implementing this correctly needs a new, cross-cutting per-stream aggregate-latch primitive this codebase does not yet have; not attempted in this batch, to avoid a rushed design of new ASIL-relevant state-tracking infrastructure. See regmap.h's own "TC18 0.5.1_RC5 terminology drift" file-header note (task #97) for the full investigation this entry is part of.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24, spec revision 0.5.1_RC5 PDF p.67 ("0x000D.7 rx_stream_status ... set automatically as a reaction to either CRC error, sequence error, watchdog overflow, EP overflow, when enabled", ticket-tagged 051RC4 "config bit added")

requirements.title: the ADC endpoint's five trigger output signals
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP defines none of the five ADC trigger outputs TC18 §13.7.9.1 Table 50 enumerates. The ADC endpoint shall generate trigger 0 when the averaged output value falls below adc_trigger_min, trigger 1 when it rises above adc_trigger_min, trigger 2 when it falls below adc_trigger_max, trigger 3 when it rises above adc_trigger_max, and trigger 4 when it finishes a measurement interval. ep_adc.h has no trigger enumeration, no threshold registers, and no evaluation function. Consequence: threshold-crossing detection is impossible, and the spec's own documented cyclic-ADC pattern — 'configured to generate responses cyclically ... by using a trigger request which triggers on the ADC EP itself having finished a measurement' (L5033-5034) — cannot be built, because trigger 4 does not exist.

requirements.title: An ADC endpoint serves exactly one channel, is limited to 16-bit resolution, and requires a selected analog input pin
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (partially): c-RCP fixes an ADC measurement value at 16 bits (RCP_EP_ADC_VALUE_LEN == 2, ep_adc.h:211) consistent with TC18 §13.7.9.1's 16-bit ceiling, but it does not model the one-channel-per-endpoint rule nor the required selection of an analog input pin for each ADC EP. regmap.h's rcp_regmap_named_signal_t index has no ADC entry, so an ADC endpoint's analog input cannot be bound to a hardware pin through the hw_pin_map table at all. Consequence: an RC Client can configure and read an ADC endpoint that is not wired to any physical input, with no way to discover or set which channel it serves.

requirements.title: ADC inter-sample spacing is one adc_sample_interval, in multiples of adc_base_clk x adc_base_clk_divider
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the ADC sampling cadence TC18 §13.7.9.1 defines. When adc_avg_intervals_per_request x adc_samples_per_avg_interval exceeds 1, successive samples shall be taken one adc_sample_interval apart, where that interval is expressed in multiples of adc_base_clk scaled by adc_base_clk_divider. rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_t carries neither adc_sample_interval nor adc_base_clk nor adc_base_clk_divider, and rcp_ep_adc_average_interval() consumes caller-supplied samples whose spacing this module never constrains. Consequence: the temporal geometry of an ADC response (the entire point of the sample_interval/averaging model) is undefined in this implementation.

requirements.title: ADC sampling occurs only while a request executes, and a compound wait compares the last acquired average without sampling
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 §13.7.9.1's request-gated sampling rule. The ADC endpoint shall sample its input only while a request is being executed, so that no ADC trigger can fire in the absence of a request to sample; and a compound wait request on an ADC endpoint shall not start sampling, comparing instead against the last acquired average value. ep_adc.h provides neither a request-execution state nor any comparison predicate (contrast ep_lin.h's rcp_ep_lin_compare_fires(), REQ-LINEP-002..005). Consequence: continuous monitoring semantics are undefined, and a compound wait targeting an ADC endpoint has no defined match behavior.

requirements.title: adc_ep_len, adc_base_clk, adc_ep_status and adc_base_clk_divider register rows of Table 51 are now modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): c-RCP now models the ADC functional-configuration block's descriptor, clock and status registers (TC18 §13.7.9.2 Table 51) via rcp_ep_adc_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() (REQ-ADC-038/039): adc_ep_len (0x0000, 8 bit, R), the reserved octet at 0x0001 (8 bit, R), adc_base_clk (0x0004, 16 bit, R — not itself stored, always renders 0, the same 'no real clock source modelled' honesty ep_gpio.h's/ep_i2c.h's/ep_lin.h's own base_clk fields already commit to), adc_ep_status (0x0006, 16 bit, R/W, new field), and adc_base_clk_divider (0x0008, 8 bit, R/W, new field). Unlike SPI's/UART's/LIN's own diverging fields, rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_t's pre-existing adc_samples_per_avg_interval/adc_avg_intervals_per_request/adc_combine_avg_values fields share Table 51's own register names exactly and are reused directly by the register block (with an honestly-documented 8-bit truncation on render for the two wider uint16_t fields, since their setters apply no range check).

requirements.title: adc_sample_interval, the ADC_CLK cycle count between two samples, is now modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): c-RCP now models adc_sample_interval (TC18 §13.7.9.2 Table 51, relative address 0x0009, 8 bit, R/W) — the number of ADC_CLK cycles the endpoint shall wait between two consecutive samples — as rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_t.sample_interval, reachable via the register block (REQ-ADC-038/039). There is still no dedicated rcp_ep_adc_set_sample_interval() named setter (matching every other endpoint type's own precedent: a register-block-only field has no dedicated named setter, only the generic §12.7.1 write path reaches it), but the sample spacing §13.7.9.1's worked examples set to 1 us is now configurable over the wire.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_render_registers()/_encode_reconfig_request() implement the generic §12.7.1 configuration request for ADC
