requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request -- evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data -- usable against every endpoint type. rcp_ep_adc_decode_read_request() already correctly rejected evt[2:0] = 111b as RCP_EP_ADC_ERR_BAD_EVT (via acf.h's rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain()), but no counterpart function implemented that path at all. rcp_ep_adc_render_registers() serializes cfg's whole Table 51 block; rcp_ep_adc_encode_reconfig_request() encodes an ACF_ABB write request (op=WRITE, evt=111b) carrying a 16-bit big-endian start address followed by data, matching PWM_OUT's/GPIO's/SPI's/I2C's/UART's/LIN's own encode_reconfig_request() shape.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 18, TC18.txt L2463-2484

requirements.title: rcp_ep_adc_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror() apply the addressed configuration write and never return NULL for a status message
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_adc_apply_reconfig() decodes the address+data payload TC18 §12.7.1 defines and patches cfg's Table 51 register block at octet granularity, then adopts the whole block atomically -- a write whose start_address+length exceeds RCP_EP_ADC_EP_FUNC_LEN is rejected and cfg left entirely unchanged (RCP_EP_ADC_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE), matching §12.7.1's own 'such a payload is to be ignored' rule; octets landing on a read-only register (EP_LEN, the reserved octet, or base_clk) are silently skipped while the rest of the span is still applied. rcp_ep_adc_reconfig_strerror() never returns NULL, including for an unrecognized error code.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints, TC18.txt L2463-2484

requirements.title: adc_resolution, adc_trigger_min and adc_trigger_max registers of Table 51 are now modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): a previously-uncatalogued gap, found while scoping REQ-ADC-035/036's own register-block fix -- TC18 §13.7.9.2 Table 51 defines three further R/W registers rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_t carried no counterpart for at all: adc_resolution (0x000D, 8 bit, R/W -- the number of bits used of the ADC reading value, <=16), adc_trigger_min (0x000E, 16 bit, R/W -- the threshold below which the ADC trigger signal is set low), and adc_trigger_max (0x0010, 16 bit, R/W -- the threshold above which it is set high). Now modeled as rcp_ep_adc_functional_cfg_t.resolution/trigger_min/trigger_max, reachable via rcp_ep_adc_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() (REQ-ADC-038/039). No dedicated named setter exists for any of the three (matching every other register-block-only field's own precedent across every endpoint type this session has fixed); only the generic §12.7.1 write path reaches them. Note this does not implement the trigger-signal evaluation logic itself (REQ-ADC-031's own five-trigger-output gap remains open) -- only the threshold/resolution configuration storage and its wire reachability.

requirements.title: NOT IMPLEMENTED: the request/response cadence scheduling adc_combine_avg_values vs. adc_avg_intervals_per_request implies
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §13.7.9.2 (immediately below Table 51) states three cadence cases comparing adc_combine_avg_values against adc_avg_intervals_per_request: when combine_avg_values > avg_intervals_per_request, several request executions must be accumulated before one response is generated (that response carrying the transaction_num of the request that produced its first included average value); when they are equal, exactly one response per request execution; when combine_avg_values < avg_intervals_per_request, one request execution yields multiple responses. ep_adc.h's own file header already honestly documents all three cases in prose ("The three documented cadence cases follow directly from the two counts and need no code of their own here -- this module models the codec and the arithmetic, never the scheduling"), but no function anywhere in this module -- nor any .fusa-reqs.json entry until this one -- decides which of the three cases applies for a given (combine_avg_values, avg_intervals_per_request) pair, or computes how many request executions a multi-request response should span, or which transaction_num such a response should carry. rcp_ep_adc_collect_response_values() packs whatever avg_values array a caller already assembled; it does not itself decide when that array is "ready" to become a response under any of the three cases. This is the same class of caller-owned-orchestration gap already tracked for REQ-E2E-021/030/045 and REQ-CANCEL-012 -- a real scheduling decision TC18 requires, with no type in this library representing the caller-side state (multiple in-flight request executions feeding one pending response, or one execution's values fanning out across several) such logic would need.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.2 ("When adc_combine_avg_values > adc_avg_intervals_per_request... When adc_combine_avg_values = adc_avg_intervals_per_request... When adc_combine_avg_values < adc_avg_intervals_per_request..."), TC18.txt L5128-5133

requirements.title: can_ep_len, can_base_clk and the CAN endpoint's three status registers
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the CAN functional-configuration block's descriptor, clock and status registers (TC18 §13.7.11.2 Table 53): can_ep_len (0x0000, 8 bit, R), the reserved octet at 0x0001 (8 bit, R, reads 0x00), can_base_clk (0x0004, 16 bit, R — the CAN system clock), can_ep_status (0x0006, 16 bit, R/W), the 32-bit CAN EP status at 0x001C (R/W), and the 32-bit FIFO status at 0x0020 (R/W). rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_t holds only bit timings, delay compensation, the execution-delay divider and the XL filter table. Consequence: bus-off, error-passive and FIFO-overflow conditions — the states those status registers exist to report — are unobservable through this endpoint, and the base clock the three bit-timing register sets divide cannot be read.

requirements.title: the CAN endpoint's receive ID filters, which are separate from the CAN XL acceptance filters and valid for all CAN variants
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP conflates two distinct filter tables TC18 §13.7.11.2 keeps separate, AND that table's own printed addresses for one of them are internally inconsistent. Table 53/56 prints acceptance filter 1 at 0x0024, filter 2 at 0x0028, and BOTH filter 3 and filter 4 at 0x002C (a genuine address collision, re-verified against the rendered PDF page image on both the baseline and newest available revision, not an extraction artifact) as 'acceptance filter for CAN XL', immediately followed by receive filters 1..4 at 0x0030..0x003C as 'ID filter for frame reception', the latter explicitly 'valid for all CAN variants' per the §13.7.11.2 bullet list. Which of two readings is intended -- only 3 real acceptance filters with the receive-filter table already correctly addressed, or 4 real acceptance filters requiring every receive-filter address to shift forward by one slot -- is undecidable from the primary source alone; see ep_can.h's own file header for the full analysis. c-RCP implements only one filter table — rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_t.xl_filters[RCP_EP_CAN_XL_MAX_FILTERS], written by rcp_ep_can_set_xl_filter() (REQ-CANEP-014) — and its own header describes it as the CAN-XL acceptance/ID filter set; no code anywhere serializes either table's byte offsets, so the address ambiguity itself carries no live wire-conformance risk today. Consequence: Classical CAN, CAN FD and CAN FD light traffic cannot be ID-filtered on reception at all through this endpoint; the only filter table available is scoped to CAN XL.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2, TC18.txt L5355 and Table 53 (acceptance filter 3/4 address collision at 0x002C, receive filter 1..4), TC18.txt L5385-5418

requirements.title: Usage of the new CAN XL physical layer is a functional-configuration setting of the CAN endpoint
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED (as configuration): TC18 §13.7.11.2 lists 'usage of new PL (YES|NO) for CAN XL' among the settings the CAN endpoint's functional configuration comprises, i.e. a per-endpoint, runtime-writable choice. c-RCP instead expresses the physical-layer selection per FRAME, as the distinction between RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_CLASSICAL_PL (4) and RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_NEW_PL (5) carried in the ACF evt[2:0] field (ep_can.h:304-311), and rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_t carries no corresponding flag. Consequence: a client cannot read back or constrain which XL physical layer an endpoint is provisioned for, and nothing rejects a frame whose XL variant contradicts the endpoint's actual physical layer.

requirements.title: The FrameFormat selector's numeric code assignment (CBFF 0 through XL new-PL 5, with 6 and 7 reserved), carried in the payload's leading quadlet
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_t shall assign exactly the FrameFormat codes TC18 §13.7.11.3 Table 54 fixes: RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_CBFF = 0, RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_CEFF = 1, RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_FBFF = 2, RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_FEFF = 3, RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_CLASSICAL_PL = 4 (XL over the classical physical layer), and RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_NEW_PL = 5 (XL over the new physical layer); codes 6 and 7 are reserved and rcp_ep_can_frame_format_valid() shall reject them, causing rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_request()/_decode_frame_response()/_decode_reassembled_frame_response() to return RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_FRAME_FORMAT. The selector shall be carried in the top 3 bits of the payload's leading quadlet (TC18 §13.7.11.3 Figure 39), sharing that quadlet with a 29-bit arbitration_id. CORRECTED (v0.109.0): this requirement previously (and incorrectly) asserted the selector was carried in the ACF byte_message_info evt field's low three bits -- verified against Figure 39 directly, that claim was never true of TC18 and was itself the bug (evt[2:0] instead carries CAN's ordinary TC18 §13.5 Table 30 Row-2 meaning: 000b plain, 111b configuration-write, else UNSUPPORTED_CMD). Found and fixed while investigating this repo's Table 30 centralization.

requirements.title: Remote frames are not supported, and an 11-bit CAN ID is right-aligned in the CAN ID field
requirements.text: The CAN endpoint shall not support sending remote frames: c-RCP exposes no remote-frame flag, encode function, or decode outcome anywhere in ep_can.h/ep_can.c, so every frame this endpoint encodes or decodes is a data frame. An 11-bit CAN identifier shall be right-aligned within the CAN ID field: rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_request()/_encode_frame_response() write arbitration_id via write_prefix()'s big-endian put_u32() into the fixed 4-octet identifier prefix, leaving the unused high bits zero, and rcp_ep_can_arbitration_id_valid() bounds a base-width identifier at 0x7FF so no bit can escape that alignment.

requirements.title: ISELED read responses are aggregated into one or more ACF messages up to the requested read_size
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement TC18 §13.7.12.1's ISELED response-aggregation rule. Responses received from the ISELED network shall be 5/4-bit decoded and aggregated into one or multiple ACF messages, bounded by the read_size the originating read request carried. rcp_ep_iseled_encode_response() (src/ep_iseled.c) encodes exactly the rx_data/rx_len its caller supplies, never reads a read_size, never enforces a ceiling, and has no multi-message emission path. Consequence: nothing prevents an ISELED response from exceeding the octets its request asked for, and the number of ACF messages a read produces is undefined.

requirements.title: iseled_collect_resp, the multi-response-per-ACF collection enable
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (FIXED 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): c-RCP now models iseled_collect_resp (TC18 §13.7.12.2 Table 55, corrected relative address 0x0009 bit 3, 1 bit, R/W -- see REQ-ISELED-029's own note on the table's address-collision editorial defect) as rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_t.collect_resp, reachable via the generic evt[2:0]=111b register-block mechanism (rcp_ep_iseled_apply_reconfig()/_render_registers()) rather than a dedicated set_collect_resp() mutator, matching every other register-block field this codebase models (no individual per-field setters, only the whole-block addressed write). A client can now choose between one ACF message per device response and one message per chain read.

requirements.title: iseled_nr_leds and iseled_rcv_timeout
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (FIXED 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): c-RCP now models both ISELED chain/reception registers TC18 §13.7.12.2 Table 55 defines, at their corrected relative addresses (see REQ-ISELED-029's own note on the table's address-collision editorial defect): iseled_nr_leds (0x000A, 16 bit, R/W, rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_t.nr_leds) records the number of LED devices in the chain, bounding the maximum number of responses to expect from a read; iseled_rcv_timeout (0x000C, 16 bit, R/W, rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_t.rcv_timeout) gives a receive timeout in ISELED clock tics after which reception ends and the endpoint returns to IDLE. Both are reachable via the generic evt[2:0]=111b register-block mechanism (rcp_ep_iseled_apply_reconfig()/_render_registers()), matching every other register-block field this codebase models. An ISELED read now has a defined completion bound in both the count dimension and the time dimension, though nothing in this codebase yet consults these two fields to actually enforce either bound at runtime -- that remains a distinct, deeper behavior gap (see REQ-ISELED-025, still not-implemented).

requirements.title: RETIRED: stale duplicate of REQ-ISELED-007
requirements.text: RETIRED (2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): this entry was a stale duplicate of REQ-ISELED-007. It described the same rcp_ep_iseled_requires_isp_n() inverted-polarity bug as "not-implemented", but REQ-ISELED-007 (Group G, PR #270, v0.213.0) already fixed the function to return use_rcv_clk directly, and its own status field carries no "not-implemented"/"partial" marker at all (this codebase's own convention for an ordinary implemented entry) -- this entry's own text was simply never updated or retired to match, leaving a requirement that flatly contradicted its own sibling entry about the identical bug. Discovered while scoping this batch's own ISELED register-block work, the same class of stale-duplicate finding as REQ-RMAP-046 (Group H). See REQ-ISELED-007 for the current, accurate status. No code change from this retirement -- text-only correction.

requirements.title: ISELED EP_func register block reachable via evt[2:0]=111b (Table 55, address-collision defect corrected)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (FIXED 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_iseled_decode_command_request() already correctly rejected evt[2:0]=111b (RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_BAD_EVT, via acf.h's rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain()), but no counterpart implemented that §12.7.1 configuration-write path. TC18 §13.7.12.2 Table 55 has a genuine address-collision editorial defect (visually confirmed, not an extraction artifact, the fourth instance of this class found this audit after ep_pwm.h's/ep_gpio.h's/ep_i2c.h's own): iseled_base_clk (16 bit, R) is printed at relative address 0x0001, one octet after iseled_ep_len, with no reserved octet at 0x0001 the way every other endpoint type's own Table prints one -- colliding with iseled_ep_enable&clr, separately printed at 0x0002. Resolved via the same cross-table structural precedent already established: iseled_base_clk moves to 0x0004-0x0005 (matching the common EP_LEN/reserved/enable&clr/options/base_clk prefix sequence every other endpoint type's Table uses), pushing every field the table lists after it down by three octets in the table's own row order: iseled_ep_status to 0x0006-0x0007, iseled_clk_divider to 0x0008, the bitfield octet (iseled_collect_resp bit 3, iseled_use_rcv_clk bit 4) to 0x0009, iseled_nr_leds to 0x000A-0x000B, iseled_rcv_timeout to 0x000C-0x000D (RCP_EP_ISELED_EP_FUNC_LEN = 0x000E). New rcp_ep_iseled_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror()/_encode_reconfig_request() implement the same generic addressed-write mechanism PWM_OUT/GPIO/SPI/I2C/UART/LIN/ADC/PWM_IN already had -- ISELED is now 8 of 11 endpoint types with it. rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_t gains base_clk/ep_status/wire_clk_divider/collect_resp/nr_leds/rcv_timeout; iseled_use_rcv_clk is reused directly for the block's own flags bit (it already names that exact wire bit -- see REQ-ISELED-007); iseled_bit_clk_divider (uint32_t, this module's own outbound-transmission clock choice) is kept deliberately distinct from the new, uint8_t wire_clk_divider carrying the real 0x0008 register, per this audit's established "don't silently redefine an existing field whose own documented semantics diverge from the real wire register" rule; iseled_crc_enable (this module's own original, second, independent CRC-8 integrity layer) is deliberately NOT part of this register block -- Table 55 defines no register for it, and it is never rendered onto or parsed from the wire here.

requirements.title: The LIN transmission-done trigger fires only after the configured trailing time has also expired
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (Phase 5e batch 2, issue #201): TC18 §13.7.10.1 requires the LIN endpoint's trigger to fire when BOTH conditions hold — the transmission has been finalized AND the configured trailing time has expired. rcp_ep_lin_trigger_fires() (src/ep_lin.c) now takes trailing_time_expired as a second, caller-classified boolean parameter and ANDs it with tx_done_event for RCP_EP_LIN_TRIGGER_TX_DONE — the same caller-supplies-already-classified-inputs convention every endpoint module in this codebase already follows for its own trigger evaluation. Table 52 (§13.7.10.2) defines no dedicated wire register for "the configured trailing time" itself — like this endpoint type's own trigger concept as a whole (no TC18 basis at all, entirely this module's own original design — see ep_lin.h's own file header), a wire-configurable duration was never something TC18 gives this codebase a register to model; the caller classifying trailing-time-expired is this module's established architecture, not a remaining gap.

requirements.title: lin_ep_len, lin_base_clk, lin_ep_status, and lin_clk_divider (Table 52) are now modeled and wire-reachable
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): c-RCP now models the LIN functional-configuration block's whole register set (TC18 §13.7.10.2 Table 52) via rcp_ep_lin_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() (REQ-LINEP-028/029): lin_ep_len (0x0000, 8 bit, R), the reserved octet at 0x0001 (8 bit, R), lin_base_clk (0x0004, 16 bit, R — not itself stored, always renders 0, the same 'no real clock source modelled' honesty ep_gpio.h's/ep_i2c.h's own base_clk fields already commit to), lin_ep_status (0x0006, 16 bit, R/W, new field), and lin_clk_divider (0x0008, 8 bit, R/W). This session's own prior text credited the pre-existing rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_t.lin_clk_divider (REQ-LINEP-011/012) with already covering the last register — imprecisely: that field is this module's own original, uint32_t, unit-unspecified design (documented as matching ep_spi.h's own non-wire clock_divider shape), not the literal 8-bit wire register. A new, distinct wire_clk_divider (uint8_t) field carries the real register instead, the same 'don't silently redefine an existing public field' caution SPI's own baud_rate_kbps-vs-clock_divider split and UART's own baud_rate_kbps-vs-baud_rate split already established.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_render_registers()/_encode_reconfig_request() implement the generic §12.7.1 configuration request for LIN
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request -- evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data -- usable against every endpoint type. rcp_ep_lin_decode_command_request() already correctly rejected evt[2:0] = 111b as not a plain command request (RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_BAD_EVT, via acf.h's rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain()), but no counterpart function implemented that path at all. rcp_ep_lin_render_registers() serializes cfg's whole Table 52 block; rcp_ep_lin_encode_reconfig_request() encodes an ACF_ABB write request (op=WRITE, evt=111b) carrying a 16-bit big-endian start address followed by data, matching PWM_OUT's/GPIO's/SPI's/I2C's/UART's own encode_reconfig_request() shape.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 18, TC18.txt L2463-2484

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror() apply the addressed configuration write and never return NULL for a status message
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_lin_apply_reconfig() decodes the address+data payload TC18 §12.7.1 defines and patches cfg's Table 52 register block at octet granularity, then adopts the whole block atomically -- a write whose start_address+length exceeds RCP_EP_LIN_EP_FUNC_LEN is rejected and cfg left entirely unchanged (RCP_EP_LIN_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE), matching §12.7.1's own 'such a payload is to be ignored' rule; octets landing on a read-only register (EP_LEN, the reserved octet, or base_clk) are silently skipped while the rest of the span is still applied. rcp_ep_lin_reconfig_strerror() never returns NULL, including for an unrecognized error code.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints, TC18.txt L2463-2484

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_response_matches() delegates to acf.h's shared TC18 §13.5.1 exact-match primitive
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_response_matches(tx_data, tx_len, rx_data, rx_len) shall return rcp_acf_compound_wait_match(0, tx_data, tx_len, rx_data, rx_len) -- the exact-match mode (evt[2:0] = 000b) of acf.h's shared TC18 §13.5.1 comparison primitive, including its length-capping rule. This is the only comparison a plain LIN command request's evt[2:0] can select, since Table 30 constrains it to 000b (REQ-LINEP-027).

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_encode_command_request() no longer accepts a client-selectable comparison mode
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_encode_command_request() shall have no compare_mode parameter of any kind; it always encodes evt = 0. See REQ-LINEP-016.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_decode_command_request() rejects evt[2:0] != 000b with RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_BAD_EVT
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_decode_command_request() shall return RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_BAD_EVT when rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain(hdr.evt) is false, per TC18 §13.5 Table 30's rule for the {ADC, PWM_IN, I2C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO} endpoint-type row: evt[2:0] = 000b is the only value a plain (non-configuration) LIN command request may carry. LIN is not called out as an exception anywhere in Table 30, and TC18 §13.7.10.1's own reference to "the conditions given by evt[2:0]" describes the same universal §13.5.1 vocabulary Table 30 constrains to 000b here, not a LIN-private multi-mode scheme.

requirements.title: The MDIO EP has no configurable parameters beyond the common block, but still exposes mdio_ep_len and mdio_ep_status
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (FIXED 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): c-RCP correctly gives the MDIO endpoint no endpoint-specific *configurable* parameters, matching TC18 §13.7.13.2's 'The MDIO EP does not have any configurable parameters' — that statement describes what a write can change, not whether the block is readable. Table 56's three register rows are now all reachable via the generic evt[2:0]=111b register-block mechanism: mdio_ep_len (0x0000, 8 bit, R), the reserved octet at 0x0001 (8 bit, R, reads 0x00), and mdio_ep_status (0x0004, 16 bit, R/W, contents still to be defined by the specification — c-RCP round-trips whatever value is written, since the specification itself defines no interpretation). A genuine address-collision editorial defect, the fifth found this audit (after ep_pwm.h's/ep_gpio.h's/ep_i2c.h's/ep_iseled.h's own): Table 56 printed mdio_ep_status at the same address (0x0002) as mdio_ep_enable&clr; corrected to 0x0004, the next unclaimed offset after the common options octet, since Table 56 defines no base_clk row the way every other endpoint type's own table does (RCP_EP_MDIO_EP_FUNC_LEN = 0x0006, one register width narrower than the common case). New rcp_ep_mdio_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror()/_encode_reconfig_request() implement the same generic addressed-write mechanism PWM_OUT/GPIO/SPI/I2C/UART/LIN/ADC/PWM_IN/ISELED already had — MDIO is now 9 of 11 endpoint types with it. rcp_ep_mdio_functional_cfg_t gains ep_status (the only field this module adds; still no set_ep_status() mutator, matching every register-block field in every other endpoint type -- reachable only via rcp_ep_mdio_apply_reconfig()).

requirements.title: MDIO EP_func register block reachable via evt[2:0]=111b (Table 56, address-collision defect corrected)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (FIXED 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_mdio_decode_read_request()/_decode_write_request() already correctly rejected evt[2:0]=111b (RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_EVT, via acf.h's rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain()), but no counterpart implemented that §12.7.1 configuration-write path at all — no rcp_ep_mdio_apply_reconfig() existed. See REQ-MDIO-020 for the register block's own content and the address-collision defect this entry's fix shares credit for; this entry tracks the mechanism itself (rcp_ep_mdio_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror()/_encode_reconfig_request()), mirroring every other Group I register-block fix's own "mechanism gets its own id, content gets the pre-existing one" convention (REQ-PWM-058/059, REQ-ISELED-026/027/029).

requirements.title: the 2-bit mdio_mode selector and the Figure 42 request payload layout
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's MDIO request payload layout does not match TC18 §13.7.13.3. Figure 42 lays the payload out as reserved bits, a 2-bit mdio_mode field, mdio_address, then mdio_payload, where Table 57 gives mdio_mode four meanings — MMD single-word access, MMD multiple-byte access, MMS single-word access (10b) and MMS multiple (double) word access (11b) — and mdio_address follows the IEEE and OA SPI specifications. c-RCP instead uses its own 5-byte prefix of a 1-octet clause selector (RCP_EP_MDIO_CLAUSE_22 / _45), a 1-octet prtad, a 1-octet devad and a big-endian 2-octet regad (ep_mdio.h:145-163, the header's own "Wire layout" section -- corrected 2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256: this citation previously pointed to ep_mdio.h:137-141, the unrelated RCP_EP_MDIO_MAX_BURST_WORDS/AVTPDU-sizing discussion, drifted after a header edit/reflow), with no mdio_mode field at all and no distinction between single-access and multiple-access modes — its burst behavior is instead carried by a separate 2-octet word_count. Consequence: c-RCP's MDIO requests are not wire-compatible with a conforming peer, and the single-word vs multiple-access selection is inexpressible. See REQ-MDIO-012 through REQ-MDIO-019, whose own entries now cross-reference this gap directly rather than silently claiming full TC18 wire conformance.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Figure 42 and Table 57, TC18.txt L5664-5684 (corrected 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group J: the prior range's own end, L5681, truncated Table 57's own mdio_payload row and its caption, both of which run through L5684)

requirements.title: MMS0 and MMS1 carry 32-bit data fields, not 16-bit
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP's MDIO data fields are unconditionally 16 bits wide, contrary to TC18 §13.7.13.3 Table 57, which requires 16-bit data fields for MMD accesses and for MMS other than 0 and 1, but 32-bit data fields for MMS0 and MMS1. rcp_ep_mdio_word_encode()/rcp_ep_mdio_word_decode() serialize exactly two octets each, rcp_ep_mdio_pack_len() returns word_count * 2, and rcp_ep_mdio_word_count_of() rejects any odd byte length — none of them consults an access mode. Consequence: MMS0/MMS1 register accesses (the OPEN Alliance SPI/MMS register spaces where 32-bit words are the norm) cannot be encoded or decoded, and a peer's 32-bit MMS payload will be misparsed as two unrelated 16-bit words.

requirements.title: UART RX FIFO overflow is not flagged in a UART EP status register
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the UART endpoint's fifo-rx-buffer nor its uart_ep_status register, and therefore never flags an RX FIFO overflow (TC18 §13.7.8.1). rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_t carries ep_rx_buffer_size (the FIFO's configured length) but no status field, and no c-RCP function sets or reports an overflow condition. Consequence: an RC Client cannot distinguish a short read caused by uart_timeout from one caused by silently discarded, overflowed RX data.

requirements.title: UART read-response completion is triggered by read_size satisfied, uart_timeout expiry, or a full RX FIFO
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not implement the UART read-request completion rule (TC18 §13.7.8.1) — a read response shall be emitted as soon as (a) the fifo-rx-buffer holds as many octets as the request's read_size, or (b) uart_timeout has expired, or (c) read_size exceeds uart_rx_fifo_size and the FIFO is full, in which case the response shall be fragmented via rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_response_fragmented(). c-RCP supplies the three ingredients (read_size in the ACF header, cfg->uart_timeout_ms, and the fragmenting encoder) but never arbitrates between them; the choice is left entirely to an unspecified caller. Consequence: two conforming c-RCP-based servers can answer identical read requests with materially different response cadence and fragmentation.

requirements.title: UART read_size is narrowed to 8 bits, below the ACF header's 12-bit read_size field
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP narrows the UART read request's read_size to one octet (rcp_ep_uart_encode_read_request()'s uint8_t read_size parameter, ep_uart.h:357), so it cannot express a read_size above 255, whereas the ACF byte_message_info read_size_or_segment_num field is 12 bits wide (0-4095, acf.h:257) and TC18 §13.7.8.1 explicitly contemplates a read_size larger than uart_rx_fifo_size driving a fragmented response. Consequence: c-RCP cannot originate — and rcp_ep_uart_decode_read_request()'s uint8_t *out_read_size cannot faithfully surface — a conforming peer's UART read request in the 256..4095 range.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1, TC18.txt L4884-4886 (read_size field width)

requirements.title: UART compound wait request comparison against the RX FIFO, bounded by uart_rx_fifo_size
requirements.text: FIXED (v0.110.0/v0.111.0): acf.h's rcp_acf_compound_wait_match() now provides a universal TC18 §13.5.1 comparison surface for every endpoint type, UART included, wired into real dispatch via server.c's rcp_server_tick_ctx_t.current_status. §13.7.8.1's own "compared length bounded above by uart_rx_fifo_size" follows directly from §13.5.1's shared length rule once the fifo's real contents (which can never exceed uart_rx_fifo_size) are supplied as current_status: an expected byte_msg_payload longer than the fifo could ever hold never matches (status shorter than payload never matches). No UART-specific comparison logic is needed; this is no longer a gap.

requirements.title: uart_ep_len, the reserved octet, and uart_ep_status register rows of Table 48
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP does not model the UART functional-configuration block's own descriptor and status registers (TC18 §13.7.8.2 Table 48): uart_ep_len (relative address 0x0000, 8 bit, R — the length of this description in octets), the reserved octet at 0x0001 (8 bit, R, reads 0x00), and uart_ep_status (0x0004, 16 bit, R/W). rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_t is a plain C struct with no register-map serialization, so a client walking the EP functional-config table cannot discover this block's length or read its status. Consequence: the UART block is not enumerable or serializable over the wire at the addresses Table 48 fixes.

requirements.title: uart_baud_rate is in kbit/s, uart_stop_bits counts HALF stop bits, and uart_timeout is in bit times measured from the last received stop bit
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I, REQ-UART-038): the register block (rcp_ep_uart_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig()) now carries these three registers at TC18's own units, as new, distinct struct fields kept separate from this module's pre-existing, differently-unitted fields of a similar name (the same "don't silently redefine an existing public field" caution SPI's own baud_rate_kbps-vs-clock_divider split already established): baud_rate_kbps (uint16_t, kbit/s, the wire's uart_baud_rate) is distinct from the pre-existing baud_rate (uint32_t, unit unspecified, untouched); wire_timeout_bit_times (uint8_t, bit times, the wire's uart_timeout) is distinct from the pre-existing uart_timeout_ms (milliseconds, a different layer entirely -- see ep_uart.h's own file header). uart_stop_bits' half-stop-bit units round-trip through the pre-existing two-valued rcp_ep_uart_stop_bits_t enum via a documented, deliberately lossy mapping (render: ONE->2, TWO->4; parse: >=3 -> TWO, else ONE) -- 1.5 stop bits (wire value 3) is NOT separately representable by this enum and rounds up to TWO on parse (the more conservative of the two representable values), a genuine, honestly-documented residual limitation rather than a full fix.

requirements.title: uart_rts_enable, uart_cts_enable, uart_half_duplex, and uart_trail (Table 48) are now modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §13.7.8.2 Table 48's four R/W fields rcp_ep_uart_functional_cfg_t previously carried no counterpart for at all -- uart_rts_enable (relative address 0x0009.2, 1 bit), uart_cts_enable (0x0009.3, 1 bit), uart_half_duplex (0x0009.4, 1 bit), and uart_trail (0x000C, 8 bit) -- are now modeled as rts_enable/cts_enable/half_duplex/trail, alongside the whole Table 48 register block (rcp_ep_uart_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror()/_encode_reconfig_request(), REQ-UART-039/040) implementing TC18 §12.7.1's generic evt[2:0]=111b configuration-write mechanism for this endpoint type for the first time (the same class of fix SPI's/I2C's own earlier fixes in this issue delivered). Unlike GPIO's/I2C's own source tables, Table 48 has no address-collision editorial defect -- its printed addresses are internally consistent.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.2 Table 48, TC18.txt L4937-4949 (uart_rts_enable/uart_cts_enable/uart_half_duplex), L4954-4955 (uart_trail)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_render_registers()/_encode_reconfig_request() implement the generic §12.7.1 configuration request for UART
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request -- evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data -- usable against every endpoint type. rcp_ep_uart_decode_write_request()/_decode_read_request() already correctly rejected evt[2:0] = 111b as RCP_EP_UART_ERR_BAD_EVT (via acf.h's rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain()), but no counterpart function implemented that path at all. rcp_ep_uart_render_registers() serializes cfg's whole Table 48 block; rcp_ep_uart_encode_reconfig_request() encodes an ACF_ABB write request (op=WRITE, evt=111b) carrying a 16-bit big-endian start address followed by data, matching PWM_OUT's/GPIO's/SPI's/I2C's own encode_reconfig_request() shape.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 18, TC18.txt L2463-2484

requirements.title: rcp_ep_uart_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror() apply the addressed configuration write and never return NULL for a status message
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_uart_apply_reconfig() decodes the address+data payload TC18 §12.7.1 defines and patches cfg's Table 48 register block at octet granularity, then adopts the whole block atomically -- a write whose start_address+length exceeds RCP_EP_UART_EP_FUNC_LEN is rejected and cfg left entirely unchanged (RCP_EP_UART_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE), matching §12.7.1's own 'such a payload is to be ignored' rule; octets landing on a read-only register (EP_LEN or the reserved octet) are silently skipped while the rest of the span is still applied. rcp_ep_uart_reconfig_strerror() never returns NULL, including for an unrecognized error code.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints, TC18.txt L2463-2484

catalogNote: Phase 22 re-certification pass (ROADMAP.md milestone 85, v0.85.0): every requirement below was individually reviewed against the source file its //cfusa:req tag actually appears in (a per-prefix audit, not a blind carry-over) and classified via the "scope" field. scope="tc18" entries (779 of 854) describe the actual implemented TC18 behavior -- register-map access control, lifecycle transitions, E2E CRC32 safe points, per-endpoint-type request/response shapes, discovery, power-mode transitions, and every ADAPT-class satellite -- and are this project's own ISO 26262 ASIL-B safety-case basis going forward. scope="legacy-compat" entries (75 of 854) describe the retired pre-TC18 Zone/Command surface (rcp.h/rcp.c and tests/legacy_mock.* only); they are demoted to level/asil "QM" and their text is prefixed accordingly, but kept -- not deleted or renumbered -- because that legacy surface is out of scope for this milestone to touch (ROADMAP.md's v0.84.0 milestone already confirmed it is the last consumer of those retired types anywhere in src/) and still carries //cfusa:req tags naming these ids; deleting the catalog entries out from under a surviving tag would only trade one inaccuracy (an unqualified legacy requirement) for another (a dangling reference cfusa trace would then report). Only the tc18 subset is this project's claimed certification basis, and it is complete against Phases 13-21 as actually shipped -- not a forward-declared placeholder the way the legacy program's own catalog was at its v0.2.0, since unlike v0.2.0 this catalog was not written before the code it describes. TC18 requirements-corpus completeness pass (v0.105.0): 158 entries were added by a clause-by-clause sweep of TC18 sections 10 through 13.7.13 for normative clauses, tables and figures that no existing entry covered. Every added entry carries a "tc18" field citing the exact section (and the line of the specification text it was read from) and a "status" field: "implemented" (behaviour c-RCP provides, scope "tc18", ASIL-B), or "partial"/"not-implemented" (a normative obligation c-RCP does NOT meet -- scope "tc18-gap", level/asil "QM", text opening with "NOT IMPLEMENTED", and a test that pins the deviation rather than pretending it is absent). A tc18-gap entry is deliberately NOT part of the ASIL-B safety-case basis; it exists so the catalog is an honest map of the specification's normative surface instead of a map of this implementation only.
